News.title: Third of home workers admit they’ve turned off their camera to eat snack, research finds
News.content:
MUTE MUNCHERS Third of home workers admit they’ve turned off their camera to eat snack, research finds







Next

A THIRD of adults who work from home admit they’ve turned off their camera to eat a snack, research has revealed.

Half admit to snacking more when working from their dwellings compared to the traditional workplace – mainly thanks to the kitchen being nearby (43 per cent), boredom (38 per cent), and feeling like they’ve earned a reward (29 per cent).



It comes as a poll of 2,000 Brits found 49 per cent agree there are very few locations they would consider it unacceptable to scoff a snack.

With those polled owning up to eating treats in a host of unusual locations, including while waiting to be seen for a job interview, on a rollercoaster or even at the top of a volcano.



The research was commissioned by Little Moons which has also produced a quiz to uncover your snacking personality and your perfect snack match based on your tastes.

In addition to this, the brand has teamed up with Amber Rose Gill for its First in My Bloodline campaign, exploring the unexpected places Gen Z now snack where parents or grandparents wouldn’t.



As part of the campaign the Love Island winner was challenged to eat miniature mochi bites, Mini Moons, while wing walking.

Milly Tuck, spokesperson for brand, said: “It looks like we’re entering a new era of snacking, with people embracing snacks wherever life takes them.

“Busy lifestyles coupled with our appetite for interesting and viral snacks means that snacking has become far more embedded into people’s daily routines, with many happy to enjoy a quick bite wherever they happen to be.”

The research also found 19 per cent of people have secretly brought snacks to a friend‘s house, while a further 14 per cent have considered it.



Reasons for this include trying to avoid going hungry (53 per cent), not wanting to ask for food (34 per cent) and because their friend always has boring snacks (18 per cent).

There were also noticeable generational differences, with 50 per cent of Gen Zs claiming they have eaten a snack somewhere they believe their parents or grandparents would never.

Conversely, just 19 per cent of Boomers thought the same, according to data from OnePoll.com.

Gen Z emerged as the most daring snackers too, with 63 per cent describing themselves as adventurous, while only 10 per cent of Boomers felt similarly.

The younger generation were also more likely to eat snacks in unconventional settings, with 47 per cent snacking while walking, 25 per cent while waiting for appointments, and 16 per cent during calls or meetings.

By comparison, only 27 per cent of Boomers eat while walking, five per cent while waiting for an appointment and just two per cent during a call or meeting.



Little Moon’s Milly Tuck added: “One of the most interesting findings was the clear generational divide in snacking habits.

“Younger adults were far more likely to describe themselves as adventurous and were more open to trying newer foods and flavours.

“Our campaign celebrates just this – the new and sometimes bizarre places that Gen Z will snack versus their parents or grandparents.”

News.title: Hate preachers and mosque bosses who allow vile sermons face bans from running charities under tough new rules
News.content:
'NO PLACE OF SAFETY' Hate preachers and mosque bosses who allow vile sermons face bans from running charities under tough new rules







Next

MOSQUE bosses who allow hate preachers to deliver vile sermons could be banned from running charities under sweeping new Government proposals.

Ministers want to give the Charity Commission more powers to ban trustees or managers who preach hate or incite violence, even if they have not been convicted of a crime.



It comes after the Metropolitan Police came under fire last year after dropping an investigation into an imam at Redbridge Islamic Centre who called for Allah to “curse the Jews and the children of Israel” just days after the 7 October terror attacks.

Officers said there was insufficient evidence to secure a conviction, while the Charity Commission has still not made a public decision on the case, nearly three years after the sermon was first reported.



The new crackdown could also target charity bosses who allow inflammatory and extremist sermons on their premises, even if they do not personally make the remarks.

The move comes after a string of mosques with charitable status faced complaints over alleged anti-Semitism, homophobia and sermons appearing to condone domestic abuse, some of which were livestreamed on social media.

Speaking at the Charity Commission’s Annual Public Meeting on Thursday, Dame Julia Unwin said: “We never want charities to be a place of safety for people who are committing those crimes.”

The Government’s fresh consultation proposes disqualifying trustees who “use charity funds, property or premises to host speakers or hold an event where views are promoted that are violent, or hateful towards a person or persons, groups or communities of a particular race, religion, or belief”.

It also highlights cases where a trustee calls for “violence or the eradication of a national, ethnic, racial or religious group”.

Since the October 7 terror attacks, the Charity Commission said it has opened more than 400 cases involving charities linked to the Israel-Gaza conflict, and has made over 80 referrals to police over suspected criminal offences.



But the Government’s former extremism tsar claimed in March that a “climate of fear” within the Charity Commission was preventing it from tackling organisations accused of undermining British values.

Writing in The Times, Lord Walney described the regulator as “currently toothless” and urged it to tackle its “enormous backlog of investigations”.

At the time, the Commission said its investigations were “rigorous and follow the evidence” and that it often ordered charities to “take immediate steps” while its cases were ongoing.



The Charity Commission said on Thursday it had seen a rapid increase in regulatory matters, up 23% year-on-year, but did not provide a total number of cases.

The watchdog has not publicly revealed how many of those cases involved allegations of anti-Semitism at British mosques and it is unclear how many investigations are still ongoing.

In July, the charity regulator confirmed it was carrying out an initial assessment of sermons at Al-Sunnah Mosque in Manchester after an imam was recorded praying for God to “deal with the Jews” and “seize them” in 2024.

The mosque was attended by Manchester synagogue terrorist Jihad al-Shamie and his accomplice Mohammad Bashir.

Meanwhile, the Mosque and Islamic Centre of Brent in London received just an ‘official warning’ after speeches delivered by Sheikh Babikir Ahmed Babikir in late 2023 included “inflammatory and divisive” remarks about Israel and Zionism, including reported claims that Zionists were plotting to “control the world”.



The Charity Commission found four of five speeches reviewed contained inflammatory or divisive material, with two potentially encouraging support for Hamas.

It ruled that trustees had failed to put adequate safeguards in place to manage the risks posed by speakers.

Babikir told the Telegraph in January 2024, he “vehemently” denied his comments were anti-Semitic, and insisted he had promoted religious brotherhood for “decades” and that his remarks referred to “Zionists, not Jews”.

In the East Midlands, the Charity Commission went further and banned a trustee at the Nottingham Islam Information Point for three years in July 2024 after an “inflammatory” sermon just days after the Oct 7 terror attack.



According to the Commission, the preacher said: “the hour will not begin until the Muslims fight the Jews and the Muslims will kill them until a Jew hides behind a rock or a tree.”

In another case, the watchdog opened a regulatory compliance case into Hounslow Jamia Masjid in West London after video footage appeared to show Imam Shaykh Ammar Siddiqui claiming gay people would “destroy the human race” during a 2023 seminar.

He also appeared to defend the use of the death penalty for homosexuality in Islamic states.

And in Birmingham, the Charity Commission issued “advice and guidance” to An-Noor Masjid after a video uploaded in September 2024 appeared to show preacher Mahamed AbdurRazaq saying a husband could hit his wife if she refused sex.



But the new proposals have already drawn criticism for failing to explicitly extend the new disqualification grounds to misogyny and homophobia.

The National Secular Society’s Megan Manson said: “These proposals fall far short of tackling some of the most egregious problems in the charity sector.

“Greater powers to tackle charities which promote violence, or hatred based on race or religion or belief, are of course welcome and long overdue. But the failure to protect women and LGBT people, who are too often the subject of stigmatising sermons hosted by religious charities, is unacceptable.”

While a spokesperson for Campaign Against Antisemitism told The Sun: “After three years of rampant political and religious extremism in the charity sector, this initiative is well overdue, but better late than never.



“So we welcome these tentative plans to clamp down on this radicalism among charities – which too often takes the form of racism toward Jews and hostility to British values.

“This consultation is an admission of what everybody already knows: the Charity Commission has been far too weak in regulating extremist charities, and has spent disproportionate energy over-regulating others to try to look ‘even-handed’.

“We will be making a submission to the consultation, and we will push the Government to follow through on its plans to root out extremism and put an end to charities being used as tax-free breeding grounds for hate.”

Fiyaz Mughal, founder of Faith Matters and Muslims Against Antisemitism, welcomed the consultation but warned that it did not go far enough.



He told The Sun: “The consultation is a positive step forward but misses out a key element, which is if a charitable organisation hosts a speaker or preacher who promotes wholesale stereotypes of communities or groups and not just ‘hateful’ comments.

“For example, as a Muslim, I have been sickened by the tens of mosques who hosted Imams or preachers who promoted antisemitism post-October 7th 2023.

“This is not what a mosque is for and there is a duty on the mosque to promote positive values, otherwise the Charity Commission should step in, remove their registration and hold them to account.”

On Thursday, Dame Julia Unwin said the Charity Commission welcomed the Government’s proposals but stressed the importance of getting the new powers right.

She said: “We are keen for our powers to be strengthened, not because we want more power, but so that we might better protect the sector against racial and religious hatred and violence crimes under the National Security Act.



“But it is important that the measures are drafted precisely and the appropriate safeguards are built in.”

The Al-Sunnah Mosque and Redbridge Islamic Centre were contacted for comment.

A previous statement from 2023 on Redbridge Islamic Centre’s website said: “It has been brought to the attention of the RIC that the video of a talk at the RIC on the Oct 20 may have caused offence to some members of the public.

“We have taken swift action to investigate this matter. Whilst the matter is investigated, we have decided that the member of staff in question cease his public speaking engagements, pending the outcome.”

A spokesman for Hounslow Jamia Masjid said its trustees had “engaged fully and transparently” with the Charity Commission over concerns about sermons delivered at the mosque.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

The mosque said its head imam, Shaykh Ammar Siddiqui, had explained that his remarks referred to “scholarly commentary from historical Muslim jurists” which had been taken out of their theological and academic context.

The spokesman added: “The Masjid has no tolerance for hatred, extremism, or any conduct that is contrary to its charitable purposes or to the values it seeks to promote.”

News.title: Man arrested after ‘raping tourist in toilets of Majorca nightclub before posting footage of sick attack online’
News.content:
‘RAPE’ HORROR Man arrested after ‘raping tourist in toilets of Majorca nightclub before posting footage of sick attack online’







Next

A TOURIST was allegedly raped in the toilets of Majorcan nightclub by a man who filmed the attack and posted the footage online.

The woman was left bleeding from her knees as she desperately tried to escape her attacker at the nightspot in Playa de Palma, near the capital.



A German man, whose age has not been revealed, has been arrested on suspicion of rape following the horrifying ordeal.

Police said the victim had previously met the suspect, who repeatedly flirted with her despite being told she did not want to have sex with him.



When she went to the toilets, the man attempted to follow her but was stopped by security staff.

He allegedly slipped past them when they were distracted and the woman was inside.



The suspect then grabbed her and forced her onto her knees as she desperately struggled to break free.

Police said her knees began bleeding as she tried to stand up and crawl away before the man allegedly raped her without a condom.

During the attack, the woman reportedly spotted him filming the assault and sending the footage to others through a messaging app.

She eventually managed to open the bathroom door, where security staff rushed to help her and alerted police.



Officers arrived to find the distressed tourist crying as a friend helped translate her account of the ordeal.

The suspect was arrested on suspicion of rape, while the woman was taken to hospital for treatment before making a formal police complaint.

Her nationality has not been disclosed.



A National Police spokesman confirmed: “Officers in Palma have arrested a man of German origin for sexually assaulting a tourist by raping her.”

Police said the woman had made it clear to the suspect that she did not want to have sex with him.

They added: “When she tried to resist, she injured her knees and they began to bleed as she tried to get up and crawl away to escape him.”

The arrest follows a string of disturbing sexual assault cases involving tourists on the Spanish holiday island.

In July, a 50-year-old masseur was arrested after allegedly sexually assaulting a pregnant British holidaymaker at her hotel in Calas de Mallorca.



The 30-year-old woman had booked a massage at the resort on the island’s eastern coast when the worker allegedly began touching her inappropriately.

She told police the session had initially been normal before he moved his hands up her inner thigh towards her groin.

Despite her demands to stop, he allegedly inserted two fingers inside her.

The terrified woman fled the treatment room screaming for help, prompting hotel staff to rush to her aid.

She then returned to her room to tell her husband what had happened and showered before police were called.



Officers found her “highly distressed and crying” and had to calm her down.

In another case in May, a van driver was arrested on suspicion of abducting and sexually assaulting a young British tourist in Palma.

The woman had been walking back to her hotel from a nightspot when the suspect allegedly grabbed her on the street and forced her into his vehicle.

Detectives said he seized her by the arm, pushed her into the passenger seat and drove off before sexually assaulting her.

She managed to escape when the van stopped at a red light and two witnesses travelling in a car behind intervened.



The pair had seen the abduction and photographed the van’s number plate, helping police track down and arrest the suspect.

The attack happened in the early hours of May 11 on Palma’s seafront promenade, Paseo Maritimo.

Just days earlier, on May 1, another tourist was allegedly sexually assaulted by two men after having her drink spiked in a bar in Manacor.

The woman, whose nationality has not been revealed, said she began feeling unwell after leaving her drink unattended while visiting the toilet.

Two men she had met that evening offered to drive her back to her hotel but allegedly took her to a patch of waste ground instead.



She was then sexually assaulted in the back seat of their car, police said.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The woman eventually escaped and begged nearby residents for help, prompting them to contact police.

Two men were arrested over the attack.

News.title: Apprentice engineer, 20, died from ‘toxic gases’ in engine room on fishing trawler as mum shares heartbreaking tribute
News.content:
TRAWLER TRAGEDY Apprentice engineer, 20, died from ‘toxic gases’ in engine room on fishing trawler as mum shares heartbreaking tribute







Next

AN apprentice engineer died from “toxic gases” in the engine room of a fishing trawler – as his mum shares a heartbreaking tribute.

Conor Moseley, 20, died on board the Resurgam in November 2019 while it was moored in Newlyn Harbour in Cornwall.



Conor and three other workers were carrying out work on the vessel – a fishing boat owned and operated by W. Stevenson & Sons Limited – on 15 November when the tragedy unfolded.

He had inhaled aerosol from the fire suppression system that unexpectedly activated after being installed in the crowded engine room.



The Health and Safety Executive said the fire suppression systemm installed by Ocean Engineering (Fire) Ltd, activated without warning and filled the engine room with hot, toxic gases, creating dangerous conditions and making it difficult to see.

On Thursday, Stevenson and Sons was fined a total of £100,000 with a further £27,906 in costs after a hearing.

The small, enclosed engine room had only one way in and out.

Workers had to climb a ladder and pass through a hatch one at a time, passing through a gas jet in excess of 75°C.

The other workers managed to climb out, but Conor was overcome by carbon monoxide and other substances, leaving him unable to escape.

Conor’s colleagues tried to rescue him but they were unable to reach him.



Cornwall Fire and Rescue Service later rescued Conor from the engine room, but he could not be revived.

Truro Crown Court heard that health and safety failings included no evacuation plan or sufficient leadership.

Conor’s mother Tracy Moseley said she was not allowed to hold her son as he lay dying on the ship and his death has left a hole in their lives which will never be filled.

Speaking after the case, she also reflected on her son’s life and the impact his death has had on them.

She said: “Growing up Conor loved nothing better than helping out on his dad’s boat.



“Conor always made himself available to help his father when he came in from sea and would be ready to help him land his catch even after a full day’s work.

“Now for Steve, my husband, there is just an empty place that cannot be filled.

“All we have now are his ashes which are kept in his bedroom. Every morning I go in and say, ‘morning little man I love you’ and blow him a kiss. I never say ‘good morning’ as it can never be a good morning without him.

“At night I blow him a kiss and say ‘night night little man, I love you’.”

An investigation by the HSE found that the risks created by several contractors working in the cramped engine room had not been properly considered.



One contractor described the room as a mess, with poor lighting and trip hazards, and said that at one point six or seven people were working in the space. One witness described it as chaos.

There was no safe system of work for installing the fire suppression system and no effective emergency plan.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The HSE said a permit-to-work system could have been used to coordinate the different activities and ensure they were carried out safely.

It said its code of practice also highlights the need for parties to work together and have an overall written plan covering responsibilities, shared risks and emergency arrangements.

News.title: BBC Bitesize used by millions of schoolchildren ‘encourages pupils to back contentious open borders & Net Zero policies’
News.content:
BEEB 'BIAS' BBC Bitesize used by millions of schoolchildren ‘encourages pupils to back contentious open borders & Net Zero policies’







Next

THE BBC has been accused of pushing woke Left-wing political views on migration, Net Zero and inequality to millions of schoolchildren.

The Beeb’s education site Bitesize – used by almost half of all children aged four to 16 – allegedly promotes “extreme” views on immigration, climate change and social justice.



It features an online game called “Increasing Immigration”, which rewards pupils for backing open borders and granting amnesties to illegal migrants, a Mail on Sunday investigation revealed.

The game tells children aged 11 to 14: “We don’t have enough people of working age to keep our society running smoothly.



“We should try to attract migrant workers and incorporate them into our economy.”

In one scenario, pupils lose points for choosing to deport migrants living in the country without the correct visas, while granting an amnesty earns rewards.

Another offers the choice of open borders, which boosts the economy score by three points and public health by two.

Those rejecting the policy as “too radical” receive nothing.



Shadow Education Secretary Laura Trott demanded the BBC remove the game.

She said: “The BBC has crossed a line. They have a duty to remain impartial, and yet they are using learning tools as a vehicle to push a Left-wing political agenda onto young children.

“Advocating open borders encourages illegal small boat crossings. These are the type of toxic resources dressed up as education which should be nowhere near the classroom.”

The BBC insists players are not rewarded for political positions, pointing out that points are also awarded for training local people and closing borders.

But other Bitesize material claims migrants contribute more in tax than they use in public services and pump a “staggering amount of money” into the economy.



The website also suggests concerns that migrants take jobs from locals are likely to stem from “prejudice”.

Former BBC television controller Danny Cohen called for an urgent investigation.

He said: “The BBC needs to explain why its educational website is pushing extreme Left-wing ideologies to schoolchildren.



“There is such a lack of balance in so many areas of the BBC’s output that it cannot be seriously defended as coincidental.”

Bitesize has also been accused of promoting contentious Net Zero policies, describing the target as an “important goal” and urging pupils to petition local government.

One video tells Welsh students reaching Net Zero could mean having to “fly less, eat less meat or stick to sustainably farmed meat”.

The material comes despite Sir Keir Starmer previously saying tackling climate change “does not mean telling people how to run their lives”.

Elsewhere, the website praises climate activist Greta Thunberg and the Black Lives Matter movement, while encouraging pupils to campaign with groups such as Amnesty International.



Alex Burghart, Shadow Cabinet Office Secretary, said: “The BBC was set up to inform, educate and entertain – not misinform, re-educate and brainwash.”

Former Tory Education Secretary Gavin Williamson added: “The mask has slipped and the BBC has yet again betrayed its rampant Left-wing political agenda.

“The state broadcaster brainwashing children using a homework game is like something from a North Korean re-education camp.”

Launched in 1998, Bitesize is one of Britain’s biggest education websites, with almost 1.7 million pupils accessing it every week.

The row comes as the BBC faces a crucial period ahead of its charter renewal, with Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy expected to publish a White Paper before Christmas.



Director-general Matt Brittin has pledged to tackle bias by introducing technology to monitor how often certain words and phrases are used.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

A BBC spokesman said: “BBC Bitesize works with educational consultants to develop resources that help young people explore and understand a wide range of topics, aligned to the respective curriculums across the UK.

“While we don’t accept the characterisation of Bitesize in this story, we regularly review content to ensure it remains relevant and to ensure it meets the BBC’s editorial standards and will review these examples in that context.”

News.title: IS terrorist who came to UK on small boat & can’t be deported is seen shopping near Windsor Castle ahead of state visit
News.content:
FREE TO ROAM IS terrorist who came to UK on small boat & can’t be deported is seen shopping near Windsor Castle ahead of state visit







Next

AN ISIS terrorist who committed public executions was left free to wander the streets of Windsor after being allowed to stay in Britain.

Mohammed Yaseen was seen in the King’s local Co-op after being allowed to stay in the UK on Human Rights grounds.



The Iraqi terrorist was allegedly a member of the Al Qaeda group that beheaded Brit Ken Bigley.

A terrorist from 16 years old, he later joined an Isis group that carried out stonings, beheadings and mass executions, The Mail on Sunday reports.



A court was told that Yaseen “posed a danger to the whole of the UK.”

He was released from prison last week after serving two years for illegally entering the UK on a small boat.

Yaseen has been put up in a hostel in Windsor where he was last week seen shopping in a Co-op close to Windsor Castle.

He came to the UK after serving a five-year sentence in Germany for being a member of Isis.

Now, Yaseen has reapplied to stay in the UK – stopping the Home Office‘s attempts to deport him.

And the Foreign Office has reportedly raised concerns that if he were returned to Iraq, he could face mistreatment.



King Charles is set to host a state banquet for the Sultan of Oman at Windsor Castle on Thursday.

And, the Prince and Princess of Wales live nearby with their three young children.

Experts say Yaseen will receive legal aid for his application to stay in the country, and that if he were to take the case all the way to the European Court of Human Rights the taxpayer could have to pay up to £500,000.

Chris Philp MP, Shadow Home Secretary, told the Mail on Sunday: “We are paying through the nose to feed, clothe and house individuals who pose a clear threat.

“If Andy Burnham took this seriously, he would deport this man at once.”



A court in Germany heard that the terrorist had been involved in bombings that killed US soldiers.

It was also heard that he had operated as a security guard during stonings, beheadings and executions where victims included children.

He was among 80 people intercepted by Border Force as they crossed the channel last December.

Yaseen gave officials a fake name and was housed in a taxpayer-funded migrant hotel before his true identity was uncovered.

His trial at Winchester Crown Court for illegally entering Britain heard that he had a “deeper and lengthy involvement in terrorism.”



He now has an ankle tag leaving him free to roam the streets between 6am and 6pm.

Yaseen arrived in Germany in 2015 and claimed asylum with authorities unaware of his past.

He worked as a hairdresser before being arrested in 2018 alongside three others after a tip-off.

He became a member of the Islamic State aged 16, planting several bombs despite his age, a court heard.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

When he was released from prison a German court attempted to deport him but a judge ruled there was a risk he could be mistreated or executed.



A source told the Mail on Sunday that he had been recalled to prison and was no longer in Windsor.

News.title: Police officer injured in UK city centre shooting as suspects on the loose
News.content:
GUN HORROR Police officer injured in UK city centre shooting as suspects on the loose







Next

A COP is in hospital after being shot in the foot in a terrifying early-morning incident – as officers hunt suspects on the run.

The officer was approaching two people in Nottingham‘s city centre when the shooting happened at around 4.50am today.

A man and a woman fled the scene and remain on the run.

Cops say a firearm has since been recovered and a large police cordon is in place in Angel Row.





The injured officer has been taken to hospital for treatment.

Assistant Chief Constable Claire Rukas, of Nottinghamshire Police, said the incident is a “sobering reminder” of the danger of the job.

She said: “This is a shocking incident and a sobering reminder of the potential dangers faced by officers as they work to protect and serve the public.

“As we investigate what happened and work to apprehend the individuals involved, my thoughts today are with the injured officer, his family and colleagues.



“I also ask that anyone with additional information shares this with us without delay.

“Even the smallest bit of information could make all the difference to this investigation.”

In a post on social media East Midlands Ambulance Service said sent its best wishes to the injured officer.

“Sending our heartfelt thoughts and support to the injured officer, his family, and all our colleagues at Nottinghamshire Police today,” the post said.



“We’re wishing him a full and speedy recovery.”

News.title: Protester dies during ‘apocalyptic’ French riots as shops looted & city hall reduced to ashes in night of violence
News.content:
Next

A PROTESTER has died as the “apocalyptic” French riots continue to grip France, with shops looted and the city hall reduced to ashes.

More than half a million people took to the streets across the country on Saturday as furious demonstrations over the cost of living descended into more chaos overnight.



The protester reportedly collapsed on Boulevard Magenta in the French capital as a march passed through the area.

He was carried by fellow demonstrators to the Château d’Eau emergency centre but could not be saved.



Paris police confirmed that one person had died following a cardiac arrest, with the exact circumstances still under investigation.

The death comes amid widespread unrest that has seen more than 1,800 people arrested across France, according to the Minister of the Interior.

Yesterday’s day of action against the high cost of living saw 800,000 people march across France.

In Paris alone, more than 110,000 protesters flooded the streets, with scenes of destruction leaving parts of the capital resembling a warzone.

Police confirmed a record 855 arrests in the city, while 13 officers were injured.

French President Emmanuel Macron has vowed to “punish” vandals responsible for the destruction.



Demonstrators continued to clash with cops overnight as new footage shows Paris’ skyline engulfed in flames.

Officers struggled to contain the violent unrest as a senior commander admits they “lost control” of the city.

Masked protesters chased police vehicles and hurled petrol bombs at officers in the streets of the capital.



Officers were forced to use water cannon, tear gas and batons to control the violence.

Rioters also smashed and spray painted luxury stores including Christian Dior, Louis Vuitton and Kenzo across several famous streets and districts.

Other videos show crowds gathered around burning cars as flames engulfed the vehicles.

Brazen looters could be seen exiting storefronts clutching onto their stolen goods with some yobs even showing off their hauls to social media.

Dramatic footage showed violent clashes erupting between police and protesters on Rue du Faubourg-Saint-Denis in Paris.



Officers wearing helmets and protective vests were seen swinging batons as crowds of demonstrators surged towards them.

Thick smoke filled the street as flares and tear gas were set off during the chaos.

The violence broke out just a short distance from Gare du Nord, where Eurostar trains arrive from London.



A police source described the scenes as “apocalyptic,” as groups of agitators engaged in violent clashes with law enforcement.

“There weren’t enough personnel or ammunition,” the source added.

The Interior Minister, Laurent Nuñez said: “At this stage, more than 500 police officers, gendarmes, and firefighters have been injured, caught up in these scenes of violence.”

Prosecutors have launched an investigation into organised property destruction.

They warned that civilians had also been targeted, sometimes violently, during the unrest.



The violence has also seen a historic 143-year-old spire collapse in flames as rioters wreaked havoc in central France.

Shocking footage showed the iconic town hall in Limoges engulfed in fire as thick smoke billowed into the sky.

Its historic spire crumbled under the intense heat before crashing down in front of crowds gathered below.



Local prefect Maurice Barate said the roof had collapsed onto the lower floors with around two-thirds of the building disappearing.

Mayor Benoît Payan condemned the attack on the government building as “unacceptable”.

Violence also erupted in Lyon, where masked rioters reportedly smashed their way into a government tourist office before setting it on fire.

French broadcaster BFMTV reported that hooded attackers vandalised the building and shattered its windows.

Meanwhile, metro stations across France were shut, including stops near the Champs-Élysées, presidential palace and parliament.



Some of the worst violence hit Paris and Marseille, where police buildings were attacked by rioters.

Footage showed masked youths smashing windows before hurling petrol bombs inside.

Gangs also ransacked nearby sports and clothing shops as riot police struggled to contain the chaos.



Macron said today: “There’s no place for violence in our Republic.

“Those who have engaged in destruction, attacked government offices and businesses, and even looted our town halls, will be prosecuted and punished.

“We will stand united against those sowing chaos-people who seek only to tear down our institutions and who prevent others from expressing their grievances peacefully.’



Prime Minister Sebastian Lecornu said: “Peaceful demonstrations have a rightful place in our Republic. Arson, looting, and attacks do not.

“Today, far-Left groups orchestrated violence in several French cities – criminals joined in to loot and destroy.”

Meanwhile, President Emmanuel Macron and his wife Brigitte faced criticism for attending a Céline Dion concert as chaos swept the country.

The couple were filmed dancing in a private box on Friday night, with critics comparing them to King Louis XVI and Marie Antoinette during the French Revolution of 1789.

News.title: Strictly Come Dancing Live: Danny Dyer appeared ‘unimpressed’ over Dani’s ‘intimate’ dance
News.content:
The glitz and the glam of Strictly Come Dancing saw the celebrities channel their favourite icons this week. With Delta Goodrem out the show due to injury, the drama continues - and we're here for all of it!

The stars of Strictly Come Dancing wowed (well, mostly all of them) as they transformed into their idols for Icons Week.

The stars and their professional dance partners brought it all to the dancefloor with performances to the likes of icons Mariah Carey, RAYE, Frank Sinatra and Jon Bon Jovi.

Even the judges transformed into Oasis, Beyonce and Lady Gaga. Much to our delight, we could star spot in the audience, with Ray Winstone supporting daughter Jaime who was sat next to Danny Dyer who there to champion his daughter Dani Dyer.
