A police officer has been injured after he was shot in Nottingham city centre.

The officer, who is in hospital with a foot wound, had approached two suspects in Angle Row shortly before the incident at 4.50am on Sunday, Nottinghamshire Police said.

The two suspects, a man and a woman, fled the scene and a firearm has been recovered by police.

Assistant Chief Constable Claire Rukas said: “This is a shocking incident and a sobering reminder of the potential dangers faced by officers as they work to protect and serve the public.

“As we investigate what happened and work to apprehend the individuals involved, my thoughts today are with the injured officer, his family and colleagues.

“I also ask that anyone with additional information shares this with us without delay. Even the smallest bit of information could make all the difference to this investigation.”

Nottingham East Labour MP Nadia Whittome wrote on X: “My thoughts are with the injured police officer and his family following this truly shocking incident. We all wish him a full and speedy recovery.”

Anyone with information is urged to call 101 quoting incident 106 of 18 October 2026.

News.title: Lesley Manville: ‘My first screen kiss was in a cowshed. I’ve had better since then’
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

When Lesley Manville was 23, she met Mike Leigh – and her future immediately came into focus. Just three years before, she’d been a soap star, appearing on Emmerdale as teenager Rosemary Kendall, but she decided to branch out to see what other roles she could find. “I wanted to be a character actor,” Manville tells me, ensconced in a cosy screening room at Chiswick Cinema. Well, mission very much accomplished. Through Leigh – a defining British filmmaker known for his realistic portrayals of working-class life – she was granted the chance to play roles she never dreamed possible. “Age 16 to 23 was fine, but it didn’t enter my head to play characters; I just played me and I was doing alright. But once I met Mike and we started working together, I loved it.”

Manville has worked with Leigh on eight films in total – more than any other actor – but this just scrapes the surface of a vibrant career that’s traversed stage and screen, big and small, with the actor always bringing a commanding, lived-in aura to her roles, be they icy, fragile, menacing or warm-hearted.

She is a prolific theatre star too: she originated Caryl Churchill and Andrea Dunbar roles in the 1980s, and starred in, among other productions, Ghosts, Long Day’s Journey Into Night and Oedipus. For the latter – her Broadway debut – she won a prestigious Tony Award. To mark the release of her new film, the thriller Winter of the Crow, we’re here to talk about all aspects of her career for interview series Life in Pictures – cutting her teeth on stage, through to her defining working relationships, being headhunted for Phantom Thread by Hollywood maestro Paul Thomas Anderson, her Oscars experience and the TV role she gets stopped for the most. You can watch the full interview here.

Lesley Manville on… starting out on Emmerdale in the 1980s

“It was Emmerdale Farm then. It was on twice-weekly at lunchtime. We shot the exteriors on the same kind of film that Paul Thomas Anderson would use to shoot Phantom Thread. I learnt so much about filming with a single camera. This was a great, great time for me. It was my first time living away from my home in Brighton – and I made some money! It allowed me, aged 19, to get my first flat, and that is not to be sniffed at. When I left, I remember they all said, ‘Why are you going? It’s so hard out there.’ But I knew I had to move on. I had lots more parts to play. It was a really good job. I had my first screen kiss… in a cowshed. I’ve had better screen kisses since then, obviously.”

open image in gallery Lesley Manville in 'Emmerdale' ( ITV )

On... her early theatre work

“My relationship with the Royal Court started from a Mike Leigh film for television that I made called Grown-ups when I was 23. It went out on the BBC and the next day, I was this new actress on the block, even though I’d been working since I was 16. I was at the Royal Court for a while. I did the original Top Girls. The original Rita Sue and Bob Too (both 1982). It was just an amazing time. It’s where I met Gary [Oldman, who she was married to from 1987 to 1989]. Everything was great at the Royal Court. You felt like you were at the cutting edge of things. Over about 12, 13 years, I did about 10 plays there, and now I think how lucky I was. Any young actor who would be able to mirror that situation now would be very lucky.”

open image in gallery Lesley Manville performing 'Serious Money' at Royal Court in 1987 ( Shutterstock )

On... working with Mike Leigh eight times

“I owe it all to him. Everything. I honestly don’t know where I’d be if I hadn’t met him. He liberated me to play characters that weren’t like me. You create a character one-to-one with him for months, then he’ll start to get you involved with other people, and then the improvisations start. You’ll do them in real time – for example, with the barbecue in Another Year (2010), we did a real-time improvisation of that at an afternoon party for five hours. And then it gets distilled into a scene. I’ve done big parts with him, small parts, as do all of his repertoire of actors. But he’s going to get you to play a character that you’ve never played before. I can’t express enough what I owe him.”

open image in gallery Mike Leigh has worked with Lesley Manville more than any other actor ( Getty )

On... working in Hollywood for the 2014 film Maleficent

“You get paid more and the catering’s better! Maleficent was the early days of motion capture. We had to wear what you’d wear for deep-sea diving, except it would have hundreds of cameras on it. You’d wear a helmet with two antennae cameras in your face, and cameras strapped to your body. Imelda Staunton, Juno Temple and I played pixies and we had the Cirque de Soleil people harnessing us up. We were quite literally flying around the studio at Pinewood! We had to do intensive pilates training to get ready for it. It was great fun. When we did Maleficent: Mistress of Evil, which was quite some years later, the technology had come on so far, we did it all with a grey T-shirt, no makeup and like 500 cameras in a semicircle all the way around us. We were on the first film for ages; the second film, I think we did in three afternoons. I wouldn’t like to do a whole big shoot that’s all green screen. I’m not that kind of girl.”

open image in gallery Imelda Staunton and Lesley Manville playing pixies in 2014 film 'Maleficent' ( Disney )

On... being chosen by Paul Thomas Anderson to star opposite Daniel Day-Lewis in Phantom Thread

“The big one. In 2016, my agent said, ‘Paul Thomas Anderson’s gonna call you tomorrow morning at 11am to talk about a film he’s got in his head.’ And I thought, ‘Well, OK. Wow. I bet he’ll forget.’ On the dot, he calls and says, ‘I've got this film. It’s you and Daniel Day-Lewis. You’d be brother and sister, and you run this fashion house, and it’s the Fifties.’ And in my heart, ‘I’m just going, ‘Please, please, please tell me this is mine!’ Because fashion has been a thing all my life.

“I’ll never forget, he said, ‘Give the script a read when you’ve got a minute.’ As if I wasn’t gonna tear through it. He called me back and said, ‘Look, Daniel and I are coming to London in a couple of months, so maybe we can meet up.’ I didn’t know if it was mine. Then I get an email from PTA over the weekend, and he went, ‘Oh sorry, I forgot to say – it’s yours.’ Little detail! So then we started shooting – it was 14 of the most heavenly work weeks of my life. The whole job was something else. I’m not superstitious, but six has been a recurring number in my life, and the script that PTA first sent me was dated 6/6/2016. I’ve still got it. It’s gonna be archived by the V&A.”

open image in gallery Daniel Day-Lewis and Lesley Manville in Paul Thomas Anderson’s 'Phantom Thread' ( Universal Pictures )

On... attending the Oscars as a nominee for Phantom Thread

“I’d never been before. At the end of the ceremony, you’ve been there for five hours and you’re hungry, and it’s a lot of small talk, you know. Nice, but a lot of small talk. I said, ‘What are we gonna do? What’s the Vanity Fair party like?’ And PTA said, ‘It’ll be just like this, but with more models.’ So we did a great thing – me, him, Maya [Rudolph, PTA’s wife] and Jonny [Greenwood, of Radiohead] went to a quiet cocktail room in a hotel, and we had omelettes and cocktails. It was the best end to the night. And at midnight LA time – which is 8am the following morning in the UK – I had to go on the Today programme, so I had to be sober. I thought, ‘I absolutely can’t be drunk as a skunk on live radio!’”

On... BBC series Mum, which ran from 2016 to 2019

“What a beautiful job that was – and it’s the thing I get stopped for the most. If I’m at the National Theatre or the Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York, it’ll be a play, but on the street, on the train, it’s Mum. It was so sublime. Obviously, I get to meet and work with so many different people, and you can’t keep all of them in your contacts list, but very unusually, there were eight principal actors in Mum, and we are all close. I mean, Peter Mullan! I don’t think he’ll mind me saying this, but I think he was nervous doing Mum because he usually plays characters who’re going to, you know, scoop your eyes out. But Peter is the most gentle, warm, loving human being. It was nice to see that natural side of him come out in this. Everyone asks if we’re gonna do any more and I say no because [creator] Stefan Golaszewski intended it as three seasons. That’s what I always saw in my head. It’s beautifully timed – of course you wouldn’t do it again!”

open image in gallery Lesley Manville and Peter Mullan in the BBC series 'Mum' ( BBC )

On… playing Princess Margaret in The Crown

“This was an amazing job. Imelda [Staunton] and I were cast two years before, so I used to wake up every morning thinking ‘I’m gonna play Princess Margaret!’, which was so exciting. And for two years, I could research really leisurely. And working with Imelda – we’d been pixies together! Maleficent was our research, really. I knew it wasn’t gonna be 20 episodes about Princess Margaret, but boy oh boy did Peter Morgan write me two amazing episodes. Astonishing. I felt for Margaret deeply. I felt the pain of somebody trapped in a circumstance and wanting to be something, but not quite having the freedom to be that person. I loved playing her – I had a cigarette holder, a silk dressing gown and a fabulous wig. It was win-win.”

open image in gallery Lesley Manville played Princess Margaret in the final two seasons of 'The Crown' ( Netflix )

On… how she chooses roles

“All I want is to play a cleaning lady in Mrs Harris Goes to Paris [2022] and then Princess Margaret – two ends of the social spectrum. You couldn’t get further away. That’s what gets me up in the morning. I don’t want people to think, ‘Oh, that’s alright for you to say, Lesley. You get those opportunities.’ I’m grateful and humble about that. But that’s my modus operandi.”

On… remaining in the UK

“I never considered moving to America. I didn’t think I would do it as a goal. Why would I do that when I was doing the best work that was on offer to anybody, anywhere? I do think we do the best theatre in the world – and I was doing it at the Royal Shakespeare Company, the National Theatre, the Royal Court, occasionally the West End, working with Mike Leigh, Max Stafford-Clark, Richard Eyre, Nick Hytner, Sam Mendes, Marianne Elliott. I mean, the list goes on and on and on. Why would I go to America?”

On… going viral for saying people shouldn’t take photos in theatres

“Lots of other actresses are doing it now. The thing is, I’m not saying it wouldn’t be all right at the end of any production, but it felt particularly wrong or inappropriate at the end of Oedipus [Robert Icke’s 2024 West End production that she starred in]. You know how it ends! It’s pretty devastating. And most of the audience were sitting there just going, ‘I don’t know what I’ve just watched.’ And then you get these other people who just think, ‘I've gotta capture this on camera.’ Cate Blanchett was going on about it recently because somebody was filming her in Electra/Persona and at the end of the show, she quite rightly said, ‘Look, you’re spoiling it for people who haven’t seen the show yet.’ I feel I’m fighting a losing battle, but I don’t feel I can’t say anything.”

open image in gallery Lesley Manville in new film 'Winter of the Crow' ( Signature Entertainment )

On… being a national treasure

“It’s not for me to say. All I want is for people to like my work, see what I’m trying to do – not just in each individual performance – but acknowledge that I’m trying to do characters that are different and keep it alive for myself, apart from anything. I think I’m just Lesley Manville!”

‘Winter of the Crow’ is in cinemas now

News.title: Nick Knowles fights back tears on live TV – days before DIY SOS ‘rested’ by BBC
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Nick Knowles fought back tears during a live TV appearance just days before it was announced that his long-running home renovation show DIY SOS is to be “rested” by the BBC after 27 years.

Knowles has hosted DIY SOS since 1999, sticking with the show as it transitioned out of being a more traditional home improvement series and into something bigger, with Knowles and his crew of builders repairing and transforming properties across Britain with help from local communities.

It was announced yesterday (17 September) that the show would be “rested” – if not outright axed – and replaced by a spin-off show composed of old footage, due to the corporation’s bid to make £500m in cuts over the next three years.

While it is unclear whether Knowles knew about the impending “resting” during a Tuesday appearance on ITV’s This Morning to promote the show, he did spend the interview discussing the show’s importance to British television and its work to represent and celebrate working class communities on TV.

“[It celebrates] the best of communities all over the country,” he said. “Thousands and thousands of working class heroes, which you don’t see much on TV. We don’t get into those areas. We don’t celebrate working class people, and that’s the kind of community I came from. So it’s a big deal for me to make sure that we represent [them].”

open image in gallery Nick Knowles fights back tears during his Tuesday appearance on ‘This Morning’ ( ITV )

Presenter Ben Shephard then insisted it’s “never felt like a more important time” to see shows like DIY SOS, “at a time when everything feels very divided and divisive and there are things going on that make people feel ostracised or isolated”.

Knowles briefly paused during the remainder of the interview after choking up while discussing an episode of the new series of the show. It sees Knowles and his crew renovating a home in Preston to accommodate the needs of a 16-year-old boy who’d been in hospital for 18 months undergoing surgery to remove a brain tumour, which has left him with complex disabilities.

“The people that turned up just worked and worked and worked because they knew they were trying to get this boy home,” Knowles said. “On this one, because it was his first time from hospital, the builders lined the road and the ambulance came…”

Knowles then choked back tears, before being comforted by Shephard and his co-presenter Cat Deeley.

“I felt exactly the same,” Deeley added.

open image in gallery DIY SOS will be rested in 2027 due to BBC cost-saving measures ( BBC )

Later in the conversation, Knowles discussed the show’s evolution over the decades.

“They wanted something on the BBC that was sort of similar [to Changing Rooms],” he recalled. “But we decided to make it more life-like … [We’ve done] the garden of Great Ormond Street for veterans, re-building at Grenfell after the fire. There have just been so many of these things that have been done. I think that’s my favorite thing and, like you say, it’s more important than ever that people see how many good people there are in the country.”

When Shephard noted that the show had been airing for 35 series “and that there’ll be plenty more as well”, Knowles pointedly did not respond.

Yesterday a BBC spokesperson confirmed that the show will be leaving the airwaves, writing: “In light of the BBC’s savings challenges we have taken the decision to rest DIY SOS in 2027 and commission a new spin-off show instead from producers South Shore.

“DIY SOS Rebuilt My Life will revisit successes from the show’s past and expand the brand on the BBC in a more cost-effective way next year.”

The Independent has contacted Knowles for comment.

News.title: Ruthless Daniel Dubois dispatches Fabio Wardley in just two rounds
News.content:
Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of Daniel Dubois vs Fabio Wardley.

When Wardley dragged himself out of the ring at Manchester’s Co-Op LIVE Arena, the physical damage was obvious, but the psychological sting was far deeper. Wardley had Dubois severely hurt early on, flooring the Londoner twice and teetering on the verge of a career-defining stoppage. Instead, he let the knockout slip away, allowed Dubois to find his rhythm, and was ultimately broken down and halted in the 11th round - surrendering his WBO heavyweight belt in a dramatic comeback victory.

Now, just five months after that gruelling night, the two heavyweights meet again at London’s O2 Arena in an immediate rematch that carries potentially massive implications for the entire division.

For Wardley (20-1-1, 19 KOs), the decision to trigger his rematch clause was instant. Dismissing concerns over the severe punishment he absorbed down the stretch, the Ipswich man is motivated entirely by redemption and the belief that his early success proved Dubois is beatable.

Dubois (23-3, 22 KOs), however, views things very differently. Entering as The Ring’s No. 1 heavyweight contender and a proven two-time world champion, Dubois has brushed off Wardley’s power, claiming his rival “punches like a baby” and insists Wardley threw away his one and only chance at glory in Manchester.

With Oleksandr Usyk approaching the final chapter of his career and the Anthony Joshua vs. Tyson Fury blockbuster looming just eight weeks away, this London clash is far more than a personal grudge match. The winner won’t just walk away with the WBO strap; they will stake an undeniable claim as the torch-bearer for the heavyweight division’s next era if they can land another title fight in short order.

News.title: Newcastle jeers tell Matthias Jaissle his ‘vertical’ football is not working
News.content:
Newcastle United look like a poor team playing badly. The evidence is increasingly damning after Matthias Jaissle’s side were loudly booed off at the end of this limp defeat.

This has all the makings of a long, hard season. Anger is already rising to the surface, even though Jaissle claimed Newcastle deserved more from a game they “controlled” in the first half and “dominated” in the second. Those comments jarred with what we had just seen.

After four years of enjoying an upward trajectory under Eddie Howe, the team faded last season, sold their best players in the summer, lost the manager and there is no evidence yet they have replaced anything with better.

This was supposed to be a reaction to the embarrassing 4-1 thrashing at Coventry City, but it led to another loss and, in the first half at least, another abject display. Aston Villa were always the more fluent and more threatening. They should have won by more than just Johan Manzambi’s first-half header.

News.title: Liverpool’s £400m front line clicks but win at Brentford turns on red card
News.content:
Only time will tell if Liverpool’s £400m front line can ever justify the extraordinary amount of money that was spent on them, but this was at least a significant step in the right direction. In a gritty victory away to Brentford, all four of Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz, Bradley Barcola and Victor Muñoz either scored or assisted goals.

Admittedly, the task was made significantly easier by the major turning point of this game: a red card for Brentford’s Yehor Yarmoliuk. At the time of Yarmoliuk’s “headbutting action” towards Liverpool defender Jeremy Jacquet, the visitors were trailing 1-0 and looking worryingly short of ideas in attack.

But as the context of the match changed, so did the level of threat from the visitors. Against 10 men, with more space in which to operate, Liverpool’s forwards looked increasingly dangerous. Wirtz began to pull the strings, Barcola started to cause problems, Muñoz stretched the Brentford defence and Isak became a lurking menace.

News.title: Steely Chelsea triumph despite losing Martinez to head injury
News.content:
This was the afternoon when Xabi Alonso’s Chelsea went from swashbuckling to stoic, thrilling to tenacious.

For all Alonso’s attacking vigour at the start of his reign, there can have been no more symbolically satisfying victory under the new coach than this resolute win at Everton – the most vivid example of an increasingly impressive transformation.

This was what Alonso described as “winning in a different way”. A triumph amid the adversity of losing goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez to what appears to be a serious injury after a head collision with Jarrad Branthwaite is just one facet of why the joyous visiting supporters might consider this an early turning point.

Where recently they wilted, on Saturday they thrived in securing a first Premier League clean sheet for nine months.

Much more of this and the adjectives which were splattered across Chelsea during the golden years of José Mourinho – solid, robust and dogged – will be part of the Stamford Bridge lexicon once more.

“Just one day,” Alonso warned, both acclaiming the importance of the win while wisely preaching caution. “It will be key when we manage 10 clean sheets, even though this one feels good. We need to repeat it again and again, but the mentality was very good. Sometimes it is not to play nice, it is to play good – to win second balls, and to be efficient. We needed one of these: a clean sheet and a win.”

Asked about Martinez’s condition, Alonso said: “It was a concussion, but beyond that I do not know. I have only seen one clip of the incident, so we need to wait.

“What we know is that he left the stadium conscious and is now in hospital undergoing precautionary tests.

“We need to wait. Hopefully it will not be too serious, but at the moment we just have to wait.”

News.title: Wallabies humiliated in ‘unacceptable’ thrashing by New Zealand
News.content:
New Zealand blew Australia off the field in an extraordinary first-half display in Sydney as they claimed a 13th successive win against the Wallabies and completed a 2-0 Bledisloe Cup clean sweep.

The annual series had already gone New Zealand’s way for a 24th successive year at Eden Park last weekend, but Australia did enough in a highly competitive first half in Auckland to suggest they could give the All Blacks a game on their home turf. And in a breathless opening six minutes in Sydney, it looked as if they might.

The ball-in-play time during that opening spell was incredible as both teams committed to fast, attacking rugby, offloading from everywhere. Like two heavyweights going toe-to-toe in the opening round of a boxing contest, throwing haymakers to see who would get knocked out first.

Ryan Lonergan produced an excellent turnover for the Wallabies to trigger an Australia counter, and the irrepressible Peter Lakai responded with one for the visitors, as the ball travelled from one end of the pitch to the other in one long unbroken spell.

But after New Zealand wing Josh Moorby finally crossed the whitewash, it was Australia who found themselves out on their feet, punch drunk.

News.title: England’s Rugby League World Cup hopes in tatters after Tonga defeat
News.content:
McDermott was full of credit. “They’re a big team, a strong team,” he said. “They’ve got some tremendous players in there, and I thought we stuck toe-to-toe with them for nearly all the game.

“They scored some tries through kicks, which are always hard to defend, and then towards the back-end of the game we made some errors chasing the scoreboard.”

It should be factored in that this was McDermott’s first match in charge and strides have clearly been made since England were woeful in losing the Ashes 3-0 last year.

“I thought we opened up Tonga in that first 20,” McDermott added. “Whether we went through the middle or the edge, we found ourselves in a good ball position, but we had some scrappy finishes to the good ball sets. It was too erratic. We wanted to put a load of fatigue into Tonga, but credit to them. I thought they were terrific defensively.”

Having been beaten by Samoa in the World Cup four years ago, England must face up to the burgeoning conviction that they are no longer among the top three countries in international rugby league. There was the palpable sense of the old order being changed in a stadium packed with the red shirts of Tonga.

As Williams said in the build-up, this is a “mad” format, with only the top two from the combined six-team group of Pool B and C going through to the semi-finals, but now it is very simple as far as England are concerned. They must beat France and Papua New Guinea in their remaining two matches, and do so heavily, then pray that Tonga can beat Samoa in the last match of the pool stage. However, Samoa thumped France 78-4 on Friday, so even that potential avenue appears blocked. McDermott has no other option but to look ahead.

“We know what’s in front of us now, we’ve got to win the next two games and improve on the things we need to improve on,” he said. “But I’ve seen enough tonight that is telling me we’re heading in the right direction.

“It would be tremendously disrespectful to either France or PNG to suggest we’re going to rack up points. I can start looking at points difference and start working out our strategies, but the road will lead us back to winning those two games, and winning them in a strong way.”

Team details

England Radley, Pearce-Paul, Nsemba (King 62), Thompson (Harvard 29, Currie 69), O’Neill (Litten 58); Brimson (Nsemba 79), Young, Savala, Farnworth, Eckersley, Williams, Smith, King (Walters 33, Thompson 76).

Tonga Frizell (Vaimauga 28, Taumalolo 64), Wong (Olakau’atu 41), Olakau’atu (Fonua-Blake 38, Utoikamanu 66), Taumalolo (Halasima 31), Foketi; Hopoate, Watene-Zelezniak, Koula, Toia, Fifita, Fainu (Lolohea 17), Katoa, Fonua-Blake (Utoikamanu 21, Wong 52).

Referee Gerard Sutton (Australia).

England’s Rugby League World Cup challenge could well be over, just 80 minutes after it started.

Brian McDermott’s hopes of qualifying for the semi-finals were all but shattered in his side’s first pool match in a brutal encounter in which Pacific Island physicality and passion ultimately earned Tonga a famous victory.

England displayed huge attacking courage with their offload strategy – in all, they made 26 – but their adventurous intent could not find the finishing touch and was not enough to topple a ferocious opposition defence in Perth. Despite excellent performances from captain George Williams and Dom Young, they were ultimately blown off HBF Park.

On their seventh attempt, this was Tonga’s first win over England and although this intense contest was for, so long, much closer than the scoreboard finally showed, there can be no doubting the excellence of Kristian Woolf’s team and the ruthlessness they displayed in the last quarter in which they never stopped tackling refused to stop coming.

News.title: ‘The boats don’t stop’: The deadly coastline that has become a trafficking superhighway
News.content:
The dangers were illustrated earlier this month, when a boat carrying more than 300 migrants sank near Obock on its way to Yemen. At least 139 people drowned, including 15 children. There were 700 drownings or people lost at sea on the route in 2025.

“The boats don’t stop, day or night,” the local coastguard chief told the Telegraph as he looked out at the waterway, walkie-talkie in hand, one day earlier this month.

The chief, who declined to be named, pointed to skiffs and fishing boats moored in a lagoon outside his outpost, that he had confiscated from smugglers and traffickers.

The world has become familiar with the 18-mile-wide Bab el-Mandeb strait as one of the globe’s most congested and strategically important maritime choke points.

Sitting to the south of the Suez Canal, the East-West artery flowing through the strait carries approximately 12 to 15 percent of global maritime trade.

What is less well known is that there is also a migration superhighway running across the strait, linking Africa via Djibouti to Yemen and the Gulf beyond.

Many tens of thousands of people cross the waterway each year and while Yemeni refugees fleeing the Houthi offensive have made headlines in recent weeks, the majority of those braving the waterway are heading the other way.

This maritime migrant route out of Africa has recently been busier than all the crossings across the Mediterranean into Europe, according to the International Organisation for Migration (IOM).

The IOM estimates there were nearly 64,000 crossings across the Bab el-Mandeb in the first four months of 2026, compared with a total of just over 23,000 across the Western, Eastern and central routes of the Med.

The vast majority heading east are Ethiopians so desperate to find work in the Gulf that they are prepared to trek through war-torn Yemen, which has been tipped into a humanitarian crisis by its civil war.

The IOM recorded some 202,000 migrant trips into Djibouti from Ethiopia in 2025 and by early October, the figure for 2026 had already hit 177,000.

The reignited war in Ethiopia’s Tigray region is expected to increase the numbers wanting to leave, yet the exodus is also being held up by escalating fighting along Yemen’s coast between Houthis and the government.

Fewer are now able to get across the strait, leaving them stranded on the western side, or forced to take more dangerous routes.

News.title: Asia’s vaccine self-sufficiency drive gets $650m boost
News.content:
An “innovative” partnership to boost vaccine security across Southeast Asia will inject up to $650 million into regional manufacturing, in a bid to reduce reliance on imported shots.

The five-year initiative, announced at the annual meetings of the World Bank and International Monetary Fund in Bangkok on Friday, will see major lenders, non-profits, and the private sector come together to invest in the region’s vaccine industry.

Currently Southeast Asia’s production base remains limited and exposed. The majority of shots are imported, and any capacity the region does have is highly concentrated – one analysis this year estimates 60 to 90 per cent sits with a single vaccine manufacturer.

Even before Covid-19 hit, this vulnerability was recognised. The Association of Southeast Asian Nations (Asean), a regional bloc of 11 countries, endorsed a vaccine security and self-reliance initiative in 2019, driven by Thailand’s National Vaccine Institute (NVI).

These concerns have mounted since the pandemic, but up until now investment as well as political will has been lacking. The partnership announced on Friday, led by NVI, hopes to remedy this, and develop a model that can be copied worldwide.

​​“If we can do it here in Asia, then that really provides a model for the world,” said Aurélia Nguyen, deputy CEO of the Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations (Cepi), a a vaccine research non-profit. “We can build it out in Africa, in Latin America, and that really gives us the resilience that we want the next time we have a major epidemic.”

Cepi has committed up to $20 million of “catalytic funding” for the programme, which is backed by the World Bank as well as organisations like the Singapore-based AVPN investment network.

In all, the package of loans and grants will include at least $174m in public financing, and up to $460m in private capital mobilisation for regional vaccine manufacturing. Further details, including recipients, have not yet been announced.

But Paschal Donohoe, the managing director and chief knowledge officer of the World Bank Group, told a panel in the Thai capital that “we believe this has the ability over time to mobilise up to $650m of finance”.

He added that the group would use public loans and grants alongside investments by its private-sector arm, the IFC, while its guarantee arm, MIGA, would help cover investors against risk.

“It’s really important because each element of the World Bank Group is involved in it,” Donohoe said. “We’re not just talking the talk, but walking the walk.”

Speaking to the Telegraph after the event, Nguyen added: “Innovative models and partnerships like this, where we’re each bringing a piece to de-risk scientific technology, [allow us] to leverage larger quantities of capital.

“But I think what’s also helpful in this model is, beyond the financing, [we] have a sort of coordinating umbrella through Asean,” she said. “So you can be smart and [avoid] duplicating investments, which brings commercial sustainability and resilience for health systems.”

Nakorn Premsri, the director of NVI, added that the investment model will help “build a more sustainable and resilient regional vaccine ecosystem, to meet both routine needs and the demands of health emergencies”.

Protect yourself and your family by learning more about Global Health Security

Sports.title: Chelsea star Emi Martinez ‘back in a few weeks’ as star breaks silence on his sickening head injury
Sports.content:
Next

EMI MARTINEZ has given a positive update on his health after his grisly clash of heads against Everton.

The Argentina international was stretchered off the field against the Toffees on Saturday after suffering a nasty clash of heads in the second half.



He contested the ball with Jarrad Branthwaite before they smashed into each other, with the Blues man coming off worse.

He was placed on a backboard and transported to hospital, with Mike Penders coming on to replace him.



But now the star and his wife have revealed that his surgery has been successful and that the outlook is a positive one, claiming he will be back in action in just weeks.

Martinez’s wife Mandinha first wrote on Instagram on Saturday night: “Thank you all for the lovely messages and for checking in on Emi.

“He’s doing fine, it’s nothing serious, and he’ll soon be back to his usual self.

“Thank you from the bottom of my heart for so much love and support.”

It was revealed on Saturday that the star was set to undergo surgery on his jaw following the scary incident.

But himself Martinez then spoke out in the early hours of Sunday morning to confirm the procedure had been successful.



He also shared a snap of him giving a gesture from his hospital bed.

He said: “Thanks to everyone for the messages. The surgery went well.

“The most important thing is that we won and kept a clean sheet.

We’ll be back in a few weeks.”

In the aftermath of Chelsea’s 2-0 win at Everton, Blues boss Xabi Alonso revealed the 34-year-old World Cup winner was in hospital.



He said: “As far as I know he left the stadium conscious. Right now he’s in the hospital doing precautionary tests, so let’s see. But this is what I know so far.”

Chelsea’s veteran midfielder Jordan Henderson also said: “He’s very important. It looked pretty bad actually so I hope he’s okay.

“All the lads and everyone will be thinking of him and texting him so fingers crossed it’s nothing major and he can be back with us pretty soon because he’s a really important figure not only on the pitch but around the dressing room too.”

Saturday afternoon’s win marked Chelsea’s first Premier League clean sheet in nine months as they rose to fourth ahead of Brentford on 13 points.

Nottingham Forest vs Arsenal preview

Nottingham Forest host Arsenal in Sunday’s Premier League clash, with Oliver Glasner in desperate need of a morale-boosting victory.

The Premier League hasn’t been too kind to the Austrian of late.

Glasner has managed just five wins in 29 games since December 2025, while his win percentage during that spell stands at just 17% – the second-lowest of any manager with 20 or more games.

His side arrive down in 15th spot with just one win in their opening six matches, with only Tottenham having scored fewer goals.

That’s something of an anomaly, though, given their shot count, expected goals and big chances are the highest they’ve recorded in any of the last five seasons.

That, and the fact they’ve converted just 4.7% of their shots, was laid bare against Crystal Palace last time out.

The Tricky Trees created eight big chances but came away empty-handed – the first time a top-flight team had created that many big chances in a single match and still gone on to lose.

They’ll need to be ruthless this afternoon if they’re to get anything against an Arsenal side they’ve struggled against in recent years.



Nottingham Forest have won just one of their last 11 Premier League games against Arsenal and have failed to score in each of their last four.

That’s bad news against a Gunners side who’ve won 14 of their last 17 Premier League games and arrive on the back of successive victories over Leeds and Lille in the Champions League midweek.

Still, Arsenal are giving up more chances than usual and have gone 1-0 down in three of their last four Premier League matches.

Sports.title: PSG star Maghnes Akliouche shares picture of ankle cut open after Strasbourg opponent escapes red card for wild tackle
Sports.content:
Next

MAGHNES AKLIOUCHE was left with a bloodied ankle following a lunging tackle by Jeyland Mitchell.

But the match referee opted NOT to send the defender off during the closing stages of Paris Saint-Germain‘s 3-1 win at Strasbourg.

Summer arrival from Monaco Akliouche was handed his third consecutive start by boss Luis Enrique following goals against Le Mans and Manchester City.



PSG trailed for much of this encounter at Strasbourg, courtesy of Giovanni Reyna‘s 17th minute effort.



But Enrique’s men turned the game on its head late on, despite a missed penalty by Ousmane Dembele.

Last year’s Ballon d’Or winner subsequently teed up Ilia Zabarnyi to score the equaliser.

The winger then completed his atonement by putting his side in front on 85 minutes.

With just one minute of regulation time remaining, Akliouche attempted to skip past a challenge by Mitchell.

The Costa Rican initially won the ball with his flying challenge.

But his follow through nastily caught Akliouche’s ankle.

BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS



The 24-year-old writhed in pain following the tackle – although no red card was forthcoming from the referee.

With PSG having already used all their substitutions, Akliouche gutted it out and completed the match.

And Desire Doue scored deep into stoppage time to seal PSG’s impressive comeback win.

After the game, Akliouche showed off the damage done by tackle.

In a picture posted by RMC Sport reporter Arthur Perrot, a nasty gash could be seen on Akliouche’s ankle through a tear in his sock.



Per French outlet Le Parisien, Akliouche is set to undergo tests on Sunday to determine the extent of the injury.

Insiders have been left bewildered at Mitchell not receiving a red card for the challenge.

PSG were handed a further injury scare as Nuno Mendes did not complete the match.

The full-back replaced Lucas Digne on 53 minutes but went off again late on after appearing to feel an issue in his thigh.

Enrique said after the game: “He felt a slight thing, we decided not to take any risks.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

“I don’t know if we can call it an injury, but we decided to play with one less player because we didn’t want to take any risks.”

PSG return to action on Tuesday night as they host Barcelona in the Champions League.

Sports.title: Grimsby star handed red card while writhing in agony after suffering horror leg break in EFL clash
Sports.content:
GRIM INJURY Grimsby star handed red card while writhing in agony after suffering horror leg break in EFL clash







Next

GRIMSBY defender Edon Pruti was sensationally sent off while suffering a suspected DOUBLE LEG BREAK n an X-rated challenge.

The Mariners fell to a 2-0 defeat against a Northampton side which was taken over by Alexandre Pato last month.



And Pruti, 24, was left writhing in agony as Grimsby desperately searched for a way back into the League Two showdown.

The former Burnley youngster crashed into a full-blooded challenge with Joe Wormleighton minutes after Jon Guthrie had doubled Northampton’s lead.



Both sets of players quickly gestured for medics to rush onto the pitch when it became clear Pruti was in serious pain.

But referee Martin Woods was in an unforgiving mood as he had already taken the red card out of his pocket before pleading for medical attention.

Pruti was then carried off on a stretcher and rushed to hospital – after being given his marching orders.

And Grimsby chief David Artell hit out at Woods for brandishing a red card following the horrific injury.

The former Crewe boss, who has been in charge at Blundell Park since 2023, said: “It looks like a double leg break, unfortunately.

“I assume he will have an operation but I haven’t been able to speak to him yet. We obviously wish him a speedy recovery.

“I don’t understand how someone can break their leg and get sent off. We also heard the ref on the comms telling Doug [Tharme] to get off the pitch when he’s clearly incapacitated.

“It’s mental and I don’t like it because player’s safety is paramount, but I don’t want to speak too much about the ref because I’ll end up saying something I shouldn’t.

“I asked to speak to the ref at Port Vale last weekend but he had already left after I had finished with the media. I asked him to stay and I got a phone call from Mike Jones apologising for the referee’s cowardice.

Sports.title: Van Gerwen suffers another early exit as Van Veen makes history
Sports.content:
Dutch favourite Michael van Gerwen suffered a shock second-round exit at the Dutch Darts Championship on Saturday, losing 6-5 to Irishman William O'Connor.

The defeat extends Van Gerwen's poor run of form, having lost his opening match at four European Tour events this season before arriving in Maastricht: the European Darts Trophy, German Darts Grand Prix, Flanders Darts Trophy and Swiss Darts Trophy. It marks his most first-round exits in a single season since the tour began in 2012.

O'Connor produced a superb display, firing in three ton-plus checkouts of 136, 131 and 121 to seal his victory and book his place in round three.

Elsewhere on Saturday, Gerwyn Price's return to the stage ended in glory as he beat Scott Williams 6-3, while Gian van Veen broke the European Tour record average.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Earlier this year, Laura Turner and Chris Murphy reviewed Van Gerwen's limp loss to Dirk van Duijvenbode at the World Matchplay and suggest he's becoming like Manchester United

Martin Schindler and Stephen Bunting also jumped into the qualification spots for Dortmund.

Van Veen averaged a staggering 120.24 in whitewashing Sebastian Bialecki, breaking the previous record of 118.66 by Dave Chisnall.

Schindler sealed his spot at the European Championships later this month with his victory over Karel Sedlacek.

Bunting left it late to secure his place at the European Championship, beating already-qualified Cameron Menzies 6-2 to book his spot. The former Masters champion needed a strong finish to get over the line.

The 41-year-old pinned six out of ten attempts at the outer ring in his victory over the Scot, and jumped into the qualifying places, knocking Kim Huybrechts out of the running.

Image: Dutchman Gian van Veen broke the European Tour record average on Saturday

Brendan Dolan remains the only player capable of pushing Sedlacek out of the European Championship qualifying spots after beating Heine Uuldriks 6-4. The Northern Irishman had led 4-1 before being pegged back.

Nathan Aspinall ended Michael Smith's hopes of qualifying for Dortmund with a dominant 6-1 victory. The World Grand Prix semi-finalist averaged over 102 to dispatch the former world champion.

Wessel Nijman and Danny Noppert also secured their places in Sunday's action, with the Dutch pair defeating Jeffrey De Graaf and Dave Chisnall respectively.

Niels Zonneveld edged a last-leg decider against Krzysztof Ratajski, hitting seven maximums for the second consecutive match to book his place in round three. Fellow Dutchman Jermaine Wattimena also progressed, beating Host Nation Qualifier Jimmy van Schie 6-2.

European Tour ranking leader Ross Smith will face Ryan Searle in round three after overcoming Ryan Joyce and Dirk van Duijvenbode respectively.

Sports.title: Dubois wants Usyk trilogy fight: 'We're coming out on top this time!'
Sports.content:
Daniel Dubois, the WBO heavyweight world champion, believes he would defeat Oleksandr Usyk if they had a trilogy fight.

Twice Dubois has boxed the imperious Ukrainian, and twice Usyk, an unbeaten and two-time undisputed champion at heavyweight, has stopped the Londoner.

But after a stunning two-round victory in his rematch with Fabio Wardley on Saturday, Dubois is convinced he has reached a new level and can beat Usyk.

No heavyweight, Dubois is adamant, can stand up to the punches he hit Wardley with.

"No. Fabio's got a great chin. He's known for taking punishment but I was going through him. I just had to pull myself back and reset. I want to know who's next!" Dubois declared.

Image: Dubois finishes Wardley in a corner

He would welcome a potential trilogy fight with Usyk. "Definitely, definitely, I'd love that," Dubois said. "We're coming out on top this time. We've made our mistakes and we're coming out on top."

Promoter Frank Warren said: "Daniel in my opinion he's not the same fighter he was even a year ago. He's a totally different fighter now.

"When he's doing what he's doing at his best, you've got to be some fighter to be standing and being able to take those shots. He's a tremendous puncher. When he gets you in trouble, you are in trouble. He's a good finisher."

Usyk vacated all the world titles he held, allowing Dubois to claim the WBO belt ahead of his first fight with Wardley, Filip Hrgovic to pick up the IBF strap after beating Moses Itauma, and Agit Kabayel to be elevated to WBC heavyweight world champion.

Image: Dubois' jab hurts Wardley

Next year Dubois is looking to add more championships to his collection. "I've heard talk about Kabayel but I'll fight whoever's next in line. Whoever pays the most cash," Dubois said.

"The future's looking bright."

Promoter Frank Warren thinks it will take 18 months for a new undisputed champion to be crowned, but expects a wave of heavyweight unifications to get under way in next year.

"I think it'll happen in about 18 months because of the timings of it all," Warren said. "We will make them as soon as we can, I expect in the first quarter we'll have at least one of those unifications on. If we get it on, somebody's going to be holding two belts.

"Filip's got a mandatory against [Frank] Sanchez," Warren noted. "We've got Agit, who's fighting in November in Germany and we've got Tyson [Fury] and AJ fighting in December [for the WBA 'super' title]. So they're all busy but we'll be out, don't worry about that.

Image: Dubois has his hand raised in victory. (Photos: Leigh Dawney/Queensberry Promotions)

"The good thing about it is everybody wants to fight. They're fighting men.

"We want the best fighting the best to find out who is the best," the promoter continued. "Get Usyk back in it.

"There's all sort of permutations. One thing for sure is 2027 is going to be a phenomenal year.

"[Dubois] wants the four belts. So do all the other guys. That's what's going to be so exciting."

Sports.title: Rangers miss chance to go top as Jones earns Dundee a point
Sports.content:
Callum Jones scored a second-half equaliser as Rangers were held to a 2-2 draw by Dundee and missed the chance to go top of the Scottish Premiership.

Dundee opened the scoring when Rangers failed to deal with a routine long ball, with Bradley Fink capitalising to round the goalkeeper and slide home.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Bradley Fink's composed finish gave Dundee the lead against Rangers.

The lead did not last long, though, as Badredine Bouanani cut inside and curled in a stunning equaliser to open his account for Rangers.

Nico Raskin scored the goal of the game when his shot from outside the area went in off the underside of the crossbar.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Nicolas Raskin produced an outrageous strike to put Rangers back in front against Dundee.

But Jones then caught Dan Neil dwelling on the ball and nicked it off the Rangers captain to slot home the Dundee equaliser.

Rangers remain second and move one point behind Celtic, who host Hearts live on Sky Sports on Sunday from 2.30pm.

The key moments from Dens Park

8: BLOCKED! Kim has a shot blocked with the goal gaping. Rangers cry for handball but nothing doing.

14: SHOT! Forrest drives from midfield and shoots from the outside of the area, but Pandur gathers comfortably.

23: SHOT! Hay has a speculative shot and again it's saved comfortably by Pandur.

28: SAVE! Hamilton whips a free kick across and Astley heads towards goal from outside of the area tipped behind by Pandur.

29: OFF THE BAR! Hay leaps to meet the corner and it rattles the bar.

36: CLOSE! Hamilton takes an early shot after Dundee win the ball back and it goes just wide.

37: GOAL! Fink rounds the goalkeeper and scores!

42: GOAL! Bouanani curls into the top corner for his first goal for Rangers!

56: SAVE! Gassama shoots from the edge of the area, and it's saved one-handed by the 'keeper

60: GOAL! Nico Raskin scores a screamer off the bar from outside of the area.

69: GOAL! Neil dwells on the ball and is dispossessed by Jones who slots past the goalkeeper to get Dundee level!

74: CLOSE! Ball falls to Neil in the six-yard box but Dundee somehow scramble the ball clear!

McInnes: We shouldn't need three goals to win

Rangers boss Derek McInnes:

"I thought Dundee's press was good, as expected, and we wanted to try and draw the centre-backs out at times and try and hit spaces and feed our wide players and try and get 1v1.

"It never quite materialised.

"We shouldn't need to come away from home and need to score three goals to win a game.

"Two goals should have been enough tonight. We had a few chances when it went to two each.

"Dundee are a good team, but I think we gifted an opportunity there not to take all three points.

"We're disappointed not to come away with three points."

Pressley: We showed grit and determination

Image: Callum Jones scores for Dundee to make it 2-2

Dundee boss Steven Pressley:

"I think it was a game of two halves.

"I thought we were outstanding in the first half, really aggressive, controlled a lot of the game.

"We were really strong on second balls, had one or two moments where we should have capitalised and restricted Rangers to very little.

"We obviously expected a reaction from Rangers and they gave that reaction. They put us under a lot of pressure in the second half.

"We showed grit and determination.

"The game was getting away from us but we never gave up, we kept going and going and (Callum) Jones got his reward for a really strong performance today."

Boyd: Dundee asked questions of Rangers

Sky Sports' Kris Boyd:

"Dundee are a good team. They're not there [in the table] by fluke or luck.

"They've got a style of play, Steven Pressley has got a group of players willing to run themselves into the ground for him and that's hard to get.

"They put in a shift and even when they're asked to dig in and suffer like they did for the first 20/25 minutes of that second half.

"They then got a second wind and came back at Rangers and asked questions of them.

"A draw was a fair result. It took wonder strikes to get Rangers two goals.

"There was a lack of creativity at the top end of the pitch and it's something they're going to have to improve."

Sports.title: Dubois smashes through Wardley to win world title rematch in two rounds
Sports.content:
Daniel Dubois smashed Fabio Wardley to defeat in the second round of their world championship rematch at London’s O2 Arena.

Dubois retained the WBO heavyweight title he won from Wardley in May in crushing style, picking up just where he left off in their first fight.

Dubois and Wardley were renewing hostilities only five months after a frenetic and ultimately brutal contest.

Then London's Dubois had needed to rise twice from early knockdowns to punch out a savage 11-round victory over Wardley, hurting the Ipswich fighter even though Wardley was stopped on his feet.

Image: Dubois finishes Wardley in a corner.

Wardley, determined to win back his world title as soon as he could, exercised the rematch clause in his contract and forced this second fight to take place.

But Dubois snuffed out his hopes with brutal speed.

A powerful right cross from Dubois sent Wardley briefly down to one knee in the opening seconds of the first round. Wardley sprang back to his feet immediately, inviting the right uppercut that followed.

The referee administered a count, and that proved to be just a momentary reprieve. Dubois set about him with shuddering force for the rest of the round.

Dubois' jab rocketed in. Wardley missed with a wild right and the champion knocked him back on his heels. Dubois dashed his right down, hitting Wardley almost at will.

He had Wardley under terrible pressure at the end of the first and trainer Ben Davison climbed up onto the ring apron, moments away from pulling Wardley out as the bell chimed to end the round.

Image: Dubois picked up where he left off in their savage first fight.

The champion continued his onslaught in the second. Wardley couldn't escape from those thunderous punches and he swayed, pained back into the ropes.

Another Dubois cross connected clean, with such force it loosened Wardley's legs beneath him. Bravely he kept himself upright. But he could not stave off the attack.

An unrelenting Dubois positioned his prey in a corner and went in for a finish. He hacked right hooks over and lashed in huge punches to the head.

He hammered those shots into him, jolting Wardley's head on his neck with a salvo of stunning punches, until Wardley's trainer Davison could leave it no longer. He threw in the towel and the referee rushed in to end it.

Image: Dubois has his hand raised in victory

'Bad intentions from the beginning'

"I had bad intentions from the beginning," Dubois said. "Our back was against the wall first time. We just had to go out there and show we meant business tonight."

Wardley reflected: "It's never fun to lose. It is what it is, I've always thrown myself in with the biggest, toughest, meanest guys around, there's no shame in testing yourself against the best.

"Daniel is testament to coming again and I'll come again."

On the undercard Bakhodir Jalolov, a two-time Olympic super-heavyweight gold medallist, showcased just what makes him so formidable as he hammered out a 10 round unanimous decision victory over Solomon Dacres.

Image: Bakhodir Jalolov dominates Solomon Dacres (Photos: Leigh Dawney/Queensberry)

But he also displayed what can make him so frustrating to watch. The towering southpaw controlled virtually the whole bout and struck Dacres over early in the fifth round.

The knockdown was superb, Jalolov using his right to take Dacres' left glove away from his guard, opening up a path for the Uzbek's booming left cross - a shot that sent Dacres to the canvas and bloodied his nose.

But Jalolov didn't capitalise and continued to work in single shots, albeit excellent single shots, as he dominated without turning up the pressure, winning 99-91 and 99-90 twice.

20-year-old Irish heavyweight prospect Adam Olaniyan made short work of journeyman Dan Garber.

Image: Adam Olaniyan takes out Dan Garber

In his fifth pro fight, Olaniyan maintained his 100 percent finish rate stopping Garber in the second round.

Busy without rushing his work, Olaniyan's right cranked Garber's back into a corner post at the end of the first round.

He picked up from there for the second, trapping Garber on the ropes and putting him down with another heavy cross.

Garber's corner threw in the towel, then threw in a second. But the referee kicked them out the ring and Garber tried to fight on. He was though promptly crumpled a second time. After rising unsteadily the referee waved it off at 1-15.

In a British and Commonwealth lightweight title fight Michael Gomez Jnr looked to have dominated Louie O'Doherty over 12 rounds, only to be held to a majority draw.

Champions Cup: Munster honour Anthony Foley with emotional win over Racing 92; Leinster, Glasgow shine as Saracens and Bath fall

Brian Gleeson was among the try scorers as Munster beat Racing 92 in Cork on a day of emotion and tributes a decade on from the death of Anthony Foley

A decade to the day since the rugby world learned of head coach Anthony Foley’s death at the age of 42, Munster marked the poignant anniversary with a stirring 33-25 Champions Cup victory over Racing 92.

The night of Friday October 16, 2016 saw Foley pass away in his sleep the night before Munster were due to face Racing in Paris, with their fixture 10 years on staged at Páirc Uí Chaoimh in Cork.

Munster crossed for five tries in a hard-fought contest, with No 8 Brian Gleeson - wearing 24 with Foley's old number of 8 retired for the match, as it was in 2016 - joined on the scoresheet by wing Shay McCarthy, lock Tadhg Beirne, replacement Fineen Wycherley and scrum-half Craig Casey.

Twitter Due to your consent preferences, you’re not able to view this Privacy Options

Racing responded with three tries of their own through wing Wilfried Hulleu, replacement scrum-half Maxime Machenaud and centre Joseph Manu, denying Munster a bonus-point victory. Under the tournament's new rules, teams must score at least three more tries than their opponents to secure the full five points.

The match came a day after the shocking death of Lions second row Hyron Andrews in France ahead of a Champions Cup fixture in La Rochelle. Emotional tributes were paid to both Andrews and Foley before kick-off.

Glasgow, Leinster post big opening away-day victories | Saracens lose at Connacht

Elsewhere, Glasgow Warriors extended their unbeaten start to the new season by pulling away to claim an impressive 47-27 win at Sale Sharks.

Glasgow's winning score might have looked convincing but they only secured victory in the final 20 minutes after Rekeiti Ma'asi-White had temporarily reduced Sale's deficit to four.

The game looked in the balance until late tries from Rory Darge, Ollie Smith and debutant Otavio Tuipulotu helped Glasgow pull away and wrap up a precious bonus-point win.

Leinster made a flying start to their campaign with an emphatic 48-23 victory away to Clermont Auvergne. Tadhg Furlong, Dan Sheehan (two), Sam Prendergast, Jack Conan and Tommy O'Brien all crossed the line, while a penalty try completed a dominant seven-try display.

Connacht pulled off a stunning 45-36 victory over Saracens in Galway, scoring tries through Cian Prendergast (two), Cathal Forde, Shamus Hurley-Langton, Ciaran Frawley (two) and Caolin Blade.

Players stood in silence, with some visibly emotional, as La Rochelle and the Johannesburg-based Lions paid tribute to South African lock Hyron Andrews before Saturday's Champions Cup clash. The 31-year-old died in France on Friday, on the eve of the fixture.

Sports.title: Kiltie double helps Kilmarnock beat fellow-strugglers Motherwell
Sports.content:
Greg Kiltie scored twice to lift Kilmarnock off the bottom of the Scottish Premiership with a 3-2 victory over Motherwell.

Kiltie struck first and last as Neil McCann's side inflicted a fifth consecutive defeat on the Steelmen, who join Killie in the bottom three, one point off bottom-placed Hibernian.

Motherwell had a dominant spell after recovering from Kiltie's second-minute opener and goals from Alex Lowry and Seb Palmer-Houlden turned the game on its head.

But Tyreece John-Jules soon equalised and Motherwell were cut open before Kiltie knocked home a 69th-minute winner.

Given their run, Motherwell fans would have feared the worst when their team gifted Kilmarnock a goal with little over 60 seconds on the clock.

Goalkeeper Alex Paulsen misplaced a short pass into central midfield and Kiltie ultimately converted after some desperate defending.

Worse almost followed several moments later when Well centre-back Martin Moorman lost possession midway inside his own half, but Joe Hugill dragged his shot wide.

But the visitors levelled in the 17th minute when Lukas Fadinger sent Emmanual Longelo down the left wing. Calum Ferrie made a great stop after Palmer-Houlden got on the end of the left-back's low cross but Lowry kept his composure to fire the rebound into the bottom corner.

Motherwell took control as Killie struggled to keep possession inside their own half. Maswanshise hit the post from 25 yards and scuffed a decent chance wide, and Ibrahim Said forced a good save from Ferrie.

Neil McCann brought on Jamie Brandon for on-loan Hearts right-back MJ Kamson-Kamara in the 33rd minute in a bid to deal with the twin threat of Longelo and Said. He was forced into another change two minutes later when the injured Bailey Rice went off for Aaron Tshibola.

The hosts improved towards the end of the half. Paulsen got down well to stop a John-Jules drive after Motherwell failed to deal with a long ball and the unmarked Tom Lowery volleyed well over.

Killie were grateful for a VAR intervention after referee Calum Scott sent George Stanger off for a high boot on Lowry. The punishment was downgraded to a yellow card after a trip to the monitor.

Motherwell were soon in front in the 56th minute after a low cross from Said. Palmer-Houlden was denied at close range by Ferrie but the ball ricocheted in off the centre-forward.

The visitors' lead only lasted two minutes. Two Motherwell defenders were barged off the ball as Brandon headed the ball back into the box after a half-cleared corner and John-Jules produced an emphatic finish.

Brandon delivered another assist when his crossfield pass played in Kiltie, who again slotted into the far corner.

Paulsen made saves from substitute Ieuan Owen and Hugill to keep Motherwell in it.

Alfred Johansson's side struggled to create chances though, and Ferrie saved from Johnny Koutroumbis deep in stoppage time when the substitute found himself in a good position.

Johansson bemoans 'low-level' defending

Motherwell manager Alfred Johansson:

"I'm very, very disappointed and frustrated with how we end this game. It's extremely difficult to accept the fact that we lost this game.

"Obviously we make it difficult for ourselves right at the start as well, but that can happen in football, you make a mistake and get punished in that way.

"But we reacted fantastically and the rest of the first half is very, very good. We're pressing together, we're aggressive, we catch them on the break, we create chances.

"They start going long into the strikers with one touch and we just don't defend those long balls well enough.

"I don't think we're winning enough second balls and also, prior to the second goal, for instance, we have the ball under control, but we give it away way too easy.

"We have chances to score more than two goals but we can't rely on scoring three goals away from home. We need to be much more solid. It's just way too low a level, how we defend."

McCann: We showed spirit and character

Kilmarnock boss Neil McCann:

"I talk about the spirit that I've got in that dressing room now.

"I talk about the character, with a group of boys that have taken a wee bit of time to come together, and I thought second half we were absolutely brilliant.

"We had a couple of wee things that we tinkered with, in terms of where we wanted to get at Motherwell.

But, tactics aside, that was just about them saying, 'no, we're going to get ourselves back in that game, and we look to go and try and win it'."

Don Revie’s side, freshly promoted, were on course for the Double. Only problem was, so were Matt Busby’s men. The pair were drawn in the semi-final of the FA Cup, and spent 90 minutes at Hillsborough kicking seven colours out of each other, Jack Charlton, Billy Bremner, Nobby Stiles, Denis Law and Paddy Crerand enjoying themselves like the proverbial pigs. Good luck if you found yourself in the middle of that. Brouhahas broke out on the terraces as well, and did so again four days later during the replay at the City Ground. The on-field behaviour was much improved, though. According to Big Jack, Manchester United put on a performance as stylish and dangerous as they ever were under Busby, but Leeds somehow held on, wrested the ascendency, and nicked it in the last minute, Bremner twisting in mid-air to steer home an outrageous curling header. Bremner was missing 18 days later when Manchester United came to Elland Road in the league. Had they won, Leeds would have gone five clear at the top with four games left. They went into the game as favourites, Busby’s side having failed to find the net against Leeds in both Cup games and the earlier league match at Old Trafford, which the visitors won 1-0. That particular lean spell ended after 14 minutes – or 284, if you like – when John Connelly drove home. Leeds failed to respond, despite the best efforts of the newly crowned Football Writers’ player of the year, Bobby Collins, and went down again in their next Bremner-less match, a 3-0 hosing at Sheffield Wednesday. Busby’s third great side won their first title; Revie’s team, not quite ready yet, lost the Cup final as well.
