Sports.title: “The Towering Inferno” Fundora Stops Hadribeaj in Final Round
Sports.content:
WBC super welterweight champion Sebastian “The Towering Inferno” Fundora stopped Ermal “The Albanian Sniper” Hadribeaj with one second remaining in the twelfth and final round of an action-packed but often sloppy fight at the Cosmopolitan of Las Vegas, Nevada.

Promoters Tom Brown of TGB Promotions and Sampson Lewkowicz of Sampson Boxing presented the card Saturday on DAZN and TNT.

In the main event, southpaw Fundora, 25-1-1 (17 KOs), of Coachella, California, stopped fellow southpaw Hadribeaj, 23-1-1 (8 KOs), of Tirana, Albania, and Miami Beach, Florida, at 2:59 of the final round.

In the second round, Fundora used his considerable height advantage to hurt Hadribeaj early. The challenger fought back and had Fundora in trouble near the end of the round. In the third, referee Thomas Taylor deducted a point from Hadribeaj for excessive holding.

There was nonstop action from the fourth through the tenth as Hadribeaj forced his way inside and Fundora answered with short punches. The challenger made it competitive, although Fundora held an overall edge and increasingly found success with his body attack.

In the eleventh round, Taylor deducted another point from Hadribeaj for holding. Despite his height disadvantage, the challenger continued trying to force the fight at close range.

In the closing seconds of the twelfth, Fundora dropped Hadribeaj with a left hand. Hadribeaj beat the count but was in no condition to continue, prompting Taylor to wave it off with one second remaining.

In the co-main event, former WBA super middleweight champion Armando “Toro” Resendiz, 17-3 (11 KOs), of Guayabitos, Mexico, defeated Koen Mazoudier, 16-5-1 (6 KOs), of Blacktown, New South Wales, Australia, by unanimous decision over ten action-packed rounds.

Resendiz rocked Mazoudier with a right hand to the chin in the final seconds of the fourth round, knocking him off balance. From the sixth through the ninth, Mazoudier pressed the action and fought his way back into the contest, giving the crowd plenty to cheer about while Resendiz continued landing the heavier punches.

In the final minute of the tenth, Resendiz hurt Mazoudier with a flurry of unanswered shots. The Australian survived to hear the final bell.

The scores were 98-92 and 97-93 twice. Harvey Dock was the referee.

In an eight-round super middleweight bout, Jaime Osuna, 12-0 (5 KOs), of Guerrero Negro, Baja California Sur, Mexico, won a majority decision over Cristian Cangelosi, 13-1-1 (5 KOs), of Palermo, Italy, and Brooklyn, New York.

Osuna suffered a cut over his right eye from a left hook in the third round, which Cangelosi took with his cleaner work.

In the fifth, Osuna rocked Cangelosi early as the fight developed into a slugfest. Cangelosi answered in the seventh, catching Osuna with a right hand to the chin in the closing seconds.

Both had their moments in the eighth and final round, fighting hard with the result still in doubt.

Two judges scored it 77-75 for Osuna, while the third had it even at 76-76. Robert Hoyle was the referee.

Super middleweight Marco “El Tiburon” Romero, 16-0 (14 KOs), of Olathe, Kansas, stopped Matias Ferreira, 8-4 (3 KOs), of Rosario, Uruguay, at 1:54 of the first round of their scheduled eight-round bout.

Ferreira landed a left hook midway through the opening round, but Romero countered with a right hand to the chin that dropped him onto the seat of his trunks. Referee Tony Weeks stopped the contest following the knockdown.

Jimmy Lennon Jr. served as the ring announcer.

The scheduled bout between Brandon Figueroa and Tomoki Kameda was canceled after Figueroa became ill following his weight cut. Figueroa was also stripped of his WBA featherweight title after failing to make the division limit.

Sports.title: Ennis vs. Kelly Winner Targeted By Sebastian Fundora
Sports.content:
Sebastian Fundora wants the Jaron Ennis–Josh Kelly winner next, but a potential Ennis fight comes with a financial obstacle: promoter Sampson Lewkowicz’s demand for a 50-50 purse split.

Fundora called for undisputed after stopping Ermal Hadribeaj with one second remaining in the 12th round. The WBC junior middleweight champion sounded ready to pursue the other belts, although agreeing on an opponent is only part of getting a unification made.

“Absolutely, let’s go for undisputed,” Fundora told DAZN when asked about facing the Ennis–Kelly winner. “We will break them down like we broke this guy, like the guy before that, before that, and before. We’ll keep breaking these guys down.”

Fundora (25-1-1, 17 KOs) had just completed his fourth successful title defense, wearing down Hadribeaj with short punches and sustained body work before dropping him with a left hand at 2:59 of the final round.

That performance supported his description of breaking opponents down. Hadribeaj made the early rounds competitive by crowding Fundora, but the champion gradually took over through his greater activity inside.

Getting Ennis into the ring could require a different kind of patience. Lewkowicz has called for an equal split for Fundora against Ennis, leaving the financial terms as something the camps would have to resolve if Ennis beats Kelly.

There is no agreement established by Fundora’s post-fight comments, nor do they show that Ennis has accepted or rejected those terms. The potential obstacle is whether an equal split becomes a firm condition or a starting position in negotiations.

Fundora has made his preference clear. If Ennis wins, the next question will be whether the promoters can find a price both sides accept and turn that undisputed ambition into a scheduled fight.

Tonight’s showing only hurts Fundora’s negotiating position. Needing until the final second of the twelfth round to finish a gritty but limited challenger like Hadribeaj showed the exact vulnerabilities that have always followed Fundora. He surrenders his 6’6″ frame, stays glued in the pocket, eats clean shots on the inside, and relies strictly on outlasting foes in a war of attrition.

Sports.title: Sebastian Fundora Stops Ermal Hadribeaj With One Second Left
Sports.content:
Sebastian Fundora stopped Ermal Hadribeaj with one second remaining in the 12th round, finishing a physically taxing fight with a left hand after gradually wearing down the challenger with body punches and a higher work rate.

The victory gave Fundora (25-1-1, 17 KOs) his fourth successful defense of the WBC junior middleweight title on Saturday night at The Chelsea at the Cosmopolitan of Las Vegas. Hadribeaj (23-1-1, 8 KOs) suffered his first defeat after making the champion work considerably harder than his heavy favorite status suggested.

Hadribeaj had little interest in remaining at the end of Fundora’s punches. The challenger stayed low, moved inside and landed hard shots, forcing the taller champion into a fight where his height and reach offered fewer benefits.

A long left hand buzzed Hadribeaj in the second round, but he recovered quickly and returned to pressing the action. Referee Thomas Taylor deducted a point for holding in the third, adding an early cost to the challenger’s attempts to crowd and smother Fundora.

The inside fighting remained competitive through the middle rounds. Hadribeaj landed some of the heavier individual punches, while Fundora answered with more frequent short shots and uppercuts.

Fundora’s body attack became increasingly effective as the fight progressed. Rather than consistently creating distance, he found room to punch where Hadribeaj wanted to fight, digging downstairs and keeping his hands moving.

That made the challenger’s approach harder to sustain. Getting close no longer prevented Fundora from scoring, and Hadribeaj increasingly held as the champion continued working.

Taylor took another point from Hadribeaj in the 11th. By then, Fundora was producing the cleaner, more consistent offense, leaving the challenger needing a dramatic finish.

The decisive punch came from the champion instead. Fundora maintained his pressure in the final round before a left hand dropped Hadribeaj and ended the fight at 2:59.

Sports.title: Sebastian Fundora vs Ermal Hadribeaj Live Results and Fight Updates
Sports.content:
Super middleweight Armando Resendiz (17-3, 11 KOs) defeated Koen Mazoudier (16-5-1, 6 KOs) by a 10-round unanimous decision in a hard-fought fight. The judges scored it 98-92, 97-93 and 97-93, giving Resendiz a wider victory than the competitive action suggested.

Mazoudier kept coming forward and throwing, making Resendiz work at close range and enjoying success through the middle rounds. Resendiz answered with the heavier punches, hurting the Australian with right hands and left hooks as the two traded throughout.

A sustained attack in the final round left Mazoudier reeling and close to being stopped, but he survived and continued firing back until the bell. Resendiz earned his first victory since losing to Jaime Munguia, while Mazoudier made him fight for it in his U.S. debut.

Marco Romero (16-0, 14 KOs) stopped Braulio Matias Ferreira (8-4, 3 KOs) in the first round of their scheduled eight-round super middleweight fight. The 20-year-old Romero immediately pressed the attack, digging to the body and landing right hands upstairs at close range.

A right hand and left hook to the body helped set up a sweeping right to the chin that dropped Ferreira hard into the ropes. Ferreira beat the count, but he was in no condition to continue, prompting the referee to stop the fight. Romero gave the veteran little chance to settle, keeping him under attack throughout the brief contest. It was the Kansas prospect’s third consecutive first-round stoppage.

Super middleweight Jaime Enrique Osuna Diaz (12-0, 5 KOs) kept his unbeaten record with an eight-round majority decision over Cristian Cangelosi (13-1-1, 5 KOs). The judges scored the competitive bout 77-75, 77-75 and 76-76 on the Sebastian Fundora–Ermal Hadribeaj undercard.

Osuna applied pressure from the start, using his activity and body punching to make Cangelosi work. His best round came in the fifth, when he hurt Cangelosi twice with straight right hands but crowded his own punches while trying to finish.

Cangelosi fought back and had a strong seventh round, landing a big shot to keep the outcome in doubt heading into the eighth. Neither fighter scored a knockdown, with Osuna’s pressure and cleaner work in key stretches earning him the narrow victory.

Sports.title: Terence Crawford Underestimates Christian Mbilli’s Threat To Canelo
Sports.content:
Terence Crawford calls Christian Mbilli “tailor-made” for Canelo Alvarez, but that description overlooks what sustained pressure could do to a fighter who increasingly needs breaks between attacks.

Mbilli gives opponents opportunities to hit him. He also keeps punching after they land. Canelo could find the uppercuts and hooks he wants and still struggle if those shots don’t slow the younger fighter down.

“He can’t do nothing but press Canelo,” Crawford told TNT Sports. “I don’t see him beating Canelo in a boxing match. I think his best success is letting his hands go, roughing Canelo up and making it a dogfight.”

That approach is precisely what makes Mbilli dangerous. Canelo’s output has dropped during stretches of recent fights, leaving him throwing isolated power shots while opponents have opportunities to collect points through activity. Against Mbilli, taking a breather could mean absorbing another combination.

Crawford also has something to gain from Canelo winning. It protects the value of his victory over the Mexican star last year and preserves whatever possibility remains of a rematch. A one-sided Mbilli win would invite an uncomfortable question about how much Canelo had left when Crawford beat him.

Calling an opponent tailor-made makes sense if the fighter in question possesses the legs, reflexes, and gas tank to punish mistakes all night. The current Alvarez operates in short spurts. He throws one or two eye-catching power counters, tucks into a high guard, and waits. That approach works fine against timid opposition, but it is a terrible blueprint against someone with an engine like Mbilli.

Mbilli gets hit, but he thrives inside the pocket and throws punches in bunches. In the past, Canelo made aggressive brawlers pay with devastating counters that made them hesitate. Now, he lacks the one-punch erase button at 168 pounds to stop a relentless tank in his tracks. If Canelo lands a crisp left hook and Mbilli shakes his head, walks forward, and fires six shots in return, Alvarez gets trapped working when he desperately needs to catch his breath.

If anything, the script has flipped. Canelo is the one who looks tailor-made for high-output, durable fighters who refuse to stand at mid-range admiring his defensive slips. Crawford is banking on nostalgia, but twelve rounds against a live motor like Mbilli exposes stamina issues that reputation alone cannot fix.

Shawn Porter expects Canelo to stop Mbilli with an uppercut or left hooks. Tim Bradley also sees a possible late stoppage. Yet Canelo hasn’t stopped an opponent since Caleb Plant in November 2021. Those predictions require more than identifying punches Mbilli is available for.

Bradley supplied the strongest qualification himself.

“If Canelo punches him and can’t hurt him and can’t get his respect, Mbilli is in the fight,” he said.

That is the risk. Canelo can land the cleaner punches without controlling the pace. If Mbilli walks through a counter and immediately starts punching again, Canelo has to defend and work before he is ready. The openings will be there. Whether Canelo still has the stamina to keep exploiting them is another question.

Sports.title: Eddie Hearn Backs Teremoana To Beat Bakhodir Jalolov
Sports.content:
Eddie Hearn is talking up a fight that would finally give Teremoana Teremoana a serious professional test, backing his unbeaten heavyweight to beat Bakhodir Jalolov despite two amateur defeats against the Uzbek southpaw.

After Jalolov’s decision win over Solomon Dacres on Saturday’s Daniel Dubois–Fabio Wardley rematch card, Hearn posted a blunt verdict on his Instagram story:

“@TEREMOANA_REP WOULD EAT UP JALOLOV”

That is a bold claim about a fighter who has already beaten Teremoana at the 2023 World Championships and the 2024 Paris Olympics. Jalolov won their Olympic quarterfinal 5–0 before going on to collect his second gold medal.

Hearn may have seen something against Dacres that makes him confident. Jalolov scored a knockdown but went the distance, giving his critics another reason to question whether his professional career will match his amateur success.

However, Dacres lasting the distance does not tell us that Teremoana would walk through Jalolov. The Australian would still have to get past the 6-foot-7 southpaw’s long punches and land without being caught coming forward. He has already experienced how difficult that can be over three rounds.

At 28, Teremoana needs opponents who can ask those questions. His 12–0 record, with every win inside the distance, looks impressive on paper, but his professional opposition has offered little evidence of how he handles someone with Jalolov’s skills.

There is some context to his career’s slow progress. Teremoana returned to amateur boxing after winning his first four professional fights to pursue an Olympic place. He has not spent the entire period since turning professional working toward a world title.

Still, another quick knockout against an overmatched opponent would tell us less than a fight with Jalolov. What happens if Teremoana’s power cannot get him out of trouble? Can he keep applying pressure when he has to work through jabs and straight lefts to get close?

Hearn’s post does not mean a deal is coming. But he has supplied a good reason to pursue one. If he believes Teremoana would “eat up” Jalolov, making the fight would give his heavyweight the chance to prove it.

Claiming Teremoana would eat him up ignores history. Teremoana could not solve Jalolov over three rounds in Tashkent, and he could not solve him over three rounds in Paris. Jalolov swept him five to zero at the Olympics by maintaining range, switching off the back foot, and drilling him with straight lefts every time the Australian lunged.

Adding extra rounds does not magically fix poor footwork or defensive leaks. If Teremoana charges in recklessly, he walks straight into a 6’7″ sniper who rarely misses incoming targets.

Hearn finds himself backed into a corner regarding matchmaking. Teremoana is 28. The six-year gap since his pro debut was eaten up by the detour back to the unpaid ranks for Paris, leaving him with an empty 12-0 record against club fighters and regional journeymen. Hearn cannot keep serving up this type of opposition on DAZN undercards without turning the Australian into an expensive prospect who never generates revenue.

Putting Teremoana in with Jalolov is high risk with no margin for error. A third loss to the exact same rival destroys Teremoana’s commercial momentum before it even starts. Hearn needs to decide whether he is testing a genuine contender or sacrificing a raw asset against a stylistic nightmare just to get attention on social media.

Sports.title: Filip Hrgovic Promises Stoppage In Daniel Dubois Rematch
Sports.content:
Filip Hrgovic believes Daniel Dubois will feel like “slow motion” after Moses Itauma, and wants a March rematch following their in-ring face-off tonight. Dubois’s second-round demolition of Fabio Wardley did little to impress the Croatian, who questioned whether Wardley had recovered from their first fight.

“I was not impressed,” Hrgovic said afterward. “Something wasn’t right, and it was an easy job for Daniel. I want to fight him.”

Hrgovic argued that Dubois should be available in March because he had escaped the short fight without injuries. That remains his proposed date, with no agreement announced.

The more interesting part is what Hrgovic believes his win over Itauma has done for him. Having dealt with the younger heavyweight’s speed, he expects more time to see Dubois’s punches coming.

“I think after Moses, fighting Daniel will be like slow motion, man.”

Hrgovic acknowledged that Dubois is strong, has a good jab, and would be a tough opponent. His plan is to take away that jab and make Dubois retreat.

“I will defend his jab,” Hrgovic said. “I will push him to go backwards, not allow him to go forward. I will control him with the jab, move my head, block his jab.”

That requires more than getting accustomed to a faster opponent. Hrgovic still has to move his head consistently when Dubois starts throwing, particularly while stepping forward himself. Trying to force Dubois backward could leave him walking onto the very jab he wants to neutralize.

Hrgovic also claimed he was sick and injured during their first fight, attributing his cuts to Dubois’s head. He expects a different finish next time.

“I think I will destroy him next fight.”

If Hrgovic turns it into a phone-booth dogfight, he’s got a chance to defeat Dubois. History shows that when Dubois gets dragged into uncomfortable, chaotic trenches where he takes clubbing shots, his self-belief wavers.

Sports.title: Dubois Knocks Out Wardley In Two Rounds
Sports.content:
Daniel Dubois retained his WBO heavyweight title with a second-round stoppage of Fabio Wardley on Saturday at the O2 Arena in London. Frank Warren’s Queensberry Promotions presented the rematch on DAZN PPV.

Dubois (24-3, 23 KOs), of Greenwich, stopped Wardley (20-2-1, 19 KOs), of Ipswich, at 2:21 of the second round after the challenger’s corner threw in the towel.

Dubois hurt Wardley almost immediately, landing a right hand to the chin that sent him down for a count from referee Steve Gray. Wardley got up but struggled to recover as Dubois continued landing heavy punches. The challenger was hurt again near the end of a punishing opening round.

In the second, Dubois maintained control and gave Wardley little opportunity to fight his way back into the contest. With Wardley taking punches and unable to defend himself effectively, his corner threw in the towel, and Gray halted the fight.

Louie O’Doherty and Michael Gomez Jr. Fight To Draw

British and Commonwealth lightweight champion Louie O’Doherty (12-0-1, 3 KOs), of Halstead, retained his titles after a twelve-round majority draw against Manchester’s Michael Gomez Jr. (23-2-1, 8 KOs).

Gomez controlled the first four rounds and continued scoring effectively in the fifth and sixth, although O’Doherty began making the fight more competitive. The champion had his best spell in the seventh and eighth, using his work rate to take both rounds.

O’Doherty was bleeding from his nose and mouth during a close ninth round in which Gomez landed well. Referee Lee Every warned Gomez for a low blow in the tenth, while O’Doherty’s activity gave him an argument for taking the round.

The pace remained high in the eleventh, with O’Doherty again doing enough to make it close. Gomez began celebrating midway through the final round and repeated the gesture in the closing seconds, allowing O’Doherty to outwork him during an important finish.

One judge scored the fight 115-114 for Gomez, while the other two returned cards of 114-114.

Bakhodir Jalolov Outpoints Solomon Dacres

Two-time Olympic gold medalist Bakhodir Jalolov (18-0, 15 KOs), of Uzbekistan, defeated Solomon Dacres (10-2, 3 KOs), of Warley, by a ten-round unanimous decision.

The southpaw scored the fight’s only knockdown in the fifth round, catching Dacres on the chin with a straight left. Dacres beat the count and completed the distance, but Jalolov remained in control.

The scores were 99-91 and 99-90 twice.

Nelson Birchall Stops Levi Giles

Morecambe’s Nelson Birchall (13-0, 10 KOs) stopped Levi Giles (17-4-1, 4 KOs), of Grimsby, at 0:51 of the seventh round of their scheduled ten-round contest.

Birchall dropped Giles with a body shot in the fifth round. Another body shot put Giles down in the sixth, and a third knockdown in the seventh brought the stoppage from referee Sean McAvoy.

Tony Curtis Wins Commonwealth International Title

London’s Tony Curtis (15-1, 4 KOs) stopped Kerim Agius at 2:57 of the fourth round to win the vacant Commonwealth International super flyweight title.

Curtis scored knockdowns in the second and fourth rounds before referee Sean McAvoy ended the scheduled eight-round contest.

Manny Safari Stops Jake Pollard

Manny Safari (1-0, 1 KO), of Bracknell, won his professional debut by stopping Bradford’s Jake Pollard in the fifth round of their scheduled six-round bout.

Safari scored a first-round knockdown and secured the finish at 2:15 of round five, with referee Amy Pu calling a halt.

Fawas Aborode Finishes Rashid Omar

Fawas Aborode (3-0, 3 KOs), based in Aberdeen, stopped Cardiff southpaw Rashid Omar in the fourth round of their scheduled six-round lightweight contest.

Aborode put Omar down in the fourth, prompting referee Sean McAvoy to halt the bout at 1:58.

Leighton Birchall Takes Shutout Decision

Morecambe featherweight Leighton Birchall (6-0, 3 KOs) defeated Mexico’s Alejandro Morales Chazaro (9-10-2, 5 KOs) over six rounds.

Referee Sean McAvoy scored every round for Birchall, returning a 60-54 card.

Adam Olaniyan Stops Dan Garber

Tallaght heavyweight Adam Olaniyan (5-0, 5 KOs) stopped Bradford’s Dan Garber (14-10, 2 KOs) at 1:15 of the second round of their scheduled four-round bout.

Olaniyan dropped Garber in the second, prompting the veteran’s corner to throw in the towel. Referee Amy Pu kicked it aside and allowed the fight to continue after Garber rose.

A second knockdown followed, with another towel coming from Garber’s corner. Pu then stopped the contest.

Aaron Noriega Stops Leonardo Baez

California’s Aaron Noriega stopped Leonardo Baez at 1:41 of the fourth and final round of their super featherweight bout.

Noriega scored two knockdowns in the fourth before referee Amy Pu halted the fight.

Zayn Ahmed Stops Kasey Bradnum

Slough southpaw Zayn Ahmed (4-0, 2 KOs) stopped Kasey Bradnum (1-51), of Harwich, at 2:49 of the second round of their scheduled four-round contest.

Ahmed scored two knockdowns during the bout before referee Amy Pu called a halt.

Issiah Hamilton-Allen Wins Every Round

Ipswich middleweight Issiah Hamilton-Allen (4-0) defeated Jensen Irving (6-41-2, 1 KO), of Swindon, by a four-round points decision.

Referee Sean McAvoy scored the contest 40-36.

Thomas Treiber served as ring announcer.

Ghana News.title: All 46 NDC aspirants pass vetting ahead of Bono East regional elections
Ghana News.content:
All 46 aspirants seeking various leadership positions in the National Democratic Congress (NDC) Bono East Regional executive elections have successfully passed vetting, clearing the way for the party’s regional polls scheduled for November this year.

The aspirants, who had earlier submitted their nominations online, completed the in-person filing and vetting process on Wednesday. The exercise was overseen by the Vetting Committee, chaired by Nuru Hamidan, who also serves as Deputy Chief Executive Officer of STC.

No one disqualified

Speaking to Joy News after the exercise, Mr Hamidan said the process had been smooth and transparent, with all aspirants deemed qualified to contest.

“The nomination exercise was peaceful. All 46 aspirants recorded on the committee’s dashboard completed the in-person filing process and went through the vetting successfully. They were deemed qualified, and no one was disqualified,” Mr Hamidan said.

He added that the committee had encountered no challenges during the exercise and expressed hope that the aspirants would comply with the party’s electoral guidelines to ensure a peaceful election in November.

“I hope that the aspirants will comply with the party’s electoral guidelines to ensure the election is peaceful,” he said.

Aspirants express confidence

With vetting complete, the aspirants are turning their attention to the campaign trail. One of the key contenders is the incumbent Regional Treasurer, Gapson Raphael Kofi, who is seeking to become Regional Secretary.

Mr Kofi expressed confidence in his chances of winning, citing his track record of integrity and truthfulness.

“My track record as someone with integrity and truthfulness puts me in a strong position to be elected as the party’s Regional Secretary,” he said.

Outgoing secretary praises party’s decision

The outgoing Regional Secretary, Adaebsa Isaac, who currently serves as Chief Executive Officer of the GRATIS Foundation, is not seeking re-election.

He commended the party’s decision to exempt current executives occupying government positions from contesting.

According to him, the move would create opportunities to groom new leaders and allow party members who are not in government to dedicate more time to party activities.

“Those occupying government positions currently are too busy to do the party’s work, and as a result, the party structure is getting weak,” Mr Isaac said.

“There’s a need to groom others and pave the way for people who are not in government and have time to work for the party.”

Call for clean campaigns

The incumbent Regional Communications Officer, Sulemana Mohammed Mustapha, has urged delegates to ensure that the campaign is free from insults and personal attacks.

He called on delegates to vote against aspirants who engage in such behaviour.

“There’s a need for the delegates to stage clean campaigns devoid of insults. I urge delegates to punish such individuals by voting against them on election day,” Mr Mustapha said.

He added that his communication experience and expertise were what the party needed to communicate the government’s policies effectively and retain power in 2028.

What’s next?

The NDC Bono East Regional executive elections will be held in Techiman in November this year.

With all 46 aspirants cleared to contest, the party is preparing for an internal election that will shape its regional leadership ahead of the next general election.

Ghana News.title: Assisi Girls SHS launches 70th anniversary as Joyce Bawah Mogtari, stakeholders champion girl-child education
Ghana News.content:
Hundreds of alumnae, traditional authorities, educators, and students converged on the campus of St. Francis of Assisi Girls’ Senior High School in Jirapa on Saturday, October 17, to mark the institution’s 67th birthday, launch its upcoming 70th anniversary celebrations, and hold its annual Speech and Prize Giving Day.

The Franciscan Old Girls Association (FOGA) homecoming drew old students from across Ghana and Nigeria, celebrating decades of educational excellence while spotlighting urgent infrastructural bottlenecks facing the Catholic girls' institution.

The multi-event celebration, held under the theme "67 Years of Nurturing Leaders and Inspiring Excellence: Time to Retrace Our Steps", served as both a celebration of institutional milestones and an appeal to address systemic overcrowding, teacher shortages, and resource deficits.

Delivering the keynote address as Special Guest of Honour, Special Aide and Presidential Adviser to the President of Ghana, Joyce Bawah Mogtari, urged students to recognise the immense potential of girls’ education and draw inspiration from groundbreaking women in leadership.

Reflecting on her own time as a student on the Jirapa campus, Mogtari recounted how transferring to the school helped rebuild her academic path and formed the bedrock of her legal and political career.

"I return to this great school not merely as your Special Guest of Honour, but as a proud daughter of this institution. I mean, who would have imagined all those years ago that one day, I, Joyce Bawah, would return here as a senior lawyer with expertise in maritime law, founder of a law firm, an entrepreneur, and Senior Presidential Adviser and Special Aide to the President of the Republic of Ghana?" she said.

Mogtari conveyed warm felicitations from President John Dramani Mahama, emphasising his administration's commitment to advancing educational access for young women.

Pointing to national and global strides in female representation, she cited Vice President Professor Naana Jane Opoku-Agyemang as living proof that glass ceilings can be shattered.

"For the first time since independence, and nearly 70 years after Ghana’s independence, we now have a female Vice President: Her Excellency Professor Naana Jane Opoku-Agyemang. Her story tells every girl in Ghana that no ambition is too great simply because she is female. If Ghana can have its first female Vice President, then surely, the curtain draws closer to us electing our first female President," she stressed.

Addressing the gathering on the state of the school, the Headmistress of St. Francis of Assisi Girls SHS, Anastasia Kaarawo, detailed the school’s academic achievements alongside severe infrastructural distress.

Kaarawo highlighted that the institution, which began in September 1959 with just 12 girls and two teachers, has grown into a Category A institution with an active student population of 1,341. She reported an 88% overall pass rate in the 2025 WASSCE, with candidates currently awaiting the results of the 510 candidates who sat the 2026 examination.

However, the headmistress lamented that exponential enrolment growth has overwhelmed existing facilities.

"If you go to the dormitories, it is overcrowded. Every available space, like the box rooms and laundries, has been converted into dormitories. In the classrooms right now, the first years who are reporting do not have furniture to sit on. They are sitting on benches, and the benches are not even enough for them," Kaarawo revealed.

She listed critical shortfalls including deficits in toilet facilities, staff accommodation, science and home economics practical equipment, textbooks for the new curriculum, and teacher shortages in Chemistry, Physics, Biology, and Integrated Science. Kaarawo also shared a harrowing logistical challenge, recounting an incident where a school pickup conveying the body of a deceased security personnel caught fire in the Jirapa market square, forcing authorities to transfer the remains into an aboboyaa (motorized tricycle).

She appealed to government, FOGA, and corporate bodies to assist in roofing and completing an ongoing chapel project, as well as providing logistical and classroom support.

Reinforcing the school administration’s call, Former National President of FOGA, Fati Bodua Seidu—who delivered an address on behalf of current FOGA National President, Amina Abugdanpoka Kaguah—emphasized that alumnae affection for their alma mater must manifest in practical intervention.

"All but one of our dormitories were built decades ago, but today accommodate almost three times the number of students they were originally intended to house. Some of our girls have had to sleep on the floor, on damaged or inadequate mattresses, and in spaces crowded between old bed frames. That should concern all of us here. And this is why FOGA has decided that our affection for this school cannot exist only in memories; it must translate into action," Seidu stated.

Seidu charged the students to complement the investments made by parents and teachers with personal discipline and academic rigor.

"A new dormitory alone will not make you successful. A new classroom will not study for you. A comfortable bed cannot write your examinations. Confidence is not arrogance; ambition is not something for which a woman should apologize; excellence is not reserved for somebody else," she told the student body.

Chairing the event, the Paramount Chief of the Jirapa Traditional Area, Naa Dinaa Donglabong Ganaa III, commended the founding Franciscan Missionaries of Mary (FMM) and traditional ancestors for establishing the premier girls' secondary school in northern Ghana.

Naa Ganaa III challenged FOGA and development partners to evolve from sporadic reunion gatherings into an active institutional development network providing structured scholarships, internships, and mentorship.

"Retracing our steps must not mean walking backwards. It means returning to our roots so that we can move forward with a clearer sense of purpose. FOGA must be more than a name, a membership list, or an organization that gathers only for anniversaries and homecomings. It must become a living network of opportunity," the Paramount Chief stated.

Awards were presented to outstanding students and staff across various disciplines, with the Managing Director of MyTURN Ltd and Lesken Enterprise presenting awards of tablets and, on behalf of the Dr. Kenneth Aneweneh Foundation, sponsored prizes for 15 students, cash rewards for awardees, and hosting a celebratory homecoming dinner.

Ghana News.title: ECOWAS, AES agree to build cooperation framework at Dakar meeting, after 2025 split
Ghana News.content:
The Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) and the Alliance of Sahel States (AES) have agreed on ground rules for life after the split.

At a foundational meeting of Ministers in Dakar, Senegal, the two blocs resolved to build a cooperation framework to govern diplomatic relations, economic ties, development and other mutual priority areas.

Thematic working groups will now hold technical consultations, with expert advice shaping the final framework. Both sides say the interests of their citizens should remain paramount.

Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger, all under military-led governments, announced their withdrawal from ECOWAS in January 2024, accusing the bloc of being influenced by foreign powers and failing to support their fight against terrorism.

The three had already formed the AES confederation.

Their exit took effect in January 2025, leaving ECOWAS without three of its fifteen members and raising questions over trade, free movement and regional security.

Following the split, ECOWAS shifted its strategy from forcing the AES to return to the bloc to finding practical ways to coexist and to protect travel, trade and security for millions of citizens.

The Dakar dialogue led by ECOWAS Council of Ministers chair, Sheikh Niang, and the AES steering committee chair, Karamoko Jean-Marie Traore, marked the first time both sides sat formally since the January 2025 split.

The agreement or framework aims to largely preserve visa-free movement and the flow of goods.

Organised by JoyNews and sponsored by Republic Bank, the event brings together businesses and other stakeholders in Ghana’s housing sector, connecting consumers with products, services and financing options.

This year’s edition in Ho forms part of efforts to extend the fair beyond Accra and other major urban centres, bringing housing-related products and services closer to prospective buyers in the Volta Region and surrounding areas.

The fair will close at 8 p.m. today, giving interested patrons a final opportunity to visit the Ho Sports Stadium and take advantage of the available offers.

Ghana News.title: Three men jailed for 158 years each for murdering Australian and US surfers in Mexico
Ghana News.content:
A Mexican judge has sentenced three men convicted of murdering Australian brothers Jake and Callum Robinson and their US friend Carter Rhoad to 158 years and nine months in jail each.

The Robinsons and Rhoad were killed in an apparent botched robbery of their truck on a secluded beach in Baja California in 2024 while they were on a surfing trip, the court heard during the trial.

The murders sent shockwaves around the world, particularly in Australia, as the area is usually safe from the violence seen in other parts of Mexico.

The guilty verdict was handed down last week. Debra Robinson, the brothers' mother, told the courtroom that her sons' murders had taken "the future we had imagined with them".

The convicted killers' full names were not given for legal reasons, meaning they were only identified as Jesús Gerardo, Irineo Francisco and Ángel Jesús.

In November last year, the girlfriend of the alleged ringleader, Jesús Gerardo (alias "El Kekas"), was sentenced in a separate trial to 20 years in prison. She had admitted to involvement in the robbery.

The court heard that the bodies of the victims were found dumped down a well with gunshot wounds to their heads.

At the time, the murders shocked locals and tourists in the beach town of Ensenada who were disturbed at the apparent ease and sheer pointlessness of the killings.

Ensenada has a reputation as a welcoming spot for surfers, but the chilling murders revealed how commonplace such extreme violence remains in Mexico.

The only explanation the authorities were able to give was that the surfers - all in their early 30s - had ultimately been murdered for being in the wrong place at the wrong time.

Their killings happened barely 36 hours after they crossed into Mexico from the US. Their bodies, however, were not found for another week, when their families were able to identify them.

Local surfers also called for greater security for residents and visiting tourists, citing other recent examples of violence in the state. Tourism is a key part of the regional economy in Baja California.

Ghana News.title: Pope discharged from hospital days after lung cancer surgery
Ghana News.content:
Pope Leo XIV has been discharged from Rome's Gemelli Hospital, just four days after an operation to remove a cancerous growth from his lung.

The 71-year-old walked unaided to his waiting car, stopping to speak to well-wishers.

The Vatican said the Pope will give the traditional Angelus prayer and blessing to a crowd in St Peter's Square on Sunday, as he did last week when he surprised the world by announcing the surgery.

On Friday, photographs were released of the Pope celebrating Mass and distributing communion in hospital for staff.

A statement from his doctors said blood tests and a chest X-ray showed "steady improvement" following his operation.

The surgery on Tuesday, which lasted for 90 minutes, included the removal of the lower lobe of the Pope's right lung. The results of further tests to check for any sign that the cancer has spread have not yet been announced.

The Pope also spoke to Russian President Vladimir Putin on Friday, in their first call since June 2025. The Vatican said the call was to urge "dialogue and peace".

It came as Russia's bombardment of cities across Ukraine intensifies, with a growing number of civilian casualties and no sign of Putin being ready to halt the invasion.

The Pope also called for a humanitarian ceasefire in the Ukrainian city of Oleshkiy, occupied by Russia and under constant shelling, to allow people to be evacuated and for the urgent delivery of food and medicine. The BBC recently reported on residents there being forced to eat garden weeds to survive.

The Pope's schedule has been cleared completely until 20 October, so his reappearance in public so soon is a surprise and will be some relief for Catholics around the world.

Those close to the Pope said he was keen not to delay a trip to Latin America, planned for early November and which includes a visit to Peru, where he was a missionary for many years.

It is not yet clear whether he might be fit to travel or require further treatment.

Meanwhile, the Member of Parliament(MP) for Abuakwa North Constituency, Nana Ampaw Kwame Addo-Frempong, said the initiative is aimed at encouraging students to work harder and develop an interest in Science and Mathematics.

He also announced scholarship opportunities for students pursuing medical education to support their studies and encourage more young people to pursue careers in science and medicine.

The support is expected to motivate students to perform better academically and contribute to national development.

Ghana News.title: Will you marry outside your tribe?
Ghana News.content:
In Ghanaian culture and traditions, every adult is expected to marry and, among others, continue the lineage. In the past, it was the duty of parents to find partners for their children.

They would search the community for a prospective partner and do a thorough search on the person and his or her extended family to ensure he or she would be a good life partner. The search was localised, so most people ended up marrying within their tribe.

Your parents get you a partner, and you accept him or her. Such marriages tended to be stable even when the partners had never met or courted.

Today, it is the young people who look for their lovers from anywhere and seek parental approval.

In many cases, if you tell your parents about a potential spouse, the first question that will come up is ‘where does he or she come from?’

Your answer could spell hope or despair because, for many parents, where an in-law comes from is an important indicator of the health of a marriage.

Why inter-tribal marriage?

The world has become a small village. We move everywhere to study, work and seek adventure. Chances are that you interact with people of similar background and interest. Love does not know tribe, and you may find yourself falling in love with someone outside your tribe.

Some marry outside their tribe for personal benefits such as the chance to travel abroad. There are also those who are disappointed with their own kind through failed relationships and think people from their tribe never make good life partners.

The reality is that Ghana is moving from a homogeneous to a heterogeneous society, and when young people meet and are attracted to each other, tribe can wait.

Challenge of intertribal marriage

Intertribal marriage has its genuine cultural conflicts because each tribe has its own beliefs and expectations of marriage. The wider the cultural conflicts, the greater the potential for conflicts.

There is also the problem of lineage. For example, Ga, Ewes, and Northerners inherit along paternal lines, while the Akans inherit along maternal lines.

If an Akan man marries a Ga or Ewe, their children traditionally are lost because they do not belong anywhere.

Studies show partners in intertribal marriages have lower support from friends, family members, and society.

Sometimes the resistance of parents is so high that many go back to their hometown to marry their own kind, secretly or openly to please their extended family members. Intertribal marriages therefore have a greater risk of marital dissatisfaction and divorce.

Will you marry outside your tribe?

Today, intertribal marriages are on the increase. You find Ghanaian marriages in so many permutations. Some are marrying outside Ghana.

This means the tribal factor is dying slowly because many know that your marriage will work if you work at it and that where one comes from does not necessarily determine the health of marriage. Inter-tribal marriages do not have greater risk than intra-tribal marriages.

There are many cases of clients who have serious standoffs with their parents on the tribe of their lovers. One case lasted four years before the parents gave in, but not without very diplomatic counselling.

Now they confess this man is the best thing that happened to the entire extended family because he is the pillar of support. They see him as their own son and not an in-law.

If you meet someone you love but who comes from a different tribe, do this: go after him or her relentlessly and track him or her down as long as you truly love each other.

Your parents may show initial resistance, but if you are patient and your lover proves himself or herself to be a good person, in almost all cases, the tribal factor will die, and you could have a fulfilling marriage.

It is, however, important that you do serious courtship and know your partner very well. Talk about the hard facts, your cultural differences, and how to cope with them.

Learn each other’s language and enjoy each other’s local food. If you show commitment, mutual respect, effective communication, and a forgiving spirit, the tribal factor will disappear, and you will find that true love is beautiful and has no tribal colours.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: Haaland’s record scoring spree helps Man City to seventh Premier League win
World.content:
Manchester City continue their 100 percent start despite calls for sanctions after being found guilty of breaking rules.

The ongoing financial scandal enveloping Manchester City is not affecting the team’s results in the Premier League, nor has it diminished Erling Haaland’s appetite for goals.

Playing in front of fans waving inflatable bananas, City became only the third team to open a Premier League season with seven straight wins by beating Ipswich 3-2 at home on Saturday. Haaland netted twice to move to a season-high eight goals for a campaign being played under a cloud of controversy.

That made it back-to-back victories in the league for City, either side of a 4-2 loss to Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League, since being found guilty of large-scale financial wrongdoing in the Premier League for nearly a decade. The seismic verdict threatens the club’s place in England’s lucrative top flight, though City continue to protest their innocence and have appealed.

City manager Enzo Maresca believes the saga has galvanised the squad, and the defiance among the fanbase continued, with many supporters bringing along inflatable bananas – a throwback to an item that fans brought to games in the 1980s for fun amid tough times for the team – for Ipswich’s visit. They also jeered the Premier League anthem before kickoff.

“The fans, the club, the players – we are all together in this journey,” Maresca said of City’s defiance in troubled times.

“Going down with the City” was the chant by some home fans in the first half at the Etihad Stadium as they watched their team extend their lead in the league to six points.

Haaland and second-half substitute Antoine Semenyo were seen hobbling off the field at the end of the game, which finished with Ipswich grabbing its second goal in stoppage time and piling on the pressure in the final minutes.



The Norwegian has become the fastest player in Premier League history to score 100 non-penalty goals. It took him 139 matches to achieve this record.

Maresca said Haaland, who had taken a blow to the foot late in the match, was not worried.

“We will see,” Maresca said. “I asked him, and he said he was OK, so hopefully it is nothing serious.”

Maresca added that Semenyo’s injury might be more serious.

Maresca became the first manager to win his first seven Premier League games in charge of a team.

“I didn’t expect to win seven out of seven,” said Maresca, who replaced Pep Guardiola in the off season, “but we are working well, working good.”

Chelsea (in 2005) and Liverpool (in 2019) are the other teams to win at least their first seven games of a Premier League season – and they both went on to win the title.

Earlier, Liverpool came from behind to win 2-1 at nine-man Brentford but lost two more players to injury in a busy stretch of fixtures.

Trailing to Keane Lewis-Potter’s 44th-minute header, Liverpool found themselves with a man advantage when Brentford midfielder Yehor Yarmoliuk was shown a red card in first-half stoppage time for aiming a head-butt at Jeremy Jacquet.

Liverpool took advantage, with Victor Munoz and Alexander Isak scoring after the break to consign Brentford to their first league defeat this season.

Vitaly Janelt became the second Brentford player to be sent off after getting a second yellow card in second-half stoppage time.

Isak has just returned from an injury sustained on international duty with Sweden, but two players are back on the treatment table, with Dominik Szoboszlai and Jeremie Frimpong – a half-time substitute – forced off with injuries.

Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola said Szoboszlai’s problem was the recurrence of the hamstring injury he got while playing for Hungary in the recent international break.

Johan Manzambi, who could easily have joined Newcastle in the off season, grabbed the winner against the team for Aston Villa.

The 21-year-old Switzerland midfielder scored for the third time in four games to seal Villa’s 1-0 victory at St James’ Park in Newcastle.

It would have been a painful sight for Newcastle, who reached an agreement with Freiburg to sign Manzambi after his impressive World Cup performances, but not with the player himself. Now he is thriving for Villa.

Fulham eased the pressure on manager Alvaro Arbeloa by beating Hull 1-0 for their first league win of the season.



Alex Iwobi scored the goal in the 33rd minute, helping Fulham climb off the bottom of the table – much to the relief of Arbeloa, the former Real Madrid coach who arrived in the off season.

World.title: Chelsea’s injury-hit Emi Martinez will return to action ‘in a few weeks’
World.content:
The Argentinian goalkeeper is stretchered off after a collision during Chelsea’s visit to Everton and later undergoes surgery.

Share Chelsea’s injury-hit Emi Martinez will return to action ‘in a few weeks’ on social media

Goalkeeper Emi Martinez says he will be “back in a few weeks” after undergoing surgery following a clash of heads during Chelsea’s 2-0 win at Everton in the Premier League.

Martinez and Jarrad Branthwaite came together on Saturday when Everton’s Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall whipped a free kick into the box, and although the Everton defender was back on his feet after treatment, the Chelsea goalkeeper required treatment from paramedics.

The 34-year-old ‌‌Argentinian was eventually strapped to a stretcher and carried off the field before being taken to hospital with a concussion as media in Argentina reported he had suffered a jaw injury in the collision.

Martinez, wearing a hospital gown, posted on social media on Sunday: “Thanks to everyone for the messages. The operation went well.

“The most important thing is that we won and kept a clean ⁠⁠sheet. In a few weeks we’ll be back.”

Martinez’s injury forced ⁠⁠Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso to give Mike Penders his Premier League debut, and the 21-year-old keeper helped Chelsea keep their first clean sheet in the league since January.

Penders, a Belgian youth international, will ⁠⁠likely have to step in until Martinez is cleared to return to training.

Chelsea host Tottenham Hotspur in the league ⁠⁠next Saturday, followed by a League Cup fourth-round game ⁠⁠at Liverpool on October 28 and a home Premier League match against Manchester United three days later.
