World.title: NDLEA issues public alert after intercepting woman with drugs concealed in palm oil keg
World.content:
The National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) has warned Nigerians against accepting parcels or luggage from other people for delivery, after its operatives discovered illicit drugs concealed in a keg of palm oil intended for shipment to Saudi Arabia.

Femi Babafemi, the agency’s director of media and advocacy, issued the warning in an X post titled “Public Alert”, accompanied by a video showing NDLEA officials removing substances wrapped in polythene from a keg.

Babafemi said the consignment was given to a woman travelling to Saudi Arabia, who was asked to deliver it to another person in the Middle Eastern country.

According to him, the woman was intercepted by NDLEA officers at the airport, where the concealed drugs were discovered.

“We’ll never be tired of repeating this warning: Never accept any parcel or luggage from anyone or on behalf of anyone no matter how close you’re!” Babafemi wrote.

He warned that the woman could have faced severe consequences if the drugs had been discovered by authorities in Saudi Arabia.

“She’ll have been counting her days on earth by now if this was discovered in Saudi,” he said.

Babafemi urged Nigerians to exercise caution when asked to transport items for other people, regardless of their relationship with the person making the request.

He advised travellers to prioritise their safety and freedom over the fear of offending friends, relatives or acquaintances who ask them to carry packages.

“Choose to offend the person than go to jail. BE WISE!” he added.

The NDLEA spokesperson also called on Nigerians to share the warning with their friends and family members to prevent unsuspecting travellers from becoming involved in drug trafficking.

The agency has repeatedly cautioned travellers against accepting packages whose contents they cannot independently verify, as traffickers may exploit personal relationships and unsuspecting couriers to move illicit substances across borders.

World.title: SERAP sues INEC over alleged ₦126bn missing electoral funds
World.content:
The Socio-Economic Rights and Accountability Project (SERAP) has sued the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) over its alleged failure to account for more than ₦126.46bn appropriated for electoral operations.

In a statement signed by Kolawole Oluwadare, SERAP deputy director on Sunday, the organisation is asking the Federal High Court in Abuja to compel INEC to disclose details of the expenditure, utilisation and disbursement of the funds, which were earmarked for the procurement of election materials, equipment, vehicles and other services.

According to SERAP, the allegations are contained in the 2023 audited report of the Auditor-General of the Federation, published on August 7, 2026. The report covers transactions from January to December 2022, with some extending to December 31, 2023.

In suit number FHC/ABJ/CS/2507/2026, filed last week, SERAP is seeking “an order of mandamus to direct and compel INEC to promptly disclose detailed information on the expenditure, utilisation and disbursement of over ₦126.46 billion appropriated for electoral operations, including the procurement of election materials, equipment, and vehicles.”

The organisation is also seeking “an order of mandamus to direct and compel INEC to disclose a full financial and documentary account of the over ₦126 billion appropriated for electoral operations, including amounts released and paid, payment beneficiaries, details of contractors and their beneficial owners.”

SERAP argued that the allegations raised questions about the management of public funds intended to support Nigeria’s electoral process.

“Electoral resources are public resources. INEC must be able to account for every naira, demonstrate that it was lawfully spent and show that it served the purposes for which it was appropriated,” the organisation stated.

It added, “These allegations are particularly disturbing given the constitutional importance of INEC and the fact that the expenditure concerns resources appropriated for the administration of Nigeria’s electoral system.”

According to SERAP, “With the 2027 general elections approaching, transparency and accountability in the management of these funds are essential to safeguarding public confidence in the electoral process and ensuring that resources intended to support credible elections are properly utilised.”

The organisation further argued that, “These findings by the Auditor-General suggest a grave violation of the public trust and the provisions of the Nigerian Constitution 1999 (as amended), national anticorruption laws, and the country’s obligations under the UN Convention against Corruption.”

The suit, filed on behalf of SERAP by its lawyers, Kolawole Oluwadare, Kehinde Oyewumi and Andrew Nwankwo, cited several alleged irregularities identified in the Auditor-General’s report.

“The Auditor-General, INEC ‘irregularly paid’ over ₦112 billion [₦112,155,597,845.00] ‘for ballot boxes, electoral devices, items and materials without competitive bidding or a BPP Certificate of No Objection,’” the suit stated.

It further alleged that the Auditor-General found “no evidence that the items were procured.”

The suit added that the “contracts were awarded to companies whose competences, experience, capacities, addresses and factory locations were unknown.”

According to the organisation, the Auditor-General was concerned that the money “may have been diverted” and recommended its recovery.

SERAP also cited an alleged payment of more than ₦1.05bn for Toyota Prado TXL 2021 Model vehicles.

The suit stated that INEC “paid over ₦1 billion [₦1,058,925,000.00] for Toyota Prado TXL 2021 Model without ,

competitive bidding, bid evaluation or a BPP Certificate of No Objection.”

It added that the Auditor-General feared the money “may have been lost” and that the contracts “may have been inflated.”

The organisation also alleged that more than ₦3.13bn was paid to four contractors for ballot guides, sensitive materials and result sheets before the contracts were awarded.

“INEC ‘paid over ₦3 billion [₦3,136,806,050.00] to four contractors for ballot guides, sensitive materials and result sheets before the contracts were awarded, with no evidence of payment.’ The Auditor-General is concerned that the money ‘may have been diverted.’ He wants the money recovered and remitted to the treasury,” the suit stated.

On another transaction, SERAP alleged that INEC “paid over ₦9 billion [₦9,245,965,502.60] for 22 contracts for similar goods

and services”, with the contracts “split to circumvent procurement procedures and awarded on the same day.”

The Auditor-General reportedly said the money “may have been lost” and that “the payment may have been made for items not supplied.”

The suit also raised concerns over payments to accounting firms, alleging that INEC “paid over ₦129 million [₦129,375,000.00] to 19 accounting firms for financial audit services without evidence of utilisation or requests and expenditure by the consultants.”

It stated that the Auditor-General believed the money “may have been diverted” and wanted it recovered and remitted to the treasury.

On accreditation devices, SERAP alleged that INEC “paid over ₦504 million [₦504,492,641.00] for accreditation devices without due procurement process.”

The suit added that the “APG had expired before the security licence key was delivered and the software was valid for only four months, raising questions about economy and value for money.”

SERAP also cited an alleged payment of more than ₦235m to contractors for sleeping mats and digital archiving, claiming that INEC “paid over ₦235 million [₦235,103,000.00] to unqualified contractors for sleeping mats and digital archiving.”

The Auditor-General reportedly identified “serious concerns regarding the eligibility and capacity of the contractors” and raised concerns that the money “may have been lost.”

Among its requests, SERAP wants INEC to provide documentary and physical evidence that the more than ₦112bn identified as irregularly paid was used to procure the relevant electoral materials, including details of their current location and status.

“Nigerians have a right to know every public act, everything that is done in the public interest, by their public institutions including INEC,” the organisation stated.

It also urged the court to direct INEC to preserve electoral equipment, materials and other public assets covered by the audit findings.

“INEC should be directed to ensure that no electoral equipment, material or other public asset covered by the Auditor-General’s findings is disposed of, transferred, destroyed, written off or otherwise dealt with in a manner that could frustrate transparency and accountability,” the suit stated.

SERAP further called for the publication of the names of contractors, suppliers and consultants who allegedly received the funds irregularly, as well as any public officials who authorised or facilitated the transactions or benefited from them.

The organisation said Nigerians were entitled to know whether the contracted goods and services were supplied, whether payments matched the items delivered and whether contracts were deliberately split to evade procurement requirements.

It also cited Section 15(5) of the Nigerian Constitution, which requires public institutions to abolish corrupt practices and abuse of power, as well as Section 13, which sets out responsibilities relating to the implementation of the Constitution’s Chapter II provisions.

SERAP further referenced Nigeria’s obligations under the United Nations Convention against Corruption, Article 25 of the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights and Article 13 of the African Charter on Human and Peoples’ Rights.

The organisation said the legal provisions support transparency in public financial management and citizens’ participation in public affairs.

No date has been fixed for the hearing of the suit.

World.title: Out-of-control truck kills 13 at Hindu festival in India
World.content:
An ambulance carrying victims of a stampede at India’s Durga Puja religious gathering stops at a hospital in Kolkata (STRINGER)

A speeding truck in India killed 13 people when it ploughed into a crowd at a Hindu festival, officials said on Sunday, with President Droupadi Murmu describing the deaths as “heartbreaking”.

The heavily loaded truck reportedly lost control in the early hours of Sunday and hit devotees gathered at a temple in Gwalior, in the central state of Madhya Pradesh.

The Press Trust of India (PTI) news agency cited hospital officials as saying 13 people had died.

“I express my deepest condolences to the bereaved families and pray for the swift recovery of those injured,” Murmu said on social media.

India, with 1.4 billion people, recorded more than 183,000 road traffic deaths in 2025, or over 500 a day, according to the roads ministry.

Many are linked to inadequate road infrastructure, ill-maintained vehicles and exhausted drivers, according to official data.

World.title: Accord Lagos chairman seeks clarity over Adeleke’s Tinubu campaign role
World.content:
Mr Oladele Oladeji, Lagos State Chairman of Accord, has called for clarification over Gov. Ademola Adeleke’s reported appointment as coordinator of President Bola Tinubu’s 2027 presidential campaign in Osun.

Oladeji said the reported appointment raised concerns about its implications for Accord’s political identity, candidates and electoral prospects.

In an open letter to the party’s national leadership on Saturday, he questioned Adeleke’s political allegiance, given that he was elected governor on Accord’s platform.

“Our letter was a genuine expression of concern about the implications of Governor Adeleke’s reported appointment as coordinator of President Tinubu’s 2027 presidential campaign in Osun,” he said.

Oladeji said his intervention was not intended to usurp the responsibilities of the National Working Committee or any other constituted party organ.

“A concerned party member does not need special authorisation to ask questions about the direction of the party to which they belong,” he said.

He described his intervention as a legitimate expression of concern about the party’s future, rather than an attempt to undermine its leadership or constitutional structures.

Oladeji acknowledged Adeleke’s right to make personal political decisions but argued that such choices should be assessed against the interests of Accord.

He said Adeleke’s position as the party’s elected governor made his political decisions significant to its public identity, candidates and members.

“Accord’s independent political direction, the electoral prospects of the party’s candidates and the party’s national ambition demand a distinct allegiance to the party’s electoral ambitions and goals,” he said.

Oladeji urged Adeleke to remain committed to the electoral success of Accord candidates nationwide, noting that party members had supported his governorship election.

He said political cooperation was not inherently objectionable but insisted that its terms, objectives and consequences should be clearly communicated to party members and candidates.

“Our concern is whether the terms, objectives and consequences of such cooperation are sufficiently clear to members and candidates who must carry the party’s name before the electorate,” he said.

Oladeji reaffirmed his position on the original letter, saying he would continue seeking clarification from the appropriate party authorities.

He said his intervention aimed to promote accountability and protect the interests of Accord and its candidates, rather than provoke unnecessary disputes.

He urged the party’s national leadership to clarify its political direction and explain the implications of the reported arrangement to members and the public.

“We will continue to express our concerns respectfully, rely on verifiable facts and defend the right of party members to seek clarity about the future of their political platform,” he said.

World.title: 2027:  APC chairman predicts 70% North’s votes for Tinubu
World.content:
APC National chair, Prof. Nentawe Yilwatda.

The All Progressives Congress (APC) National Chairman, Prof. Nentawe Yilwatda, says the North will deliver more than 70 per cent of its votes to President Bola Tinubu in 2027.

Yilwatda spoke on Saturday in Abuja at the opening of Arewa for Asiwaju (A4A), a political pressure group mobilising support for Tinubu and the APC.

He described the 2027 presidential election as an opportunity to renew Tinubu’s mandate, citing infrastructure projects, political appointments and inclusive governance.

The APC chairman expressed confidence that northern voters would support Tinubu’s re-election, arguing that the region had benefited significantly from his administration.

He listed road projects across the North, including the Trans-Saharan Super Highway, covering routes from Benue through the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Akwanga, Jos, Maiduguri and Biu.

“I can’t mention all of them, but President Tinubu has done wonderfully. He has covered all the geopolitical zones in the North in terms of road projects,” he said.

Yilwatda said the administration was also undertaking railway and healthcare projects across the region, including health centres and free medical services for pregnant women.

He identified the appointment of northerners to key political positions as another reason the region should support Tinubu’s re-election.

The APC chairman urged supporters to secure votes for Tinubu at the grassroots, expressing confidence in their ability to deliver the projected 70 per cent.

“Even if in our hometown alone we can win our polling units for President Tinubu, we have over 70 per cent of the vote in the North, just us alone in our polling units.

“So we have no reason not to return Tinubu. Therefore, I move that he should be returned for the second time,” Yilwatda said.

World.title: Messi brace lifts Inter Miami to 3-1 win in Atlanta
World.content:
Inter Miami’s Argentine forward #10 Lionel Messi runs with the ball during a Major League Soccer (MLS) regular season football match between Inter Miami CF and New York City FC at Nu Stadium in Miami, Florida, on October 14, 2026. (Photo by CHANDAN KHANNA / AFP)

Lionel Messi scored twice in the space of four minutes to lift Inter Miami to a 3-1 victory at Atlanta United on Saturday as the Herons’ MLS title defense continued to gain steam with the playoffs approaching.

The 39-year-old superstar tops the Major League Soccer scoring chart with 25 goals, six ahead of Croatian striker Petar Musa of FC Dallas and Philadelphia’s Milan Iloski.

At the same Atlanta stadium where Messi helped Argentina beat England in the World Cup semi-finals in July, Messi delivered two scintillating goals to secure Miami’s third straight victory.

German Berterame, who put Miami up 1-0 in the 45th minute, turned provider, finding Messi who weaved through the Atlanta defense to unleash a left footed shot from the center of the box and make it 2-0 in the 56th minute.

Four minutes later Messi struck again, breaking away on a pass from Luis Suarez and getting the better of hapless Junior Alonso to fire past Atlanta keeper Lucas Hoyos.

Messi had helped put Miami on top shortly before halftime, heading the ball to Suarez who shook off his defender in the box and lofted a pass that Berterame nodded home to make it 1-0.

Messi was credited with an assist, that saw him pull level with LAFC’s Son Heung-min atop the assists table. Messi is the first player in MLS history to record at least 15 assists in three straight seasons.

Messi now has four goals in three matches since his emotional Argentina send-off. Miami, who clinched a playoff berth on Wednesday, won their third straight game under Cristian “Kily” Gonzalez, who took over as coach last month.

Fafa Picault converted a penalty in the 89th minute to pull a goal back for Atlanta, but at second-from-bottom in the Eastern Conference Gerardo Martino’s team are running out of time to turn things around in time to reach the playoffs.

– St. Louis streak ends –

Elsewhere, St. Louis City’s MLS record-tying 19-match unbeaten streak ended with a 3-2 loss at Minnesota as Philadelphia’s undefeated run reached 15 matches with a 2-2 draw with Charlotte.

Canadian Marcus Caldeira scored the game winner for Minnesota in the 86th minute after United fell behind early on St. Louis goals by Brazilian forward Rafael Navarro and South Korean winger Jeong Sang-bin.

Aziel Jackson answered for Minnesota in the 49th minute and Kelvin Yeboah netted the equalizer in the 68th.

St. Louis City, already headed to the playoffs for the first time since 2023, missed the chance to break the MLS unbeaten streak mark it now shares with Columbus, Dallas and Inter Miami.

City also saw their MLS-record 21-match unbeaten streak across all competitions snapped.

City had not lost an MLS match since falling 2-0 at Austin on May 3, with 13 victories and six drawn in the run.

Philadelphia had won eight MLS matches in a row before the fightback home draw with Charlotte.

Philadelphia lost 6-4 at Miami on May 24 but since then the Union have won 12 times and drawn three, taking 39 of a possible 45 points since Ryan Richter took over as interim head coach during the league’s World Cup break.

World.title: Oyedele: World Markets Have Written Off Opposition, Eyeing Tinubu’s 2nd Term
World.content:
•Rules out return to fuel subsidy, warns of risks to naira

•CBN seeks Chinese capital, deeper financial ties to boost investment in Nigeria

• World Bank report: ADC asks Tinubu to explain ‘missing’ $12.4bn

Nume Ekeghe in Bangkok, Thailand and Chuks Okocha in Abuja

The Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, has said financial markets and the international community have largely written off Nigeria’s opposition political parties as unserious, with investors already pricing in the prospects of President Bola Tinubu securing a second term and expecting continuity in his economic reforms.

This is just as the Governor of the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN), Olayemi Cardoso, also said policy consistency and transparency were essential to sustaining investor confidence, as improvements in economic and foreign exchange stability created better conditions for long-term investment.

Meanwhile, the African Democratic Congress (ADC) has called on President Tinubu to explain the $12.4 billion gap, an equivalent of about N16.5 trillion, in Nigeria’s external accounts identified in the World Bank’s October 2026 Nigeria Development Update.

Oyedele and Cardoso spoke at the closing press briefing of the IMF/World Bank Annual Meetings in Bangkok, Thailand, where the CBN governor said policy consistency would be critical to attracting long-term capital, sustaining economic stability and accelerating growth.

On his part, Oyedele argued that investors’ expectations of continuity under Tinubu had influenced their assessment of Nigeria’s economic outlook, including their response to opposition proposals to restore fuel subsidies.

“In all the meetings I have had, I came to a conclusion that the markets, including the domestic market, which you can read from the capital market, and the international market, have largely written off the opposition in Nigeria as being unserious. That is why they have not priced in the proposed return of subsidy,” he said.

He added that any indication that the president intended to restore the subsidy would immediately be reflected in market prices.

“So, maybe the international and domestic markets are aware about who is sincere about Nigeria and what direction they should travel,” he said.

“As I said, the markets and the international community have been pricing in the prospect of a second term for the President, and they expect continuity in the reforms.”

The minister’s comments followed repeated questions from investors about whether the government would sustain its policies as Nigeria approaches another election cycle.

He said concerns about possible policy reversals had featured prominently in his engagements with investors in Thailand and during two visits to London, particularly over whether electoral pressures could force the administration to abandon its reform agenda.

“Throughout the meetings we have had this week, as well as those I attended before now, including two visits to London to meet investors, one question has repeatedly come up: Are you going to reverse your reforms? Are you under pressure because of elections?” he said.

According to Oyedele, the government remained committed to the reforms, which he described as necessary to restore macroeconomic stability and lay the foundation for sustainable growth.

He said the next phase of the economic programme would focus on translating the gains in stability into stronger investment, lower financing costs, job creation and improved economic opportunities for Nigerians.

Oyedele said private investment had increased twentyfold since the reforms began, rising from about $300 million in 2023 to $6 billion in 2026.

He also highlighted improvements in Nigeria’s external position, saying net reserves had risen from barely $3 billion to more than $45 billion, representing a fifteen-fold increase.

Oyedele ruled out a return to fuel subsidies and multiple exchange rates, warning that reversing the reforms could undermine investor confidence, trigger capital flight and put renewed pressure on the naira.

“Let me be clear: there will be no return to fuel subsidies or multiple exchange rates,” he said.

“If, for any reason, Mr President were to say today that we were considering bringing back fuel subsidies, what happened in Indonesia would be child’s play in comparison,” he said.

“At the end of the day, capital would leave because investors understand what such a decision means.”

He argued that capital flight could intensify pressure on the foreign exchange market and weaken the naira, with the consequences ultimately borne by ordinary Nigerians.

“When capital leaves, the foreign-exchange market will come under pressure, and the naira will crash. The exchange rate could move to N3,000, N3,500 or N4,000 to the dollar,” he said.

Oyedele said such a development would worsen the economic pressures facing households.

The minister also defended the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited’s recent temporary reduction in petrol retail margins, insisting that it was a commercial decision rather than a subsidy financed with public funds.

“The recent temporary reduction in the retail margin on fuel was a time-bound commercial decision by the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited to reduce margins and support Nigerians,” he said.

“It is not a subsidy paid for with public funds.”

He explained that a company’s decision to reduce its profit margin to lower prices should not automatically be classified as a subsidy.

“If you offer a discount by reducing that profit margin, how does that become a subsidy?” he asked.

Cardoso: Policy Consistency, Transparency Critical to Investor Confidence

Meanwhile, Cardoso has stressed that policy consistency and transparency were essential to sustaining investor confidence, as improvements in economic and foreign exchange stability created better conditions for long-term investment.

Cardoso said Nigeria was seeking to deepen financial cooperation with China to attract more Asian investment into its markets and improve cross-border payments, settlement arrangements and trade finance.

He disclosed that discussions with the Governor of the People’s Bank of China, Pan Gongsheng, had focused on practical ways to strengthen cooperation among financial institutions in both countries.

Cardoso said China’s developed payments infrastructure offered lessons for Nigeria, while stronger financial links could facilitate trade and investment between the two economies.

He said the discussions would be followed by technical engagements during his forthcoming visit to Beijing, where officials would examine specific areas of cooperation and identify initiatives capable of delivering practical results.

The CBN governor said Nigeria was particularly interested in attracting Chinese capital into its financial markets, noting that investment in Nigerian financial instruments had remained limited despite the substantial liquidity available in China.

“Finally, bear in mind that, despite the considerable liquidity available in China, there has not been much investment in Nigerian financial instruments over time,” he said.

“This could be an opportunity to change that trajectory and generate greater interest from Asian markets in Nigerian instruments and African instruments generally.”

Cardoso said the initiative formed part of a broader effort to strengthen Nigeria’s financial relationships with Asian economies and expand the pool of capital available to domestic markets.

World Bank Report: ADC Asks Tinubu-led Govt to Explain ‘Missing’ $12.4bn

Meanwhile, the ADC has called on President Tinubu to explain the $12.4 billion gap, equivalent to about N16.5 trillion, in Nigeria’s external accounts identified in the World Bank’s October 2026 Nigeria Development Update.

In a statement issued yesterday by its National Publicity Secretary, Mallam Bolaji Abdullahi, the party said Tinubu owed Nigerians a clear account of the discrepancy, especially as families struggling with the cost-of-living crisis were forced to account for every naira.

Citing the report, the ADC said Nigeria recorded a $12 billion current-account surplus and $6.2 billion in net financial inflows in the first half of 2026.

The party said these inflows should have strengthened the country’s reserves, but the report instead identified a $12.4 billion gap.

Abdullahi said the World Bank attributed the gap, in part, to oil export earnings that were not repatriated. He added that the report noted that the repatriation of export proceeds remained limited, partly because Nigerian oil had been pledged against several long-term loans.

“The scale is staggering,” the ADC said.

“This unexplained gap is larger than the entire current-account surplus for the same period. It is about 5.6 times the $2.2 billion Nigeria attracted in foreign direct investment. In naira terms, it is almost a quarter of the N68.32 trillion 2026 federal budget.

“This cannot be dismissed as a minor accounting discrepancy. President Tinubu welcomed this report. He cannot celebrate one part of the report and stay silent on a gap bigger than the surplus that he and his government are celebrating.

“Due to President Tinubu’s failed policies, families across Nigeria are forced to skip meals and account for every naira just to survive. Meanwhile, money that could have eased their hardship is currently unaccounted for. Tinubu owes Nigerians an explanation.

“Sacrifice cannot be compulsory for everyday citizens while accountability remains optional for the government that is in charge of our collective resources.”

The ADC called on the federal government to publish a full public reconciliation of the $12.4 billion gap and disclose all oil-backed loans and pledged crude commitments.

It also demanded updated net reserve figures and clear evidence that higher revenues were improving essential services such as health, education and power.

“President Tinubu must open the books. Nigerians have sacrificed enough. We deserve answers,” the party said.

World.title: North Will Give Tinubu Over 70% of Votes in 2027, Says Yilwatda
World.content:
•Shettima: Region will re-elect president

•Makinde will defeat Tinubu in his 12 battleground states, others, says campaign council

Deji Elumoye, Chuks Okocha and Adedayo Akinwale in Abuja

The National Chairman of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Professor Nentawe Yilwatda, has predicted that the North will give President Bola Tinubu more than 70 per cent of its votes in the 2027 presidential election.

Vice President Kashim Shettima has also said the North will re-elect Tinubu, stressing that the region had spoken with a resounding voice and unmistakable conviction for Tinubu’s re-election.

But the Makinde-Daura Presidential Campaign Organisation (MDPCO) declared that its presidential candidate on the platform of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), Governor Seyi Makinde of Oyo State, will defeat Tinubu in the 12 battleground states identified by the president, as well as in other states across the federation.

Speaking yesterday in Abuja when Shettima unveiled the Arewa for Asiwaju Campaign Head Office and formally inaugurated the campaign structure of the northern think tank, Yilwatda urged people in the North to support Tinubu’s re-election bid, citing infrastructure projects, appointments and other initiatives of the President’s administration.

The APC chairman listed road projects across northern states, the Ajaokuta-Kaduna-Kano gas pipeline, irrigation dams, railway projects, healthcare initiatives and the Nigerian Education Loan Fund among the interventions he said should encourage the North to support Tinubu for a second term.

“I can’t mention all of them, but President Bola Tinubu has done wonderfully. He has covered all the geopolitical zones in the North in terms of road projects,” he added.

He moved a motion for the northern region to support the re-election of the Tinubu/Shettima ticket, outlining reasons why the region should mobilize massively for the president.

He noted that the region’s strong backing stems from the Vice President’s inclusive leadership and progressive mindset over the past three years.

Shettima: Region Will Re-elect President in 2027

Also speaking, Shettima declared that the North will re-elect Tinubu, adding however, that the growing northern support for president’s re-election was not a blank check.

According to him, Tinubu’s administration will earn it through facts, radical transparency and measurable results.

He maintained that expanding loyalty in the region would demand greater accountability and an honest dialogue with citizens about ongoing reforms undertaken by the administration.

Shettima said the North had spoken with a resounding voice and unmistakable conviction in its support for the President.

According to him, renewed political confidence should never be taken for granted, adding that the government and its supporters must continue to engage Nigerians with facts and show how the ongoing reforms are improving security, livelihoods, and economic opportunity.

“By now, I believe the North has spoken. We have spoken with a resounding voice and unmistakable conviction. From Adamawa to Zamfara, from Borno to Niger, we have spoken. Such confidence places an obligation upon us that no officeholder should ever underestimate,” he stated.

The Vice President noted that President Tinubu’s bid for a renewed mandate must rest on the administration’s record and a clear account of how another term would advance Nigerians’ interests.

He restated that the North had nothing to fear in President Tinubu’s second term as Nigeria’s leader.

Shettima acknowledged that Nigerians had endured difficult economic adjustments, warning campaigners against dismissing genuine concerns or relying on political slogans to defend government policies.

“Our citizens have endured difficult adjustments. We cannot pretend otherwise. What we owe them is an honest account of the decisions taken, the gains achieved and the difficulties that persist. We lose our hearing when applause becomes our only source of information,” he added.

The Vice President said the concerns of traders facing higher costs, graduates searching for work and families struggling with daily expenses must remain central to government decision-making.

“A failed policy enters somebody’s home as a missed meal, an unpaid school fee or an opportunity lost,” he said.

He also defended criticism as essential to democratic governance, saying the administration must remain open to useful ideas irrespective of political affiliation, ethnicity, religion or region.

“There is no democracy without critics. Progress demands that our assumptions endure the examination of those who disagree with us,” Shettima said.

The Vice President said the administration’s priorities remain security, economic opportunity, poverty reduction, education and stronger public institutions.

“The farmer should be able to cultivate in safety. A child’s education should prepare that child for a productive life. Public institutions should give citizens confidence that effort can yield opportunity,” he said.

Earlier, Deputy Senate President Barau Jibrin said the inauguration of the A4A structure for the 2027 presidential elections came at a time when the region needed a strong, trusted platform to mobilise support for Tinubu.

Similarly, Secretary to the Government of the Federation (SGF), Senator George Akume, said history was beckoning the North to act with wisdom and evidence, not sentiment, in its decision to support the Tinubu administration in the 2027 elections.

On his part, Kano State Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf, speaking on behalf of all the governors of the North, said the northern region’s support for the President in the forthcoming elections would be based on its conviction to uphold fairness, equity, unity and the progress of the country.

In his welcome address, the Director General of A4A and former Jigawa State governor, Abubakar Mohammed Badaru, said the group’s emergence was not accidental, but born of the conviction that President Tinubu and his deputy have performed well and deserve re-election.

Makinde Will Defeat Tinubu in His 12 Battleground States, Others, Says Campaign Council

Meanwhile, the Makinde-Daura Presidential Campaign Organisation (MDPCO) has declared that its presidential candidate on the platform of the APM, Governor Makinde will defeat Tinubu in the 12 battleground states identified by the president, as well as in other states across the federation.

Makinde also declared that Nigeria’s biggest problem is grinding poverty, not religion, urging Christians to stop shunning politics and take an active role in transforming the country.

The MDPCO, in a statement by its Director of Strategic Communications, Hon. Richard Nnanna Ihediwa, asserted that Makinde would decisively defeat Tinubu and his APC Presidential Campaign Council in Rivers State and the FCT, insisting that no amount of political manoeuvring, intimidation or abuse of incumbency by the President’s henchmen can reverse the growing tide of opposition to his re-election.

The organisation said the arrogance and political overreach of Tinubu’s inner circle had deepened public resentment and further weakened his electoral prospects.

It added that President Tinubu’s decision to personally visit and campaign in only 12 states — Oyo, Kaduna, Rivers, Plateau, Borno, Enugu, Bauchi, Sokoto, Delta, Kano, Adamawa and Lagos — further confirmed his apprehension over the mileage and foothold already achieved by Makinde with his RESET NIGERIA Agenda message in the aforementioned and other states of the federation.

“Mr President should know that his visit to these states, if he eventually does, will not in any way change the direction or the determination of the people to vote him out, given his unpardonable failures in office which have brought unprecedented hardship across the country,” the organisation said.

“President Tinubu has no meaningful achievement he can boast of in these and other states of the federation where Nigerians now refer to his government as ‘T-Pain’ following the suffering they have been subjected to by the policies of the Tinubu administration in the last three and a half years.”

The MDPCO challenged President Tinubu not to have a change of mind but to visit the states to face the people.

“We challenge President Tinubu to travel around the country by road and witness the decrepit state of federal highways, the squalor in which Nigerians live and the level of infrastructural decay across the country, while his government squanders trillions of Naira on white elephant projects and wasteful programmes.

“If President Tinubu believes he is popular as he claims, he should not stop at the rally ground or at the airport when he gets to any of the states. He should go beyond waving to a gathering of APC rented crowd and be bold enough to directly engage the people in the communities and towns to seek their votes, as the APM candidate, Makinde, has been doing since he started his campaign,” it said.

“Nigerians are gravitating towards the core campaign pillars and proposals in Makinde’s RESET NIGERIA Agenda, which include the establishment of an all-inclusive, four-year transitional government of national unity with four priority pillars of education, economy, security and socio-political policies.

“Unlike President Tinubu’s visionless, thoughtless and rudderless rule characterised by crass arbitrariness, Makinde’s RESET NIGERIA Agenda offers data-driven strategies that revolve around tackling poverty through massive production; a security plan that prioritises intelligence gathering, social reorientation and decisive kinetic and non-kinetic actions; an education plan that focuses on expanding access to quality functional education; and institutional reform that emphasises inclusive governance and sincere public leadership.”

The campaign urged Tinubu “not to waste the nation’s resources on his ‘Nebuchadnezzar’ Campaign Council of failed politicians who, like the president himself, cannot attract votes from Nigerians.”

In another development, Makinde has declared that Nigeria’s biggest problem was grinding poverty, not religion, urging Christians to stop shunning politics and take an active role in transforming the country.

He said Christians could not afford to stand aloof from politics because it was dirty or because they should not serve under leaders who did not share their faith, stressing that national transformation required their active participation.

Makinde spoke yesterday in Abuja after receiving a Christian Icon Award at the Christian Association of Nigeria’s (CAN) 50th anniversary celebration.

The governor said Christians should draw lessons from biblical figures who accepted difficult assignments in pursuit of a greater purpose.

Makinde cited David, who, despite having been anointed king, served in the palace of Saul, from whom God had departed.

World.title: Tinubu Mourns as Journalist, Ex-Nigerian Ambassador, Dele Cole, Dies in London at 86
World.content:
Deji Elumoye in Abuja



President Bola Tinubu last night expressed profound sadness at the news of the passing of a distinguished diplomat, journalist, politician, historian and elder statesman, Ambassador Patrick Dele Cole, who died in London at 86.

Cole’s death was confirmed yesterday by a family source, who disclosed that the former Nigerian ambassador died earlier in the morning following weeks of deteriorating health.



The source revealed that Cole had recently been discharged from the Intensive Care Unit (ICU), but his health had continued to decline.

“He left ICU a few days ago. He had been doing poorly in recent weeks leading to this end,” the family source said.

Born on August 4, 1940, Cole turned 86 in August, barely two months before his death.

He was widely known for his contributions to Nigeria’s diplomatic service, journalism, and historical scholarship, having held several prominent positions throughout his career.



Before entering diplomatic service, Cole established himself in Nigeria’s media industry, serving on the editorial board of The Guardian newspaper and subsequently as Managing Director of Daily Times, one of the country’s most influential newspapers.

He later represented Nigeria as Ambassador to Argentina and Brazil, extending his public service career into international diplomacy.

He served as Special Adviser on International Relations under President Obasanjo from 1999 to 2007. He was also appointed Nigeria’s ambassador to Brazil and Argentina.



He also ventured into politics and was associated with the Social Democratic Party (SDP) in the 1990s.

Beyond his diplomatic assignments, Cole was recognised for his involvement in national discourse, particularly on governance, politics, and Nigeria’s historical development.



His career spanned journalism, public administration, and diplomacy, placing him among a generation of Nigerian public figures who contributed to the country’s political and institutional development.

In a statement he personally signed, President Tinubu said Ambassador Cole devoted his life to national service, bringing distinction to his work in diplomacy, journalism and politics.



Tinubu noted that Cole’s career reflected the enduring value of dialogue, tact, mutual respect and the pursuit of shared interests in advancing national development and international cooperation.

“His contributions to Nigeria’s media landscape were particularly notable. As Managing Director of the Daily Times, he upheld the vital role of the press in holding public officials accountable, speaking truth to power, and strengthening democratic governance. His legacy in journalism and public life remains an enduring part of our national story,” Tinubu explained.



The president added that at 86, the deceased witnessed defining moments in Nigeria’s history and contributed to the nation’s development through his work in the media, diplomacy and public service.



According to Tinubu, his life stood as a testament to the value of experience, principled engagement and commitment to the public good.

“As we mourn his passing, I extend my heartfelt condolences to his family, friends, professional associates and all whose lives he touched. I pray that memories of his remarkable life will bring them comfort and strength at this difficult time. May Almighty God grant Ambassador Cole eternal rest and give his family and all who mourn him the fortitude to bear this profound loss,” the statement added.

World.title: Over 40 Companies Raise N2.45 Trillion from Stock Market in Nine Months
World.content:
Kayode Tokede

Over 40 companies raised N2.45 trillion from the Nigerian capital market between January and September 2026, as businesses positioned themselves for growth amid persistent economic pressures, according to data on corporate listings on the Nigerian Exchange Limited (NGX).



The capital-raising surge underscores the NGX’s growing importance as a source of long-term financing for businesses seeking alternatives to expensive bank loans.

Data on corporate listings on the NGX show total corporate capital raising hit about N2.45 trillion in nine months of 2026, covering public offers, private placements and supplementary listings.



The surge came as the Nigerian Exchange Limited All-Share Index gained 61.43 per cent year-to-date (YtD) as of September 2026 to 251,211.67 basis points, making Nigeria one of Africa’s best-performing exchanges.

Among the over 40 companies are: Dangote Sugar Refinery, which raised N485.88 billion through a rights issue; Abbey Bank raised N64.547 billion; Guinea Insurance listed 12.673 billion new shares; Regency Alliance Insurance raised N6.051 billion; Sunu Assurance raised N9.339 billion; Sovereign Trust Insurance raised N5.022 billion; Neimeth International Pharmaceuticals raised N2.442 billion; Critical Minerals Financing Corporation raised N1.807 billion and Eunisell Interlinked raised N200 million, among others.



Of the corporate listings, Fidelity Bank Plc, United Bank for Africa Plc (UBA), FCMB Group Plc, First HoldCo Plc, Access Holdings Plc, Sterling Financial Holdings Company Plc and Guaranty Trust Holding Company Plc led the listed firms, with listings of N883.8 billion in the period under review.



The N883.8 billion listing on the NGX by these four financial institutions came against the backdrop of the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) policy mandating that firms raise fresh equity to meet paid-up capital thresholds.

As GTCO listed N10 billion after a successful private placement of 125,000,000 ordinary shares of 50 kobo each at N80.00 per share, NGX admitted UBA’s and First Holdco’s N157.8 billion and N128.7 billion rights issue and private placement in early January 2026, respectively. Access Holdings, N21.4 billion; FCMB Group, N231.83 billion; Sterling Financial Holding Company, N106.978 billion; and Fidelity Bank, N227.05 billion, were new listings on NGX.



The Managing Director of Globalview Capital Limited, Mr. Aruna Kebira, said the recent surge reflected rising investor confidence in the Nigerian Exchange, not apathy, and that confidence is key to capacity building.

Speaking on market participation, Kebira said innovations, improved transparency and the T+1 settlement cycle, where investors get proceeds a day after selling, have deepened retail participation and awareness.

Kebira cited the Dangote Refinery offer, where platforms like OPay and banks actively mobilised investors, as a driver of serious market awareness.



He said the market had evolved significantly since 2011 and was aligning with global standards, moving away from the speculative ‘kalokalo’ approach seen in 2004.

On funding options, Kebira said equity remained the cheapest way to run and expand a manufacturing organisation, as interest on bank loans must be paid regardless of profitability, while equity allowed profits to be ploughed back into the company to do more for shareholders.



He added that the funds had a multiplier effect on capacity expansion, technology adoption and job creation.

He said boards would be under pressure to deliver value, increase production, pay good dividends and put square pegs in square holes because reputation was at stake, adding that the recapitalisation in insurance was necessary to restore the ability to pay claims and rebuild public confidence in the sector.



On his part, the National Chairman of New Dimension Shareholders Association, Mr. Patrick Ajudua, however, stated that fresh capital raising did not automatically translate to higher dividends or immediate job creation.

“You need to know that investment has a risk element. Not all companies that raise fresh capital deliver better dividends,” Ajudua said.

He noted that, in fairness, many companies had delivered dividends, particularly since this administration came to power, which stabilised the economy, especially the foreign exchange market.

World.title: Kwara APC: Ex-VC Leads High-profile Group to Resolve Disputes, Reconcile Aggrieved Members
World.content:
Elder statesman and former Vice-Chancellor of the University of Ilorin, Prof. Oba AbdulRaheem, is leading a group of prominent Kwara indigenes to reconcile aggrieved members of the All Progressives Congress (APC) and mobilise support for the party ahead of the 2027 general election.

The group, which held its inaugural meeting at Abdulraheem’s Ilorin residence on September 17, said it is committed to resolving all disagreements that trailed the outcome of the APC’s primaries.

Abdulraheem, also a former Chairman of the Federal Character Commission (FCC), chairs the group, the Kwara APC Peace Committee.

Apart from Abdulraheem, eminent indigenes of Kwara in the group include Dr. Johnson Adewumi, a foremost educationist/ entrepreneur and founder of the Thomas Adewumi University, Oko; former Minister and former Speaker, Kwara State House of Assembly, Hon. Issa Bio Ibrahim; and former Secretary to Kwara State Government and former Member, Federal House of Representatives, Hon. AbdulGaniyu Cook Olododo.

Other members include Oloriewe Raheem Adedoyin, a veteran journalist and member representing Africa in the Executive Board of the International Press Institute; elder statesman and former Speaker, Kwara State House of Assembly, Hon. Benjamin Ezekiel Issa; elder statesman and Member of Tinubu Shettina PCC, Pastor John Dara; and former Commissioner, Federal Character Commission, Hon. James Jiya Kolo.

According to the statement, the committee intends to serve as a voice of conscience among APC leaders by addressing internal grievances and promoting the achievements of the administrations of President Bola Tinubu and Kwara State Governor AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq.

It said the group had reached out to some aggrieved political leaders and influential stakeholders to encourage reconciliation and forge a common front ahead of the elections.

The committee is also canvassing support for the APC’s governorship candidate, Hon. Yakubu Danladi, and other party candidates in the state.

The statement said the initiative aimed to secure the backing of party stakeholders for the candidates and strengthen cohesion within the APC ahead of the general election.

World.title: Elumelu Backs $15bn Infrastructure Investment Drive Across West Africa
World.content:
Festus Akanbi

Heirs Holdings Chairman Mr Tony Elumelu is backing efforts to assemble a $15 billion portfolio of infrastructure projects across West Africa, as regional leaders and investors seek to turn economic integration ambitions into bankable investments.

The initiative, being developed ahead of the inaugural West Africa Integration and Investment Summit (WAIIS) in Sierra Leone next month, will bring selected projects before prospective financiers to mobilise capital for infrastructure and productive enterprises.

Elumelu, who co-chairs the summit, disclosed the plans in an emailed response to questions from Bloomberg, which reported the development on Thursday.

Potential financiers include United Bank for Africa (UBA), the African Export-Import Bank (Afreximbank), Africa Finance Corporation (AFC) and Africa50. Priority sectors comprise energy, trade, industrialisation, strategic minerals, agriculture and digital infrastructure.

The proposed $15 billion represents the anticipated value of the investment pipeline, rather than funding already committed by Elumelu or the participating financial institutions.

Organisers have so far shortlisted 26 projects worth more than $10 billion from 170 submissions spanning more than 10 countries, with expectations that the portfolio will expand before the November gathering.

Special Envoy for WAIIS, Dr Kandeh Kolleh Yumkella, said the selection reflected progress towards presenting investors with concrete opportunities across the region.

“We received 170 project submissions and have selected 26 real projects worth more than $10 billion from over ten countries,” Yumkella said in a statement issued by the organisers.

“We expect that portfolio to reach $15 billion or more,” he added.

Convened by Sierra Leone’s President, Julius Maada Bio, the summit is scheduled for November 17 and 18 at the Julius Maada Bio International Conference Centre in Lungi. It will bring together governments, business leaders, project developers and development finance institutions to advance strategic regional investments.

The investment drive places project preparation and access to finance at the centre of West Africa’s integration agenda. Its immediate task is to connect viable proposals with institutions capable of financing their development, while aligning commercial opportunities with national and regional priorities.

Energy and transport connections, agricultural investment and digital networks are central to that ambition, offering opportunities to strengthen trade, expand production and improve access to markets.

The initiative also comes against the backdrop of efforts to develop major cross-border infrastructure, including the proposed $25 billion Nigeria–Morocco Gas Pipeline, also known as the African Atlantic Gas Pipeline.

Backed by the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS), the project is intended to carry Nigerian natural gas through several West African countries to Morocco, with potential connections to European markets.

The proposed gas link illustrates the scale of the region’s infrastructure ambitions and the importance of coordinating governments, project sponsors and financiers across national boundaries. It is a separate undertaking from the investment portfolio being assembled for the summit.

Elumelu’s involvement in the regional financing initiative coincides with the expansion of his interests in Nigeria’s energy sector.

According to Nairametrics, Heirs Energies Limited acquired an additional six million shares in Seplat Energy Plc on September 30, increasing the combined holdings of Heirs Energies and Heirs Holdings from 120.4 million to 126.4 million shares.

The acquisition raised their combined voting interest from 20.07 per cent to 21.07 per cent.

A separate analysis by the publication estimated that the combined market value of Elumelu’s holdings in Seplat, UBA and Transnational Corporation Plc rose by N684.59 billion between June and September, reaching approximately N2.43 trillion.

For the West African initiative, the next milestone is presenting the shortlisted projects to prospective financiers in Sierra Leone, where the proposed portfolio will be tested against investors’ financing requirements.

World.title: Makinde Will Defeat Tinubu in His 12 Battleground States, Others, Says Campaign Council
World.content:
• Challenges president to travel to Kaduna, Kano, Plateau, others by road

•Insists Nigeria’s biggest problem is grinding poverty, not religion

Chuks Okocha in Abuja

The Makinde-Daura Presidential Campaign Organisation (MDPCO) has declared that its presidential candidate on the platform of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), Governor Seyi Makinde of Oyo State, will defeat President Bola Tinubu in the 12 battleground states identified by the president, as well as in other states across the federation, in the January 2027 presidential election.

This is as Makinde declared that Nigeria’s biggest problem is grinding poverty, not religion, urging Christians to stop shunning politics and take an active role in transforming the country.

The MDPCO, in a statement by its Director of Strategic Communications, Hon. Richard Nnanna Ihediwa, asserted that Makinde would decisively defeat Tinubu and his All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council in Rivers State and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Abuja, insisting that no amount of political manoeuvring, intimidation or abuse of incumbency by the President’s henchmen can reverse the growing tide of opposition to his re-election.

The organisation said the arrogance and political overreach of President Tinubu’s inner circle had deepened public resentment and further weakened his electoral prospects.

It added that President Tinubu’s decision to personally visit and campaign in only 12 states — Oyo, Kaduna, Rivers, Plateau, Borno, Enugu, Bauchi, Sokoto, Delta, Kano, Adamawa and Lagos — further confirmed his apprehension over the mileage and foothold already achieved by Makinde with his RESET NIGERIA Agenda message in the aforementioned and other states of the federation.

“Mr President should know that his visit to these states, if he eventually does, will not in any way change the direction or the determination of the people to vote him out, given his unpardonable failures in office which have brought unprecedented hardship across the country,” the organisation said.

“President Tinubu has no meaningful achievement he can boast of in these and other states of the federation where Nigerians now refer to his government as ‘T-Pain’ following the suffering they have been subjected to by the policies of the Tinubu administration in the last three and a half years.”

The MDPCO challenged President Tinubu not to have a change of mind but to visit the states to face the people.

“We challenge President Tinubu to travel around the country by road and witness the decrepit state of federal highways, the squalor in which Nigerians live and the level of infrastructural decay across the country, while his government squanders trillions of Naira on white elephant projects and wasteful programmes.

“If President Tinubu believes he is popular as he claims, he should not stop at the rally ground or at the airport when he gets to any of the states. He should go beyond waving to a gathering of APC rented crowd and be bold enough to directly engage the people in the communities and towns to seek their votes, as the APM candidate, Makinde, has been doing since he started his campaign,” it said.

The organisation said the APM candidate had been engaging Nigerians with his clear-cut RESET NIGERIA message, focused on rebuilding systems and institutions that produce excellent outcomes rather than relying on sloganeering like President Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda.

“Nigerians are gravitating towards the core campaign pillars and proposals in Makinde’s RESET NIGERIA Agenda, which include the establishment of an all-inclusive, four-year transitional government of national unity with four priority pillars of education, economy, security and socio-political policies.

“Unlike President Tinubu’s visionless, thoughtless and rudderless rule characterised by crass arbitrariness, Makinde’s RESET NIGERIA Agenda offers data-driven strategies that revolve around tackling poverty through massive production; a security plan that prioritises intelligence gathering, social reorientation and decisive kinetic and non-kinetic actions; an education plan that focuses on expanding access to quality functional education; and institutional reform that emphasises inclusive governance and sincere public leadership.”

The campaign added: “Our campaign is proud to acknowledge that feedback from the field indicates that Seyi Makinde’s RESET NIGERIA Agenda is resonating with Nigerians, especially the youths, who not only see light at the end of the tunnel, but a bright sunny day under a Makinde-Daura presidency.

“President Tinubu is for the umpteenth time urged not to waste the nation’s resources on his ‘Nebuchadnezzar’ Campaign Council of failed politicians who, like the president himself, cannot attract votes from Nigerians,” the campaign said.

In a development, Makinde has declared that Nigeria’s biggest problem is grinding poverty, not religion, urging Christians to stop shunning politics and take an active role in transforming the country.

He said Christians could not afford to stand aloof from politics because it was dirty or because they should not serve under leaders who did not share their faith, stressing that national transformation required their active participation.

Makinde spoke yesterday in Abuja after receiving a Christian Icon Award at the Christian Association of Nigeria’s (CAN) 50th anniversary celebration.

The governor, the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential candidate, said Christians should draw lessons from biblical figures who accepted difficult assignments in pursuit of a greater purpose.

“It is typical for us to say, ‘Politics is dirty. I don’t want to be yoked with unbelievers’, and things like that. But we must look at biblical examples,” he said.

Makinde cited David, who, despite having been anointed king, served in the palace of Saul, from whom God had departed.

He said the biblical account should challenge Christians who believe they cannot serve under leaders of different religious persuasions.

“I will use this opportunity to encourage our Christian brothers and sisters across the country to rise and participate in the agenda to transform Nigeria and reset our country,” he said.

Makinde urged Christians to focus on the hardship confronting Nigerians rather than allowing religious differences to define their engagement with national affairs.

“Our problem is not primarily a religious one. Our problem in this country is poverty — grinding poverty,” he said.

“At this stage, we must focus on addressing the issues currently confronting us. Those are the challenges we need to tackle.”

World.title: Okonjo-Iweala: $2.4bn Subsidy Fraud Probe Triggered My Mother’s Kidnap
World.content:
Francis Ndubuisi in Abuja

The Director-General of the World Trade Organisation (WTO), Dr Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala, has recounted how her efforts to uncover an alleged $2.4billion fuel subsidy fraud in Nigeria led to threats against her and the kidnapping of her mother.

Okonjo-Iweala said the abductors demanded that she resign as finance minister and leave the country in exchange for her mother’s release.

She recounted the ordeal during an interview with Bloomberg’s Francine Lacqua on the Leaders programme, published earlier this week.

The former finance minister said the investigation began after officials noticed that claims submitted by fuel importers under Nigeria’s subsidy programme were increasing sharply.

Nigeria, despite being an oil-producing country, relied on imported refined petroleum products to meet domestic demand at the time.

Under the subsidy arrangement, importers received government payments that enabled them to sell petrol at regulated prices.

However, Okonjo-Iweala said the amounts being claimed had risen to levels that raised suspicion.

“So, I went to the president and said, look, something is going on here. Could we audit the accounts? And he said, ‘yes, go ahead.’ And we found about $2.4 billion worth of fraud. So, we refused to pay,” she said.

She said the decision triggered threats against her before her mother was abducted.

“I was told that for her to be released, I should resign and leave the country,” she said.

Describing the experience, Okonjo-Iweala said the five-day ordeal was among the most painful periods of her life because she feared that her actions could lead to her mother’s death.

“It was a terrible, terrible five-day ordeal. I think it’s the worst in my life,” she said.

She disclosed that her mother was held in a forest before escaping one night.

“She was held in the middle of a forest, and one night she escaped. She’s still alive. She’s 96 now,” she said, adding that her mother still becomes distressed whenever the incident is mentioned.

Asked whether she had considered quitting her job during the crisis, Okonjo-Iweala said she would have prioritised her mother’s life over remaining in office.

“Between my mother, having my mother alive and staying in a job, I would pick my mother any day,” she said.

However, she recalled that her father urged her not to surrender to the kidnappers’ demands.

“He said, ‘we don’t give in to blackmail.’ And he said, ‘you’ve got to carry on. You’ve got to go to work,” she recounted.

Okonjo-Iweala said she initially felt paralysed by fear and considered resigning to secure her mother’s release, adding that the experience left her with a sense of guilt that she still felt today.

“I never dreamt my parents could ever be touched in this way – that people would be that evil,” she said.

She added that her experiences over the years had made her more patient and helped her focus on finding solutions when confronted with difficult situations.

“I feel that this is a real fight that has to be waged. If you are a country that is not that rich, every single penny counts,” she said.

Okonjo-Iweala served as Nigeria’s finance minister under former President Goodluck Jonathan before becoming director-general of the WTO in March 2021.

Her mother, Kamene Okonjo, was kidnapped from her home in Ogwashi-Uku, Delta State, in December 2012.

The incident drew national attention amid concerns over the safety of the finance minister’s family.

World.title: French police probe into Hyron Andrews shock death
World.content:
The police in France have launched an investigation into the untimely and shocking death of 31-year-old South African rugby star Hyron Andrews.

FRENCH POLICE PROBE HYRON ANDREWS’ DEATH

The French police have launched an investigation into the death of 31-year-old Hyron Andrews, who died on Friday 16 October while on tour with the Lions in France. La Rochelle public prosecutor Arnaud Laraize confirmed told AFP that an investigation had been opened to find the cause of Andrews’ death.

Investigators are reportedly treating the incident as a suspected accident, with an autopsy set to be conducted.



“He was found unresponsive in a shower cubicle located in the hotel’s spa area. The shower was locked from the inside,” according to the prosecutor’s office.

“There are no signs of violence on his body, and the involvement of a third party is not currently considered a likely scenario. An investigation into the cause of death has been entrusted to the gendarmerie,” according to the prosecutor’s office.

WHAT WE KNOW ABOUT HYRON ANDREWS’ PASSING

The Lions confirmed the death of Hyron Andrews in a statement expressing their heartbreak and passing on their condolences to his family. Hyron was believed to have died after a fall at the hotel on the Île de Ré. This was the Lions base ahead of their Investec Champions Cup match against La Rochelle on Saturday 17 October.

Emergency services were reportedly called to the hotel shortly after 10:20am on Friday. However, attempts to resuscitate the rugby star were unsuccessful.

The Sun reports that Andrews was found unconscious in a shower cubicle at the team’s hotel on the Ile de Re, an island off France’s western coast.

“LIONS SADDENED BY THE PASSING OF STAR LOCK. It is with broken hearts that we mourn the passing of Hyron Andrews, a valued member of our Lions family. Our deepest condolences are with Maiglin, Hendrix, Emerson and the entire Andrews family during this incredibly difficult time,” read the post.



“Rest in peace, Hyron. You will always be part of our family. ❤️,” read the post.

World.title: Crime in this farming town could reach record-breaking levels
World.content:
Swellendam, nestled in the foothills of the Langeberg Mountains, is dealing with crime levels last seen more than a decade ago.

Crime in the Swellendam police precinct has increased 23.5% over 3 years. Criminal activity is also up in the municipality’s other police precincts.

Crime in Barrydale is up 34.9% and in Suurbraak 12%.



But what’s behind this record-breaking crime spree?

283-year-old town reeling from crime

Founded in 1743, Swellendam, a farming community in the Overberg, is falling victim to a common culprit in the Western Cape: drugs.

Swellendam doesn’t have the poverty levels present in other Overberg municipalities.



In Swellendam, most households live in formal dwellings and have access to formal ablution facilities.

Only 5.79% of the local municipality’s 47 114 people receive a Social Relief of Distress (SRD) grant. To qualify, the grant’s beneficiaries must live below the Food Poverty Line (FPL).

Theewaterskloof is the only Overberg local municipality where the percentage of beneficiaries is lower. Only 4.59% of residents in Theewaterskloof receive the grant.



In the Overstrand, 6.42% of residents receive the grant, and in Cape Agulhas, 8.2%.

The level of beneficiaries points to unemployment among working-age adults who could otherwise find work.

In Swellendam, the data suggests crime may not be linked to poverty but to drug dependence.



Drug-related crime has had the largest increase across multiple police precincts in Swellendam.

In Barrydale, for example, drug-related crime increased by 52% in the year ending March 2026.

In Swellendam, drug-related crime rose 44.6% over the same 12-month period.



In the first quarter, drug crime continued this trend, rising by 47.7% in Swellendam.

Drug crimes have a trickle-down effect, bringing with them a host of other crimes as dealers fight over territory and users support their habit.

In the full-year data, common and serious assault are increasing, as are residential burglaries.



In the year ending March 2026, theft rose 33.2% from the same period the year before. Common assault rose 30.8% and serious assault 26.7%.

While residential burglaries rose 41.3% over 12 months, they declined by 18.2% in the first quarter.

Record-Breaking Crime

In the year ending March 2026, crime in Swellendam’s largest police precinct reached a 10-year peak.



The last time crime was this bad in the town was in the year ending March 2015.

In the first quarter of this year, crime rose 8.2% in the Swellendam police precinct.

If crime continues its first-quarter trend, the Swellendam police precinct could reach record-breaking levels by March 2027.



In Barrydale, the situation isn’t as severe.

Crime peaked in the Barrydale police precinct in the year ending March 2016.

March 2026 data shows the town still reports 13.5% fewer crimes than at its peak.



However, crime isn’t under control in Suurbraak.

The town has had two record-breaking years in the past five years.

World.title: The daring Dunedin Star rescue off the Skeleton Coast in 1942
World.content:
Wreckage of the British Dunedin Star is still visible on the Skeleton Coast not far from the Kunene River mouth. Image: File/Fotor

All is quiet aboard the British Blue Star liner, the Dunedin Star, on 29 November 1942. En route from Liverpool to Egypt via Cape Town, the ship strikes a submerged reef off the Skeleton Coast near the Kunene River mouth. A part of her keel is suddenly ripped open with water streaming into the engine room.

The thing is its wartime in Europe and the Dunedin Star isn’t just carrying civilian passengers but valuable Allied munitions and military supplies, too. There are 107 passengers aboard and now they’re stranded on the most hostile shoreline on Earth.

DUNEDIN STAR SKELETON COAST RESCUE

Crew on the Dunedin Star get an SOS out, and Walvis Bay answers. The survivors who reach the beach, 63 people, three babies and a pregnant woman, now find a deadly desert on one side and a freezing, foggy Atlantic Ocean on the other, with scorching days in between. The other 44 stay aboard.



Help comes first by water. The South African tug Sir Charles Elliott and converted minesweeper Nerine steam north from Walvis Bay. The heavy surf and strong currents keep them from the beach and attempts to float supply rafts ashore failed. Then the tug herself runs aground on 3 December. Two of the crew die.

Next, a South African Air Force Ventura bomber flies from Cape Town to drop supplies. Most of what it drops is destroyed and lost on impact. The crew then makes a bold call to land and evacuate the stranded women and children. But the plane crash-lands into the desert’s salty crust and the rescuers needed rescuing, too.

SEA, AIR AND LAND RESUCE

An AI-generated depiction of what the Dunedin Star liner might’ve looked like in 1942. Image: AI generated, for illustrative purposes only

Meanwhile, a South African Police convoy led by Captain J.W.B. Smith has left Windhoek. Driving across endless Namib desert. Approximately 11 trucks struggle through the deadly dunes for days. The Dunedin Star rescue convoy eventually reaches survivors on the beach and begins to move them out.



All the survivors reach Windhoek on Christmas Eve, 26 days after the wreck. Not a single person aboard the Dunedin Star dies. However, the cost of the incredibly difficult rescue mission is one tug, one bomber, several army trucks and the lives of two tug crewmen.

In a wartime period defined by death and destruction, the Dunedin Star rescue stands out as a remarkable triumph of the human spirit over adversity. And the wreckage remains on the Skeleton Coast to this day …

But what do you think? Had you ever heard of the Dunedin Star rescue mission back in 1942? Please share your thoughts in the comments section below …

World.title: South Africa is ending support for ‘screwdriver’ car plants. Here’s what it means for jobs
World.content:
South Africa will phase out support for car plants that rely on imported vehicle assembly kits, to encourage more local manufacturing. Image: Pexels

South Africa will phase out support for car plants that rely on imported vehicle assembly kits.

Instead, the government wants carmakers to build more of their vehicles locally.

It’s a major shift for one of the country’s most important industries.



And it’s aimed squarely at creating more jobs.

Here’s what it means: the government wants to move away from plants that mostly bolt together imported parts, towards factories that manufacture more of each vehicle in South Africa, which typically creates more jobs.

Minister of Trade, Industry and Competition Parks Tau announced the change at SA Auto Week in Durban on Thursday, 15 October.

WHAT ARE VEHICLE ASSEMBLY KITS?

The change targets a process called semi-knocked-down (SKD) assembly.

In SKD assembly, carmakers import vehicle bodies and most of their components in kit form, then put them together locally. Plants like these are sometimes called “screwdriver” plants.

That’s different from completely knocked-down (CKD) manufacturing, where much more of the vehicle is built and sourced locally.



SKD assembly typically creates fewer jobs than full manufacturing, and is usually used for tax efficiency.

WHAT THE GOVERNMENT HAS ANNOUNCED

According to Tau, the government has agreed to:

Phase out existing SKD operations.

Stop providing policy support for any new SKD facilities.

for any new SKD facilities. Strengthen the legal definitions of what counts as CKD manufacturing.

“We will work to strengthen the legal definitions around what we determine as complete-knock-down manufacturing,” Tau said.

The changes won’t apply to medium and heavy commercial vehicles.

WHEN WILL THE CHANGES TAKE EFFECT?

That’s still unclear.

The Department of Trade, Industry and Competition (dtic) hasn’t given a deadline for the phase-out.

WHY THE CHANGE?

The announcement follows years of pressure from South Africa’s established carmakers.

Earlier this year, BMW Group South Africa chief executive officer (CEO) Peter van Binsbergen said the industry had urged the government to close what he called an SKD “loophole”.

Toyota South Africa Motors CEO Andrew Kirby said in July that the country’s car industry had moved beyond the need for SKD operations.

He warned that assembling vehicles from kits risked undermining larger investments in full-scale production.

WHAT IT MEANS FOR JOBS

The changes are part of the South African Automotive Master Plan, which sets out the industry’s goals for 2035.

The plan aims to:

Raise local content in vehicles to 60% , up from the current average of 38% .

in vehicles to , up from the current average of . Double employment in the sector.

in the sector. Increase South Africa’s share of global vehicle production to 1%.

Because full manufacturing involves more local work than kit assembly, the government hopes the shift will support more jobs over time.

WHAT ABOUT CAR PRICES?

Tau didn’t say how the changes could affect vehicle prices.

The dtic also hasn’t released any analysis of the possible impact on what South Africans pay for new cars.

WHAT ELSE IS CHANGING?

The government is reviewing the Automotive Production and Development Programme (APDP), the incentive framework for the car industry.

It’s working with the Automotive Business Council, as well as the National Association of Automotive Component and Allied Manufacturers and organised labour.

Tau also said the government would formally investigate the competitiveness of South Africa’s ladder-frame light commercial vehicle (LCV) segment, which includes pickups, or bakkies.

“We have agreed that the strategic competitiveness of South Africa’s ladder-frame LCV segment warrants formal investigation,” he said.
