World.title: Can Pirates and Sundowns meet in the CAF Champions League group stage?
World.content:
After an intense MTN8 final, football fans would love to see Orlando Pirates and Mamelodi Sundowns meet again in the 2026/27 CAF Champions League.

With both South African giants aiming to qualify for the 16-team group stage, some supporters have questioned whether the two teams could be drawn into the same group.

Unfortunately, Pirates and Sundowns cannot be drawn into the same CAF Champions League group if the competition’s rules prohibit clubs from the same national association from sharing a group.



The draw regulations determine how teams are allocated to the different groups.

The rules are designed to prevent clubs from the same country from meeting in the group stage, ensuring that teams from different national associations are represented across the groups.

Both South African sides are currently competing in the second preliminary round as they seek to secure places in the group stage.



Pirates and Sundowns eyeing group stages

Orlando Pirates faced Namibia’s African Stars in the first leg in Gaborone, securing a 1-0 victory to put themselves in a promising position ahead of the return fixture.

Mamelodi Sundowns, meanwhile, are scheduled to face Angola’s Wiliete SC away from home in their first-leg encounter as they look to take a step closer to qualification.

Should both teams advance to the group stage, they would be placed in separate groups under the applicable draw regulations.



An all-South African showdown between Pirates and Sundowns could still happen later in the competition. If both clubs progress beyond the group stage, they could meet in the knockout rounds, depending on the draw and the tournament’s regulations, or potentially in the final.

For now, both teams must first navigate the preliminary rounds before turning their attention to the possibility of another showdown on the continental stage.

Do you want the two teams to meet in the final?

World.title: Kaizer Chiefs coach Da Cruz failing to meet his mandate?
World.content:
Kaizer Chiefs suffered a 1-0 defeat to Red Arrows in the first leg of their CAF Confederation Cup second preliminary round tie, leaving Amakhosi with work to do in the return leg.

The Soweto giants will need to overturn the deficit at home to secure their place in the group stages of the competition. With their continental campaign hanging in the balance, the pressure is mounting on head coach Fernando Da Cruz.

The defeat was Chiefs’ second across all competitions this season, adding to concerns over their early-season performances.



Last season, Amakhosi failed to progress beyond the group stages of the CAF Confederation Cup. An early exit this time around would be another setback for a club desperate to re-establish itself among the continent’s top sides.

Kaizer Chiefs struggling

Chiefs’ disappointing start has already raised questions following their quarter-final exit from the MTN8. Combined with inconsistent league form, the loss to Red Arrows will have supporters increasingly concerned about the team’s direction under Da Cruz.

Failure to overturn the deficit in the second leg would intensify the scrutiny on the French coach, with the upcoming Soweto Derby against Orlando Pirates potentially becoming a crucial fixture for his future.



A victory in the derby could help ease some of the pressure and buy Da Cruz valuable time to improve the team’s league performances. However, another disappointing result would only deepen the concerns surrounding his tenure.

The Carling Knockout Cup also presents Kaizer Chiefs with an opportunity to salvage their campaign and compete for silverware.

With expectations always high at Naturena, Amakhosi will be under pressure to respond quickly and give their supporters something to celebrate.



For now, the immediate priority is clear: Amakhosi must produce a strong performance in the return leg against Red Arrows. Anything less could leave Da Cruz facing difficult questions about his future at the club.

Will Da Cruz survive?

World.content:
SASSA Child Support Grants in November 2026 will go ahead on this date. Image: AI generated, for illustrative purposes only

It’s some form of good news for SASSA Child Support Grants in November 2026. It has been announced that the 13-million recipients with children will receive their grants two days earlier than originally scheduled

Due to a previously unforeseen clash with local government elections in the first week of the new month, payments will now take place on Tuesday 3 November 2026. And not Thursday 5 November, one day after voting, as originally stipulated. Therefore, the payment gap reduces to 28 days from the last one.

SASSA CHILD SUPPORT GRANTS IN NOVEMBER 2026

As ever, the grant amounts for SASSA Child Support Grants in November 2026 are unchanged. No October top-ups went ahead this month:



Child Support pays R580 , up by R20 from R560 back in April 2026.

, up by from R560 back in April 2026. Foster Child pays R1 300 , up by R50 from R1 250 back in April 2026.

, up by from R1 250 back in April 2026. Care Dependency pays R2 400 up by R80 from R2 320 back in April 2026.

Don’t forget that you register your child with the Department of Home Affairs from the month of their birth, you can start claiming government money immediately. Calculated all the way to their 18th birthday, this is a benefit of roughly R185 000 in aid to the parents (inflation adjusted) till they’re no longer eligible.

INCOME ELIGIBILITY REQUIREMENTS FOR CHILD SUPPORT

13-million beneficiaries of SASSA Child Support need all the help they can get. Image: File

Likewise, applicants shouldn’t forget that the department has revised income eligibility requirements from the South African Social Security Agency. Previously, a single caregiver on Child Support could earn R5 100 per month and still qualify. Now that limit has increased to R5 800. While, for married couples looking after a minor, the figure increases from R10 200 to R11 600 per month.

Tallied up annually, that is R69 600 (single person) and R139 200 (couple). Note that there is no asset portion to the means test, like with SASSA Old-Age Grants. On a positive note, the agency also claims new maximum wait times of 90 minutes at SASSA offices. Thanks to self-service kiosks with Wi-Fi, beneficiaries can complete eLife and biometric verification in double-quick time and for free.

SAME-DAY SERVICE FOR CHILD SUPPORT

As such, the agency also says first-time applicants for SASSA Child Support Grants in November 2026 can be approved on the same day. Previously, the waiting period used to be closer to three months. However, you must have all your documents in order on your first visit. Here’s what you need to bring to your application appointment:

Valid identity documents (IDs) and birth certificates of you, your child and spouse (if married).

Proof of marital status (marriage, birth or death certificate of your spouse).

Proof of income (you and your spouse).

Certified three-month bank statement, not older than three months.

bank statement, not older than three months. Proof of address (a utility statement with your name on it that’s not more the three-months old).

If you don’t produce all the correct documents and copies, you may be sent away and asked to return. And if you are denied a SASSA grant, you have three months to lodge an appeal with the DSD HERE.

You can contact SASSA through the following channels for more information:



SASSA Toll-Free Call: 0800 60 10 11

SASSA Head Office: 012 400 2322

Email SASSA: grantenquiries@sassa.gov.za

Visit the SASSA Service portal HERE

But what do you think? Are you happy SASSA Child Support Grants in November 2026 moved two days early? Let us know in the comments section below …

World.title: ConCourt may have saved teary Mbabula's job
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The Constitutional Court ruling may have just saved Fikile Mbalula's job as ANC secretary general.

That's the word from Sunday Times Deputy Editor Mike Siluma.

The Apex Court ordered the IEC to include 181 of the party's candidates on ballot papers for next month’s municipal elections.

Mbalula was in tears after the ruling and later fainted while addressing the media.

"A lot of people understand why he had to break down in tears, because really, it would have been almost impossible for him to continue unchallenged in that position. And a lot of people were already blaming him, actually.

"But also, I was going to say, on the day, he would have been the most relieved and the happiest man, even though he fell ill. And he wants, know, there are always rumours that he wants to stand as the next president, you know. Now, if you are toughed out of office in a disgraceful way like that, that you lost us an election his chances of making a comeback would have gone up in smoke."

World.title: MK Party says leader is 'healthy and jovial'
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The MK Party said leader Jacob Zuma is doing well following his recent stay at St Mary's Hospital in Pietermaritzburg.

A statement released by the party said Zuma is back at work, attending to party matters.

Zuma's doctors diagnosed him with fatigue.

MK Party said they recommended that he takes time off to rest while they monitor his health.

They have described the former statesman as healthy and jovial.

World.title: Childhood vaccination in the spotlight
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Declining childhood vaccination rates are raising fears that diseases may return.

Earlier this year, researchers found two polio strains in wastewater in Cape Town.

Outbreaks of whooping coughs and measles have also occurred.

Experts said the biggest worry is that one in three children are left unprotected.

SANOFI South Africa's Diane Buron said the data is very telling.

"The vaccination rates for the first dose for children has dropped from 87% in 2019 to 67% in 2025. So that's a 20% drop in only six years and it means that today one in three children is completely unprotected against potentially serious diseases.

"So, it is a warning call to make sure that we protect our children in South Africa and that we make sure that they are vaccinated. What we see happening is disease coming back unfortunately. So, in even only the first seven weeks of 2026, over 160 cases of whooping cough were reported and over 5,000 cases of measles have been reported since the beginning of 2026.

"Even polioviruses have been detected in the wastewater in Cape Town. So, it's not an outbreak in the sense that no polio cases were detected in humans, but it is a very important warning sign that it is a real risk and if vaccination rates and if children do not get their vaccination."

World.title: Counterfeit goods worth more than R160m seized from Joburg CBD
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The National Counterfeit and Illicit Goods Unit seized counterfeit goods worth more than R160 million during a multi-disciplinary operation in the Johannesburg CBD this week.

Police spokesperson Colonel Amanda van Wyk said the team, with support from the Public Order Policing (POP) Unit in Pretoria, the South African Revenue Services (SARS) Customs Division, and brand protectors, executed search-and-seizure warrants at several identified shops located in a retail building.

"This resulted in the seizure of more than 62 000 counterfeit items including high-end branded clothing, footwear, cosmetics, watches, jewellery, and sunglasses.

"The operation forms part of ongoing nationwide efforts to dismantle illegal trade, manufacturing, and distribution of counterfeit and illicit goods in the country," she said.

World.title: 'No favours for connected friends' - Zille tells DA rally
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - DA Johannesburg mayoral candidate Helen Zille has declared war on corruption.

She has promised an independent investigation into alleged corruption, with public hearings and published findings, and calls for stronger protections for whistleblowers.

Speaking during her campaign for the city, Zille also called for stronger protections for whistleblowers.

"Joburg needs its own Madlanga moment We will initiate an independent investigation into the corruption that has crippled this city, with public hearings and published findings. We will act on the evidence from the Auditor General, from whistleblowers, the Zondo Commission, and others.

"We will rebuild this city's anti-corruption capacity, shield it from political interference, and do whatever is possible to protect whistleblowers.

And we will scrutinize city contracts, starting with the biggest and the most suspicious. We will open up procurement to public scrutiny. Who got the contract? Why? What were they paid? And what did they deliver? No more secret deals. No favours for connected friends. No work, no pay," she said.

World.title: 'Cockroach' party founder released from Indian police custody
World.content:
NEW DELHI - India's Cockroach Janata Party founder Abhijeet Dipke was released from detention on Saturday, a day after his arrest during a police crackdown on protests against the election authority.

Dipke, 31, was detained on Friday in New Delhi as he headed to join a rally that the CJP protest movement had called in the capital's central Connaught Place district.

He walked out of a police station on Saturday afternoon, waving to the media and giving a thumbs up as he was driven away, an AFP photographer saw.

"Abhijeet Dipke released," CJP legal affairs chief Ratna Singh said on social media.

Opposition parties and CJP activists have defied a security crackdown, rallying to demand the resignation of India's chief election commissioner after accusing the poll body of manipulating voter rolls to benefit Prime Minister Narendra Modi's ruling party.

The commission, which oversees voting in the world's most populous nation, has denied any wrongdoing.

Two other senior CJP leaders, Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das, were arrested on October 14 after entering Jantar Mantar, a decades-old protest site that police have declared off-limits for demonstrations. They remain in custody.

Members of Modi's Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party have long alleged that large numbers of undocumented Muslim migrants from neighbouring Bangladesh have fraudulently entered India's electoral rolls.

Rights groups and critics however say Modi's government has eroded democratic freedoms during more than a decade in power, citing pressure on journalists, civil society groups and political opponents -- allegations the government rejects.

World.title: Joburg Crisis Alliance sounds the alarm on city's problems
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The Joburg Crisis Alliance warns that Johannesburg cannot afford another five years of poor service delivery and crumbling infrastructure.

The alliance calls for stronger civic structures and greater community participation to hold the incoming city council accountable.

JCA co-convener Neeshan Balton said urgent action is needed to keep the city from sliding deeper into crisis.

The alliance met in Parkview earlier.

"It needs to now move beyond being a crisis alliance to something more formal to do the work that has been outlined here. Because the JCA itself must become a democratic organisation that must bring together people, that must build these civic structures.

"And when we build them, we need to make sure that all the education and advocacy work that we've spoken about here takes place across the length and breadth of the city.

"Because on the 4th, a new government comes into place in Johannesburg. They will be there for five years until 2031. Now, keep that in mind. 2031, we are going to be having these summits, and we will gather here in 2031. And very little would have changed besides having to pay more for very little. I don't think we can afford that. I don't think we can afford for this city to collapse."

World.title: Nepal floods 'defining moment' for climate action: UN
World.content:
KATHMANDU - Nepal's devastating floods should be a turning point for global climate action, with the international community helping the Himalayan nation recover, a top UN official told AFP on Saturday.

The country suffered one of the worst disasters in its history on August 26, when a mountain collapse near the China border triggered catastrophic floods that killed more than 1,400 people and left over 5,000 missing.

Scientists said climate change played a significant role in that disaster.

Jorge Moreira da Silva, executive director of the UN Office for Project Services (UNOPS), which implements humanitarian and development projects, said he had witnessed "massive devastation" during a visit to affected communities.

Nepal, a largely rural country of 30 million people that contributes little to global greenhouse gas emissions, estimates reconstruction will cost $4.78 billion.

"This is a defining moment not only for Nepal, this is a defining moment for the international community," Moreira da Silva told AFP in Kathmandu.

"It's not fair to ask a country that emits almost nothing of CO2 to suddenly pay alone the consequence of something that was not generated by the country," he added.

"That's why it's fundamental that global solidarity is brought to this equation."

- 'Climate justice' -

Moreira da Silva said reconstruction and resettlement must account for future climate risks, while the international community must "renew its commitment to climate".

"It's also about climate justice and climate responsibility," he said, warning that low-emitting countries would continue to bear the brunt of climate change.

"This is going to happen unless those countries that emit the most... change their pathway," he said.

Moreira da Silva said Nepal was rebuilding as global disruptions threatened food security. He also leads the UN task force for the Strait of Hormuz.

"The simultaneous disruption of the three maritime shock points... the Strait of Hormuz, in the Black Sea and in the Red Sea, poses a significant challenge, particularly on food security," he said.

The UN and its humanitarian partners launched a $49.6 million appeal last month to provide emergency assistance to flood victims.

Nepal's Prime Minister Balendra Shah told the United Nations last month that the flooding "was a warning to the world" about the growing dangers of climate change.

By Paavan Mathema

World.title: Kenya confirms third Ebola case
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Kenya has confirmed a third case of Ebola involving a 65-year-old woman who is a close relative of the first two patients.

The Ministry of Health, in a statement, said the woman developed a fever, sore throat and malaise while in quarantine, prompting her isolation and testing.

Her samples tested positive for Ebola at both the National Virology Reference Laboratory and the Kenya Medical Research Institute (KEMRI).

According to the Health Director-General Patrick Amoth, the patient has been transferred to an infectious disease unit, where she is receiving supportive care and being monitored.

“Having been in quarantine, she was diagnosed early and is currently receiving supportive care, improving her chances of recovery while limiting the risk of further spread of the disease,” the statement read.

The second patient, on the other hand, is in stable condition and responding well to supportive care.

The latest case brings the number of confirmed Ebola infections in Kenya to three.

According to the Ministry, of the 130 contacts identified so far, 127 had been traced and placed in quarantine, with efforts ongoing to trace the remaining three.

World.title: Motorists, households face fresh fuel price hikes
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

EPRA attributed the price increases to the escalating conflict in the Middle East. [FIle, Standard]

The Energy and Petroleum Regulatory Authority (EPRA) has increased fuel prices, raising the cost of super petrol by Sh12.93 per litre, diesel by Sh9.90, and kerosene by Sh28.49.

The new prices, effective from October 15 to November 14, 2026, will see motorists in Nairobi pay up to Sh226.96 per litre for super petrol, Sh227.76 for diesel, and Sh219.85 for kerosene.

EPRA Director-General Edward Mwirigi Kinyua attributed the price increases to the escalating conflict in the Middle East, which has disrupted petroleum supply chains and driven up the cost of importing fuel.

The rise in kerosene prices is likely to hit low-income households that rely on the fuel for cooking and lighting.

Meanwhile, higher diesel prices could raise the cost of transporting goods and operating public service vehicles, potentially driving up fares and commodity prices.

Diesel is a key fuel for the country's freight transport sector and a significant portion of public service vehicle operations, meaning the increase could have a ripple effect across the economy.

The latest review comes after EPRA maintained pump prices during the September 15 to October 14 pricing period, despite a decline in the cost of importing petrol.

World.title: Oburu Oginga to leave hospital soon - ODM
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

ODM SG Catherine Omanyo criticised bloggers spreading unverified information about the veteran politician.

ODM Secretary General Catherine Omanyo has dismissed social media reports about the health of party leader Oburu Oginga, saying he is recovering well and is expected to be discharged from hospital either today or tomorrow.

Omanyo criticised bloggers spreading unverified information about the veteran politician, accusing them of exploiting his health condition to attract online attention and increase engagement.

“It's unfortunate what I've been reading on social media. Those people who are seeking to have more likes or viewers, they will be disappointed because he's up, he's well, he's fine. In fact, he's headed home either today or tomorrow,” she said.

Omanyo insisted that the reports had exaggerated his situation, dismissing claims of his death and assuring the public that he was doing well.

She noted that health conditions could fluctuate, saying Oburu's position as ODM party leader had made his well-being a subject of heightened public interest.

“Everybody, everybody, including you and me, our health is not static. You can be under the weather any time. It's just that he's a party leader, and it makes breaking news,” Omanyo said.

She urged social media users to exercise restraint when discussing the health of public figures, warning against spreading unverified reports, particularly claims of death, before confirmation from credible sources.

Her remarks come amid growing speculation on social media about Oburu's health, with some users circulating unverified claims about his condition.

World.title: Kenya declares Ebola a formidable epidemic disease, sets new rules
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale, who declared Ebola caused by the Bundibugyo virus a formidable epidemic disease under the Public Health Act. [File,Standard]

Kenya has declared Ebola virus a formidable epidemic disease, introducing new rules governing screening, isolation, quarantine, contact tracing and the handling of bodies.

Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale issued the declaration through a legal notice published in the Kenya Gazette on Monday, October 12, under Section 35 of the Public Health Act.

The declaration follows Kenya’s confirmation of its first imported case of Bundibugyo Ebola virus disease on October 6, after a Kenyan citizen who had been living in the Democratic Republic of Congo travelled through Uganda to Nairobi. The patient died despite receiving supportive treatment.

The case prompted health authorities to trace people who may have come into contact with the patient and strengthen screening at points of entry.

In an update on October 12, the World Health Organization (WHO) said Kenya had listed 127 contacts, with 94 in quarantine, and screened more than 665,000 travellers at points of entry.

WHO also supplied protective equipment and testing materials worth about US$70,000 to support the response.

The government published two legal notices on October 12. Legal Notice No. 203 declares the disease a formidable epidemic, while Legal Notice No. 204 establishes the Public Health (Ebola Disease) Rules, 2026.

The regulations provide for screening at points of entry, medical assessment, isolation, referral, quarantine and monitoring.

They also assign responsibilities to transport operators, health facilities, medical practitioners and laboratories.

Health authorities will conduct investigations and contact tracing, while designated health facilities will manage suspected and confirmed cases. The rules also provide for the inspection and decontamination of premises.

The regulations cover the safe and dignified disposal of bodies, burial procedures, record-keeping, transportation and repatriation. They also address public communication, media houses’ responsibilities in public sensitisation and assistance from enforcement agencies.

The rules provide for offences and penalties, although the Gazette extract does not specify the penalties for individual violations.

What the declaration means

Bundibugyo virus disease is a form of Ebola that spreads through direct contact with the blood or other bodily fluids of an infected person or contaminated materials.

Contact with the body of someone who has died from the disease can also expose people to infection during unsafe burial practices.

Symptoms can include fever, fatigue, muscle pain, headache and sore throat, followed by vomiting and diarrhoea. The incubation period ranges from two to 21 days.

WHO says no approved vaccine or specific treatment currently exists for the Bundibugyo strain, making early detection, isolation, supportive care and contact tracing central to controlling its spread.

The health agency has advised against travel or trade restrictions on Kenya, Uganda and the Democratic Republic of Congo based on the information available.

The new rules establish a legal framework for managing the disease, from identifying suspected infections and monitoring contacts to caring for patients and preventing exposure during burials.

World.title: Ruto wades into growing ODM-UDA conflict
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President William Ruto marks Mazingira Day by planting trees in Elgon downs, Trans-Nzoia County. [PCS]

President William Ruto delved into the growing tension among Orange Democratic Movement (ODM) and United Democratic Alliance (UDA) contenders in the Coast and asked them to tone it down during his recent tour of the region.

Speaking hours before he wound up his eight-day tour, Ruto appeared to notice the widening cracks and told politicians within the two parties to embrace a ceasefire and unite against the opposition.

The head of state, who is facing a formidable challenge from the united opposition, warned that divisions in the ODM and UDA could weaken their team, whose union gives it a chance to win the 2027 general election.

“ODM and UDA are one team, and you should accommodate each other under a broad-based government. We should not allow divisions in ODM and UDA to undermine our unity of purpose,” he stated.

His statement appeared to be directed at the growing tensions among contenders, particularly in Kwale, Mombasa and Kilifi counties where prominent politicians face challengers within the ODM and UDA political union.

President Ruto’s earlier attempt to zone the region in favour of sitting governors is also blamed for the cracks in the broad-based team at the Coast.

In Mombasa County, UDA secretary general Mr Hassan Omar has already rejected a plan by the so-called broad-based team to support governor Abdulswamd Nassir’s re-election.

Omar, who is also a member of the East African Legislative Assembly (EALA) insisted that he will challenge Mr Nassir.

Already, businessman and EALA member Mr Suleiman Shahbal has quit ODM after he left he could not get the party ticket as the president's allies favour Nassir, a deputy party leader.

Shhabal has since aligned himself to former Laikipia governor Mr Murithi Nderitu’s Kenya Reform Party even as he insisted that he will be on the ballot.

In Mombasa, Mining, Blue Economy and Maritime Affairs Cabinet Secretary Mr Hassan Joho and governor Nassir appeared to be handing over Coast which was the ODM leader late Raila Odinga’s political turf, to President Ruto.

“This region stands with Ruto because he has dignified us with title deeds and many other development projects. We however expect him to support us when we seek the presidential seat in 2032,” Joho said.

Joho’s elder brother Abubakar Joho, who is a prominent businessman, has also joined the campaign for President Ruto.

While touring Kwale, Ruto addressed the growing noise among the main contenders, Governor Fatuma Achani (UDA), Prof Hamadi Boga and Engineer Lung’anzi Chai (ODM) after the broad-based leaders appeared to settle for Ms Achani who has the backing of Sports CS and former Kwale governor Salim Mvurya.

After witnessing the rising political tension, Ruto changed tone and told the three contenders to directly seek support from the voters rather than relying on external political backing.

In a complete change of heart and political tact, Ruto emphasised that the power to choose leaders ultimately belongs to the electorate, who will evaluate candidates based on their track record and development agenda for the region.

“You should all seek votes from the people and not rely on external backing. What I need from all of you is your support,” he stated.

For long, Governor Achani has enjoyed unwavering backing of President Ruto, Mvurya and recently Joho, who had preferred Kwale to be zoned in favour of the governor and UDA.

But Prof Boga, who has been Mr Joho’s ally, described the broad-based government’s zoning arrangement as undemocratic and a coercion to the Kwale electorate who he said should be allowed to choose their leaders without external interference.

Boga has been critical about the attempt to stop some aspirants from contesting seats in the broad-based government, noting that it was possible to zone candidates and difficult to do so for the voters.

In a statement, Boga noted that former Gender CS and Kilifi governor aspirant Ms Aisha Jumwa’s recent departure from UDA to Wiper Patriotic Front (WPF) reflected a growing sense among a segment of coastal leaders that decisions about their political future are increasingly being made elsewhere, then handed down as settled outcomes rather than negotiated realities.

“Zoning at the Coast is a fantasy: You can zone candidates but you cannot zone the voters,” Boga had warned.

“And if UDA and ODM are not paying attention to that signal, they may be underestimating the political consequences of their emerging arrangements at the Coast. “There is a dangerous assumption taking root in the broad-based arrangement: that coastal politics can be settled around a table in Nairobi and then delivered to voters as a finished political package. You take this seat, we take that one, and the voters will follow,” he added.

Boga, who came second in the 2022 governor poll, warned that if the Coast is mishandled, the problem will not necessarily be that voters have suddenly embraced another political formation, but the greater danger is that voters may decide that none of the established arrangements speak for them, creating either a rebellion or apathy.

In Kilifi County, the broad-based team publicly worked with Governor Gideon Mung’aro, forcing Ms Jumwa, his main challenger, to quit the government team in protest.

Kilifi Senate aspirant Mr Stephen Kahocho and Ganze parliamentary aspirant Ms Zawadi Kingi have publicly warned that they might be forced to quit UDA and vie as independent candidates or join other political formations.

This is after it emerged that the broad-based arrangement was behind Mung’aro (ODM), Kilifi senator Stewart Madzayo (ODM) and Ganze MP Kenneth Kazungu Tungule of Pamoja African Alliance (PAA), an affiliate of UDA.

World.title: Egypt reaffirms support for Iraq’s unity, sovereignty
World.content:
Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty reaffirmed Saturday, October 17, 2026, Egypt’s support for Iraq’s unity, sovereignty, national institutions and the principle of placing all weapons under state control.

Abdelatty made the remarks during a meeting Saturday with Ammar al-Hakim, head of Iraq’s National Wisdom Movement, on the sidelines of the 52nd session of the Organization of Islamic Cooperation’s Council of Foreign Ministers in Baghdad.

Foreign Ministry spokesperson Nader Zaki said Abdelatty underscored the deep-rooted fraternal ties between Egypt and Iraq. He also welcomed al-Hakim’s recent visit to Cairo, during which he met with President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi, and praised his role in promoting stability and political consensus in Iraq.

Abdelatty expressed hope that Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Faleh al-Zaidi would visit Cairo on Nov. 23 to convene the fourth session of the Egyptian-Iraqi Joint Higher Committee.

The meeting would seek to strengthen economic and trade cooperation and expand the participation of Egyptian companies in Iraq’s development and reconstruction projects.

He also stressed the need to accelerate coordination among technical committees under the trilateral cooperation mechanism involving Egypt, Iraq and Jordan to advance priority joint projects.

The meeting addressed regional developments, with Abdelatty emphasizing the importance of shielding Iraq from the repercussions of escalating tensions in the region.

The two sides also exchanged views on developments in Syria and Yemen and on maritime security and freedom of navigation, including in the Strait of Hormuz.

They stressed the need to de-escalate tensions, prioritize political and diplomatic solutions, and maintain Egyptian-Iraqi coordination to support regional security and stability.

World.title: Egypt’s Hamza Abdelkarim leads Barcelona Atletic to victory over Utebo
World.content:
Egyptian football player Hamza Abdelkarim led Barcelona Atletic FC to a 2–1 victory over Utebo on Saturday evening, in the seventh round of the 2026–27 Spanish fourth-division season.

Abdelkarim scored Barcelona Atletic’s opening goal against Utebo from the penalty spot in the fifth minute.

He was substituted in the 74th minute of the match.

The promising forward also featured for the Egyptian senior national team during the most recent international break.

World.title: Egypt urges dialogue to contain conflicts in Middle East, West Asia
World.content:
“Egypt called for intensified efforts to contain conflicts and prioritize dialogue and preventive diplomacy, particularly in West Asia and the Middle East,” Deputy Foreign Minister Mohamed Abu Bakr said on Saturday, October 17, 2026.

Addressing the seventh summit of the Conference on Interaction and Confidence-Building Measures in Asia (CICA) in Baku, Abu Bakr reaffirmed Egypt’s commitment to dialogue, state sovereignty and the peaceful settlement of disputes.

He said that the Palestinian Cause remained central to Egypt’s diplomatic efforts, including consolidating the Gaza ceasefire, facilitating negotiations and advancing an agreed roadmap to end the conflict. He also called for unhindered humanitarian aid to Gaza and rejected the forced displacement of Palestinians, stressing the need for a two-state solution.

Abu Bakr said Egypt was intensifying contacts with regional and international partners to ease tensions following the recent war involving Iran and reiterated Cairo’s condemnation of attacks targeting Gulf states.

He also urged stronger economic and investment ties between Africa and Asia.

World.title: Abdul El-Sayed disavows Muslim Brotherhood and criticizes implications that he has ‘dual loyalty’
World.content:
Michigan Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed on Saturday disavowed the Muslim Brotherhood, an Islamist political movement, during a heated exchange at a town hall.

El-Sayed, who could make history as the first Muslim elected to the Senate, has frequently faced Republican accusations that he is sympathetic to interests connected to Islamic terror. In recent days, Republicans including his GOP challenger, Mike Rogers, and President Donald Trump have commented about potential connections to the organization.

An attendee at a town hall in Caro, Michigan, repeatedly pressed El-Sayed about the Muslim Brotherhood, saying he had yet to hear the candidate reject the organization.

“Abdul, will you disavow the Muslim Brotherhood?” the man shouted from the crowd.

El-Sayed, after disavowing the movement, blasted the man for implicitly assuming his “dual loyalty.”

“You assume … that because I am Muslim, that somehow I would have some allegiance to something that is not our Constitution,” El-Sayed said. He later added, “For me, that Constitution is the guiding light.”

The audience member walked out after the exchange as the crowd cheered for El-Sayed.

The nominee has faced questions about potential connections to the organization. The latest attacks came after old tweets from El-Sayed’s half-sister resurfaced online, including a post from 2012 in which she described having “an amazing talk with my mom about her activism in the Muslim Brotherhood during the early 70s while she was in college.”

Earlier this week, El-Sayed denied allegations that he or his family has ties with the Muslim Brotherhood, telling reporters that to think that anybody in his family was part of the organization was “an insane thing to assume.”

El-Sayed has said he does not know what his mother was doing in Egypt during the 1970s, explaining he was 3 when his parents divorced and didn’t see his mother for years after being raised by his father and stepmother.

“They want to talk about me or point to my mom or my sister,” El-Sayed said on Thursday, adding, “I’m running for office. Judge me by my actions and my work.”

The Muslim Brotherhood is an Islamist movement with global offshoots that once wielded significant political power in Egypt, where it was founded. The movement officially rejects the use of violent means to secure its goals. However, offshoots of the group have been linked to attacks in the past.

Trump signed an executive order in November that initiated a process by which certain chapters or other subdivisions of the Muslim Brotherhood could be considered for designation as Foreign Terrorist Organizations.

El-Sayed has suggested that questions about supposed ties to the Muslim Brotherhood are rooted in bigotry.

“To insinuate that somehow, because of my Muslim faith, as somebody who might be the first senator who has that faith, that I would have anything but allegiance to the Constitution, that should be called into question,” El-Sayed said Sunday on MSNOW.

World.title: Deadly fire breaks out after ‘serious incident’ at Canada military base
World.content:
A major fire caused deaths and injuries at one of Canada’s busiest military bases on Saturday, sparked by an unspecified “serious incident.”

The fire began at the base in Wainwright, a town in eastern Alberta province, according to officials, and “spread rapidly due to high winds,” said the municipal district in a Facebook post Saturday evening. A call for assistance came around 4 p.m., according to the Wainwright Royal Canadian Mounted Police.

Defense Minister David McGuinty said in a video statement “that there have been both fatalities and injuries as a result of an incident on the base.”

He did not provide details about the number of casualties or what caused the initial blaze, but called it an “active and delicate situation” and said an investigation would be launched soon.

Late Saturday night, the municipal district said the fire was “being held at this time,” though fire crews will continue to monitor the area.

CFB Wainwright, located about 210 kilometers (130 miles) southeast of provincial capital Edmonton, is one of the country’s busiest Army bases, according to a government website. It houses the Canadian Manoeuvre Training Centre and the 3rd Canadian Division Training Centre. It’s also a training ground for Army field force units based in Edmonton.

Prime Minister Mark Carney confirmed the fire had stemmed from “a serious incident,” without specifying details.

Canada’s Prime Minister Mark Carney speaks at a Forever Canadian rally in Calgary, Alberta, on October 15. Jeff McIntosh/The Canadian Press/AP

A code orange, which designates an emergency response protocol for a high number of patients, has been declared in Edmonton, according to CNN’s newsgathering partner CBC, citing emergency department physician Dr. Warren Thirsk at the city’s Royal Alexandra Hospital.

“It’s a one in every 15- to 25-year disaster,” he said, adding that Wainwright’s healthcare centers have been “completely overwhelmed.” Patients are now being diverted to hospitals across Edmonton.

CNN has reached out to the Royal Alexandra Hospital, other Edmonton health centers, and Alberta Health Services for comment. CNN has also reached out to the military base, the Wainwright fire department, the Alberta premier’s office, and the municipal district.

The Canadian Armed Forces, the federal government, provincial and local authorities are cooperating “to mobilize all necessary support, and working through the details of what actually occurred,” McGuinty said.

Alberta Premier Danielle Smith called the disaster “significant and tragic,” saying it was “affecting many of our brave military personnel.”

No evacuation order has been issued. Authorities have asked residents to avoid the incident area, keep roads clear, and avoid visiting the Wainwright Health Center except for critical medical needs.

“I cannot recall such an incident in my short time for sure as a minister … I cannot recall an incident like this in recent memory,” McGuinty said in the video statement, responding to a journalist’s question.

Opposition leader Pierre Poilievre also wrote in a post that he had spoken to McGuinty and Carney about the fire, thanked emergency responders, and added: “Pray for Wainwright, everyone.”

This is a developing story and will be updated.

World.title: Israeli settlers attack group of European diplomats in the occupied West Bank
World.content:
Jerusalem — Israeli settlers attacked a group of European diplomats in the occupied West Bank on Saturday, one day after Israeli settlers attacked a group of European diplomats in the occupied West Bank on Saturday, one day after a Washington Post journalist was injured in another assault.

Settlers attacked the group of European diplomats in the village of Taybeh, a Palestinian Christian village east of Ramallah, according to Israeli media and Wafa, the official Palestinian news agency. The diplomats, local media reported, were from France, Belgium and Poland.

Belgium’s Foreign Minister Maxime Prevot slammed the attack and said it was a directly related to Israeli policies in the West Bank.

“As the occupying power, Israeli authorities must protect Palestinians, ensure the safety of diplomats and journalists, and bring those responsible to justice,” he said in a statement on X. “Impunity for violent settlers must end.” He said the group also included Catholic representatives.

Poland’s Foreign Ministry condemned the attack in a statement on social media, saying that they “expect the Israeli authorities to provide urgent and detailed explanations, identify those responsible and ensure that they are held accountable.”

“We are deeply outraged by this incident and condemn it in the strongest possible terms,” the ministry said. “Poland has consistently opposed violence perpetrated by Israeli settlers in the occupied West Bank. Attacks against members of the diplomatic corps are absolutely unacceptable.”

French Foreign Minister Jean-Nöel Barrot called the attack “outrageous” in a social media post, urging the Israeli government to arrest those responsible immediately.

In one video from the scene, a French official, identified as Aulnoye-Aymeries mayor Bernard Baudoux, is sitting on the ground outside a vehicle with a smashed window. In other videos, masked settlers – some armed with clubs or riding all-terrain vehicles – are blocking the roads and demanding identification.

Hussein al-Sheikh, Vice President of the Palestinian Authority, called on the international community to hold Israel responsible for the attack. “This is a miniature model of the scale of the daily terrorism to which our Palestinian people are subjected, and it requires a firm international stance that imposes international protection for the Palestinian people.”

Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Sa’ar said he strongly condemns “the severe acts of violence by Israeli rioters.” He said the foreign ministry was in touch with the ambassadors of the countries involved and was assisting law enforcement.

The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) said there were no soldiers in the area at the time of the attack, and the visit had not been coordinated with the military.

“The IDF strongly condemns the severe act of violence that took place in the area of Taybeh, during which diplomatic representatives were attacked by Israeli rioters,” the IDF said. Israeli police are investigating.

The settler attack on the diplomats comes one day after a different incident in which settlers attacked veteran Washington Post journalist Heidi Levine as she accompanied a group of Palestinians for the start of the annual olive harvest. Levine was hospitalized and required surgery after the assault, during which she said her camera and passport were stolen. She said the assault lasted about 10 minutes, even though she was clearly wearing a protective vest that identified her as press.

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who has repeatedly downplayed settler violence, tried to cast doubt on the attack. He said that Israel “unequivocally condemns violence against anyone,” but he issued no condemnation of the masked and armed settlers who were seen on video attacking Levine.

Despite clear and unequivocal condemnation from Sa’ar and Israeli President Isaac Herzog, who called the attack on diplomats “outrageous and shocking violence,” Netanyahu once again tried to question the veracity of Saturday’s settler violence, with his office saying in a statement on X that “SERIOUS ACCUSATIONS REQUIRE SERIOUS EVIDENCE.”

World.title: Buildings torched and over 1,000 detained after half a million protesters sweep France
World.content:
Riots broke out across major French cities on Saturday night as unrest spread beyond the capital, with government buildings torched and more than 1,000 people detained by police.

In the central city of Limoges, the historic town hall was set ablaze, with video showing its roof collapsing. In Marseille, black-clad protesters broke into city hall and defaced the building, and in Lyon, protesters torched the city’s tourist office, the Reuters news agency reported.

A fire destroys the city hall in Limoges, central France. Pascal Lachenaud/AFP/Getty Images

As night fell in Paris, groups of young people looted and started fires as protests ended, prompting police to respond with tear gas and baton charges in the narrow streets.

Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu said 1,200 people had been detained nationwide in the unrest, and condemned the “unacceptable levels of violence.”

The destruction followed what had been largely peaceful protests, which have grown out of sweeping student-led rallies that gripped parts of France last month, sparking a broader movement against crumbling schools, the spiking cost of living, and perceived government inaction. The rallies have become emblematic of long-simmering, intergenerational anger among people who say their calls for social and political change are going unmet by negligent governments.

Some 550,000 protesters hit the streets across France, including 110,000 in Paris, interior minister Laurent Nunez said. Organizers estimated an even higher turnout.

“There’s an accumulation of wealth and power that’s completely out of control,” one protester, who gave her name as Pauline, told CNN in Paris on Saturday.

“We’re also here to support the youth. There are victories, but if we look at the bigger picture, it’s not going in the right direction,” the 36-year-old added.

Another demonstrator complained of “less democracy” and a “concentration of power” under President Emmanuel Macron’s leadership. “There are billionaires who control the media,” Louise, 38, told CNN. “We are fighting to change things.”

Macron slammed “sowers of chaos” for interfering with peaceful protests, and warned late on Saturday that “those who have broken, attacked (police) prefectures, as well as businesses, looted even our town halls, will be prosecuted and punished.”

French police detain a protester during clashes prior to the start of a demonstration in Marseille, southern France, on Saturday, October 17, 2026. Thibaud Moritz/AFP/Getty Images

“We do not back down in the face of rioters and those who’ve come to attack law enforcement,” said the Paris Police Prefecture – the body that oversees the Paris Police Force, emergency services and various other administrative departments – adding that its staffers stood “their ground with courage and professionalism.”

The police response to the weeks of protest has come under scrutiny. Earlier in the week, that response had left a 14-year-old boy with a fractured jaw. Another police officer was captured on camera using a headlock on a girl in the northwestern area of Alençon, an action now prohibited by law.

A protester in the city of Saint-Étienne, about 40 miles southwest of Lyon, lost his hand during a march there on Saturday, a police source told CNN affiliate BFMTV. This is the second reported instance of a demonstrator losing their hand in the current wave of student protests.

A student in the northeastern city of Lens lost his hand after reportedly picking up a grenade earlier this month, prompting the temporary suspension of one type of stun grenade by police. That ban, which still allowed police to use several different grenades, has now been rescinded.

Overall, authorities said that the “vast majority of individuals” had demonstrated peacefully on Saturday, according to BFMTV.

Police officers charge at demonstrators at Place de la Republique in Paris on Saturday, October 17, 2026. Geoffroy Van Der Hasselt/AFP/Getty Images General view of the Place de la Republique as protesters walk through tear gas during a demonstration at the Place de la Republique in Paris on Saturday, October 17, 2026. Jack Taylor/Reuters

Posting on X, Jean-Luc Mélenchon, leader of the far-left La France Insoumise Party, emphasized that the majority of demonstrators on Sunday had made their point peacefully. “While news channels are flooded with images of violence in dozens of cities, everything is unfolding peacefully with tens of thousands of people calmly mobilized. Two worlds, two realities.”

Masked protesters raise their arms as they face off with French riot police during a demonstration in a street near the Gare du Nord train station in Paris on Saturday, October 17, 2026. Abdul Saboor/Reuters

Youth activists led solidarity protests in Belgium, Albania and Italy on Saturday as well.

Earlier this fall, high school students in France organized scattered protests demanding reduced class sizes, increased spending on teachers, investments in infrastructure designed to withstand the climate crisis and end to police violence against young people.

In the past decade and a half, a rise in fertility coupled with funding cuts has led to more students, but fewer teachers in classrooms. The French Education Minister Edouard Geffray has met with student protesters multiple times in recent weeks, although an agreement is yet to be made.

This story has been updated with additional information.

World.title: How Hegseth’s Pentagon tenure is shaping his possible political future
World.content:
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has rarely shied away from controversy, but his latest spectacle — announcing that the convicted Fort Hood mass shooter’s execution would be livestreamed — proved a bridge too far even for President Donald Trump.

While Trump pulled the plug on the broadcast Thursday, the episode underscores the risks behind Hegseth’s increasingly provocative public persona — one that some of his closest advisers believe could carry him all the way to the White House, but which others caution could jeopardize his possible political future.

Hegseth’s push to livestream the execution of Nidal Hasan by firing squad initially surprised Trump, as CNN has previously reported. Two Trump advisers described the move as an attempt by Hegseth to play into the impulses of Trump and the MAGA base. But Trump’s eventual decision to backtrack on the idea amid bipartisan backlash was also viewed by some inside the administration as a blow to Hegseth — and a warning about the combative, made-for-TV image he has cultivated at the Pentagon.

Still, Hegseth’s push to livestream a public execution overlaps with his future political ambitions, two sources familiar with the matter told CNN. The livestream was “pure id,” one of the sources said, noting how it comports with Hegseth’s eye for theatrics as a former TV personality who believes he knows what resonates with the American public.

Conversations with more than a dozen current and former administration officials, Trump allies, Republican operatives and people familiar with Hegseth’s political orbit reveal a defense secretary who, while never holding elected office, is taking steps that could set up a political future. He has cultivated a macho public image, empowered a small group of media-savvy advisers and tested messages that appeal to the MAGA base — even as his record at the Pentagon and his appetite for controversy threaten to narrow his path.

As he’s sought to craft his “warrior” image, Hegseth has surrounded himself with former Fox News producers and social media personalities — chief among them his wife, Jennifer Hegseth. Sources said that group wields outsized influence within the shrinking circle of advisers he still trusts.

Many of those advisers have encouraged Hegseth to consider political office — including a possible presidential run in 2028, sources said. Their argument: The two main alternatives, Vice President JD Vance and Secretary of State Marco Rubio, may not run and face an uncertain path to the nomination. Hegseth, they believe, should keep his options open.

“A lot of them are all in,” said one administration official who supports Hegseth’s political ambitions. Many of those closest to Hegseth are focused on his political future in part because they see elected office as one of his few viable options after the Pentagon, the source added.

His closest advisers also argue that Hegseth has the “look” of a candidate and presents a stronger image than some of the other likely contenders to replace Trump. However, some also acknowledge the criticism his overhaul of the Pentagon has sparked, and that his consistently combative attitude toward those who question his views or policies present headwinds toward winning over the electorate.

Unlike Vance, who has served as the Republican Party fundraising chair this past year, and Rubio, a 2016 presidential contender, Hegseth also lacks deep connections to the donors needed to mount a White House bid. Meanwhile, a super PAC close to Texas Sen. Ted Cruz remains active as he publicly flirts with another presidential campaign.

Vice President JD Vance, Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth attend a bilateral meeting with President Donald Trump and German Chancellor Friedrich Merz, in the Oval Office of the White House on March 3. Win McNamee/Getty Images

Some Trump allies told CNN they believe Hegseth would entertain a 2028 presidential bid only if Vance decided not to run.

Vance has the inside track to get Trump’s support — choosing a potential successor was part of the calculus in selecting the Ohio senator as a running mate in 2024 — and Hegseth would face a steep climb without the president’s backing, sources added.

NBC News first reported on Hegseth’s private discussions about a possible 2028 run in August. At the time, Hegseth called the report “100% false.”

In response to CNN’s questions for this article, Pentagon press secretary Kingsley Wilson said in a statement that “Secretary Hegseth is not running for president, and his only priority is leading the War Department.”

Chief Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell in a statement said that Hegseth had “not once” discussed any of what CNN was reporting. “As one of Secretary Hegseth’s senior advisors, I can attest that he spends every single day working to protect the nation and give our service members everything they need to be successful,” Parnell said.

While Hegseth’s image and blunt style have obvious appeal with a MAGA base that will be looking for a future home after Trump’s presidency, his oversight of the Iran war is a significant challenge. America’s latest military campaign in the Middle East is deeply unpopular with voters, and polls show it driving down support for both Trump and Republicans in the midterms.

Hegseth’s political activity — including traveling to Iowa earlier this year to rally for a GOP House candidate — has helped fuel speculation that he could someday run for office.

His political movements are watched with increasing interest in Tennessee, where his family moved several years ago, though GOP sources there say he has not taken steps in the state yet that might suggest he harbors political ambitions there.

“We’re very proud that he is serving us,” said Scott Golden, chairman of the Tennessee Republican Party. “And I would just say I hope he considers running for office at some point, at some level, whatever level he wants to do.”

The making of a ‘warrior’

Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth lifts weights as he meets with troops at the US naval base at Guantanamo Bay, Cuba, on June 10. Phil Stewart/Reuters

Hegseth has focused much of his efforts at the Pentagon on crafting a particular public image for himself, based around the idea he is leading a charge to root out so-called “woke-ism” from the military.

At times referred to inside the Pentagon as the Secretary of Culture War, Hegseth’s priorities have included slashing the number of generals in the military, changing the Department of Defense to the “Department of War,” and even creating a screening program for “testosterone deficiency.”

“We are no longer the woke department or the weak department. Simple translation of that? No fatties, no trannies, no beardos, no weirdos, no wimps, no radicals. Just warriors,” Hegseth said at a September “State of the Force” speech. “The ideological clowns are out. The patriotic cowboys are in — with testosterone testing on top.”

In what is seen as an effort to manufacture the specific public image he wants, Hegseth has largely insulated himself from the press and often declines to answer questions on his decision-making. Press conferences held near the beginning of the war with Iran began on many occasions with Hegseth’s ranting against the press and reporters’ coverage of the conflict, which he found to be “incredibly unpatriotic.”

The Pentagon has also taken on a more political tone in some of its public messaging, particularly on X, where an official Defense Department Rapid Response account dedicates itself to sharing images of Hegseth and snippets of his speeches.

Several far-right social media personalities and accounts — including at least two active-duty Army officers— routinely and vigorously defend Hegseth’s decisions and attack his critics on X. (This despite strict regulations for how service members can conduct themselves online.) Several of the individuals are employed at the Pentagon and many in the building see the small group as an online army tasked with influencing public perception of Hegseth and his policies.

Hegseth has repeatedly insisted his overarching goal is to make the military more “lethal” by removing guardrails intended to prevent things like civilian casualties and by endorsing legally dubious combat operations — including some that have prompted allegations of war crimes.

Those moves have garnered criticism from officials both inside the Pentagon and elsewhere within the Trump administration. But they appear to have also helped Hegseth maintain the one relationship that matters most if he envisions some sort of political future for himself: the president.

Secretary of DefensePete Hegseth walks near President Donald Trump before departing for Baltimore County, Maryland, on October 6. Jonathan Ernst/Reuters

While Trump has remained a steadfast defender of Hegseth, others close to the president — including some in the West Wing — are less enthusiastic, sources familiar with the matter told CNN.

Hegseth has been at the center of controversies even before the execution livestream, many of which the White House has brushed off, but some have left a lingering unease among White House officials and even some other Cabinet members.

One such issue is the Signal chat scandal, in which Hegseth shared specific operational details with senior administration officials in a Signal messaging app just hours before the US military carried out strikes on Houthi rebels in Yemen. His messages laid out exact timelines and target surveillance prior to the March 15, 2025, operation. Unbeknownst to Hegseth and the group, the editor-in-chief of The Atlantic was part of the chat.

The president’s then-national security adviser Mike Waltz took the brunt of Trump’s ire following the controversy, but many advisers thought at the time Hegseth should have faced stronger repercussions.

“These people have long memories,” one Trump adviser told CNN.

Hegseth’s eagerness to go to war with Iran and his removal of high-ranking military officials have also put him at odds with some senior advisers to the president.

In the immediate lead-up to the first bombs being dropped on Iran, Hegseth was one of the biggest cheerleaders for military intervention.

While the debate played out internally, Hegseth not only validated Trump’s idea to move forward, he downplayed the inherent risks of the conflict spiraling, CNN reported at the time — a reality that’s now come to fruition.

White House principal deputy press secretary Anna Kelly said in a statement that the White House and Pentagon “are fully aligned on ensuring justice is brought to evil traitor Nidal Malik Hasan who killed 13 innocent people.”

“Secretary Hegseth is doing a great job leading the Pentagon — and the results of Operations Epic Fury, Absolute Resolve and Midnight Hammer speak for themselves,” she said, referencing US military operations in Iran and Venezuela.

The episode over the Fort Hood shooter has resurfaced some of these frustrations over Hegseth’s movements. And, notably, it was Vance, whose own 2028 ambitions cast a shadow over all possible contenders, who was among the first to publicly express doubt about Hegseth’s plans to livestream an execution.

“I mean, look, if it’s all through live stream, I’m not going to be watching it,” Vance said.

In search of a political home

Pete Hegseth, then a Republican Senate candidate, in March 2012. Bruce Bisping/Star Tribune/Getty Images/File

A turn to politics would not be new for Hegseth. Before joining Fox News, he ran for Senate in Minnesota in 2012, when he was leading a conservative veterans’ advocacy group.

An adviser for Hegeth’s Senate campaign told CNN that while Hegseth was a young candidate at 32 years old, he had natural talent on the campaign trail.

“Pete was great on the stump,” said the adviser, who requested anonymity to candidly discuss Hegseth’s Senate campaign. “He’s one of those people that when he’s talking to you, he’s talking to you. He has an amazing ability to do that. His eyes are focused on you.”

But Hegseth ultimately dropped out of the race after the Minnesota GOP convention that year, when he lost the party’s nomination to Kurt Bills, as a candidate who eschewed 2012 GOP presidential candidate Ron Paul’s libertarian-leaning ideology.

Hegseth now owns a home in Tennessee, a state much more amenable to Trump’s brand of politics.

Trump held a rally last weekend in Clarksville, Tennessee, where questions about Hegseth’s political future have at times become fodder for speculation for his post-Pentagon career. That speculation has intensified at times, like when Hegseth’s nomination was jeopardized by revelations about a past accusation of sexual assault — which Hegseth has repeatedly denied — and during early scrutiny of his uneven start as defense secretary.

But GOP officials there say Hegseth hasn’t made any moves that would suggest he’s eyeing a run for office there.

“I, for one, would love him to run for office at some point in the future. But honestly, there’s not been a lot of talk,” said state Rep. Aron Maberry of Clarksville, Tennessee. “But we love him. And we are excited that he’s in DC in the Department of War and a Tennessean.”

A senior GOP official in the state said that other than some rumors and intrigue, there was never any serious discussion about Hegseth potentially running for governor or senator back when his confirmation vote in the Senate was in jeopardy.

The official never got the sense that Hegseth or anyone close to him was lining up support from county chairs or that there was pressure coming from Washington to help him find a safe landing spot.

Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth speaks at the 2026 International Christian Media Convention in Nashville, Tennessee, on February 19. Seth Herald/Reuters

He could have the same challenge turning to Tennessee politics now, should he leave the Pentagon.

“His biggest challenge is, he’s a Minnesota guy, he’s a DC guy, he doesn’t have real Tennessee ties,” said Steve Gill, a conservative political commentator and editor and publisher of TriStar Daily, a digital media publication in Tennessee. “He has work to do if he wants to create that base of connections and support. I’m not seeing any indications yet that he’s doing that.”

At Trump’s Tennessee rally, Hegseth received mostly rave reviews from the MAGA faithful. Many attendees CNN spoke with had close ties to nearby Fort Campbell and approved of Hegseth’s military overhaul.

Kris Grempler is the owner of a school that teaches members of the 160th Special Operations Aviation Regiment how to drive armored vehicles. Speaking to CNN at Trump’s rally, he said that morale among service members is noticeably improved since Hegseth took over the Pentagon.

“I love him to death. You know, getting to see him like do PT and stuff with these guys still, like he’s just — he’s a guy’s guy. And these troops love that,” Grempler said.

Emily Vierra, 47, a teacher at a Department of Defense school at Fort Campbell, said she thinks Hegseth could have a future in politics. “I can see it 100%. I can see him doing it in a heartbeat,” she said. “He’s a great communicator, able to deliver and relay the message in a way that resonates with people.”

“I don’t think he needs to change a thing,” Vierra said as she waited for Trump to arrive in Clarksville. “I think he needs to be authentic and true to who he is.”

But there was also some skepticism at Trump’s Tennessee rally. Hunter Meade, a 22-year-old server from Nashville, said that Hegseth struck him as overly performative, pointing to the defense secretary’s appearance in Memphis during a National Guard deployment earlier this year. He also found the animated comedy series South Park’s recent portrayal of Hegseth as a social-media obsessed brute amusingly accurate.

So while Meade said he’d keep an open mind if Hegseth ran for office, he has his doubts. “Do I care for Pete Hegseth as a person or as a leader? Not particularly,” Meade said. “I think he’s more like for show.”

World.title: Liberia: LAA Unveils $59 Million Modernization Plan Under Hughes’ Leadership
World.content:
Five-Year Strategy Targets Aviation Safety, Airport Security, Financial Reforms and Domestic Connectivity

By Gerald C. Koinyeneh

Monrovia — The Liberia Airport Authority (LAA), under Managing Director Ernest Hughes, has outlined a five-year, US$59 million modernization plan aimed at addressing critical aviation safety gaps, improving airport services, strengthening financial management and expanding domestic connectivity.



The LAA Strategic Plan 2027–2031, themed “Modern Airports. Connected People. A Stronger Liberia,” positions Roberts International Airport (RIA) as the centerpiece of efforts to establish Liberia as a competitive aviation and logistics hub in West Africa.

The plan acknowledges longstanding challenges, including outdated navigation systems, inadequate emergency equipment, airport encroachment, weak financial controls and limited revenue diversification. It proposes measurable targets and institutional reforms, but implementation will depend on financing, procurement and sustained management oversight.

US$59 Million for Five Priorities

The strategy distributes its proposed investment across five areas:

US$18.5 million for aviation safety and navigation;

US$15 million for revenue diversification and cargo logistics;

US$12 million for airport security and perimeter protection;

US$9.5 million for passenger services; and

US$4 million for governance and enterprise resource planning.

The LAA proposes financing the program through a combination of public-private partnerships, development-bank financing, donor grants, government allocations and internally generated revenue.

The plan identifies more than US$8 million in European Union funding secured for safety, security and critical infrastructure improvements at RIA.

Its proposed financing model aims to reduce dependence on government appropriations, although the authority will need to secure commitments and demonstrate sound financial management to attract the necessary investment.

Safety Gaps Top the Agenda

The most urgent challenge identified in the plan is aviation safety and regulatory compliance.

The document cites a 2022 international aviation audit score of 27 percent, well below the global benchmark of 75 percent. It also identifies the destruction of the airport’s Doppler Very High Frequency Omnidirectional Range (DVOR) navigation system, the absence of a functional air traffic control voice-recording system and inadequate firefighting capacity.

According to the plan, RIA has two obsolete fire trucks, compared with four identified as necessary to meet applicable requirements. The loss of navigation infrastructure has also forced aviation personnel to rely on operational workarounds.

The proposed US$18.5 million safety allocation would fund replacement navigation equipment, a modern Instrument Landing System, upgraded air traffic control communications, runway safety improvements and modern fire and rescue apparatus.

The LAA is targeting international certification by the fourth quarter of 2027. That goal, however, depends on completing corrective measures and satisfying regulatory requirements.

The Liberia Civil Aviation Authority (LCAA) retains responsibility for certification decisions, while the LAA must provide and maintain the infrastructure and systems needed to meet applicable standards.

The division of responsibilities makes coordination between the airport operator and regulator essential as the deadline approaches.

Security and Perimeter Protection

The plan allocates US$12 million to strengthen airport security, including perimeter fencing, surveillance, signage and passenger and cargo screening.

It identifies illegal land occupation, community encroachment and informal settlements around RIA as potential vulnerabilities that could expose airport operations to unauthorized access, wildlife hazards and foreign object debris.

The authority also intends to work with communities and wildlife management specialists to reduce hazards around operational areas.

Delivering these improvements will require effective coordination with security agencies, careful procurement and progress in resolving land-related disputes.

Passenger Services and Cargo Development

Despite improvements to RIA’s passenger terminal, the strategic assessment identifies congestion, unreliable air conditioning, inefficient baggage handling and maintenance shortcomings.

The proposed US$9.5 million passenger-services investment would support digital check-in, improved passenger movement, upgraded commercial spaces and lounges, and digitized parking operations. The authority also plans to strengthen performance requirements for concessionaires and ground handlers.

Alongside these improvements, the LAA intends to develop RIA into a specialized cargo and logistics hub, using US$15 million to expand revenue-generating activities and cargo-handling capacity.

Proposed investments include temperature-controlled storage for agricultural products, seafood and other perishable exports. The strategy builds on the existing Roberts Air Cargo Center, operated through a public-private arrangement involving Global Logistics Services and National Aviation Services.

The plan argues that improved cold-chain facilities could reduce post-harvest losses and help Liberian producers reach overseas markets. However, success will also depend on reliable electricity, export certification, appropriate handling standards and coordination with producers and relevant government agencies.

The LAA projects that non-aeronautical revenue will increase from less than 15 percent of gross income to more than 45 percent by 2031. Achieving that target would reduce reliance on passenger traffic and aviation-related charges, but will require commercial investments that generate sustainable returns.

Financial Reform and Accountability

The plan identifies manual accounting, procurement delays, weak internal controls and limited performance monitoring as obstacles to institutional efficiency.

It states that the authority has completed a physical asset verification and established a fixed-asset register. It also reports that IFRS-compliant financial statements were produced in 2027 for the 2024 and 2025 financial years.

The next proposed step is an Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) system integrating finance, procurement, human resources and airport operations. The system is intended to strengthen reporting, reduce revenue leakages and improve expenditure controls.

Additional measures include a board-level governance, risk and compliance committee, a specialized legal and regulatory unit, stronger procurement safeguards and independent governance audits.

The LAA also proposes a Program Management Office to coordinate implementation and monitor performance. Under its results-based management framework, departmental heads would report quarterly against defined indicators, with corrective action required when targets are missed.

The LAA Strategic Plan 2027–2031, launched under Ernest Hughes’ leadership, themed “Modern Airports. Connected People. A Stronger Liberia,” positions RIA as the centerpiece of efforts to establish Liberia as a competitive aviation and logistics hub in West Africa.

Reviving Domestic Airports

These mechanisms could improve accountability, but their effectiveness will depend on reliable reporting and the authority’s willingness to address persistent underperformance.

Beyond RIA, the strategy proposes public-private partnerships and Build-Operate-Transfer arrangements to rehabilitate and operate five secondary airports: Harper, Greenville, Zwedru, Voinjama and Foya. Improvements would include runway and apron rehabilitation, terminal upgrades, perimeter fencing and safety equipment.

Foya receives particular attention because of its proximity to Guinea and Sierra Leone and its potential connection to the Mano River Union Hub.

To attract investors despite limited traffic, the plan proposes viability-gap funding to help cover initial financing and commercial challenges. It also outlines revenue-sharing arrangements under which private operators would retain a larger share of aeronautical revenue in the early years before progressively sharing non-aeronautical surpluses with the state.

The strategy further envisages requiring a selected private operator to establish and operate a domestic and regional airline.

Such a model could improve connections between Monrovia and other parts of Liberia, but it raises questions about route profitability, public financial exposure and the capacity to enforce concession terms. Transparent procurement, rigorous due diligence and clear performance obligations will be critical to protecting public assets.

Workforce and Energy Modernization

The plan recognizes that infrastructure investment must be matched by a technically capable workforce.

Training priorities include aviation security, fire and rescue, safety management, engineering maintenance and technical services aligned with International Civil Aviation Organization and International Air Transport Association requirements. A proposed Human Resource Information System would help track staff qualifications and recurrent training.

The authority also plans to modernize internal electrical distribution systems and explore solar and other renewable energy solutions. Reliable power is essential for navigation equipment, screening systems and terminal operations, while reduced dependence on diesel generators could improve resilience and lower operating costs.

Hughes’ Implementation Challenge

Despite its wide-ranging ambitions, the plan acknowledges significant constraints, including limited departmental budgets, staffing shortages, outdated equipment and uncertainty over sustained financing.

An internal assessment cited in the document gave confidence in the LAA’s ability to become a leading West African aviation hub within five years an average score of 4.88 out of 10. Only 29.4 percent of respondents expressed high confidence in that prospect. Departmental budget adequacy scored 2.5 out of five, while confidence in readiness for an unannounced aviation regulatory audit scored 2.8.

The findings underline the gap between the authority’s ambitions and its current capacity.

For Hughes and his management team, early tests will include restoring critical navigation systems, improving firefighting capacity, strengthening perimeter security, maintaining credible financial records and demonstrating measurable progress toward certification.

The authority must also ensure that public-private partnerships are competitively awarded, financially viable and structured to protect the government’s long-term interests.

The LAA’s proposed US$59 million program is distinct from the broader US$250 million aviation-sector investment projected under the civil aviation master plan; the figures represent different levels of planned investment.

If implemented effectively, the strategy could improve safety, expand domestic connectivity, support agricultural exports and give the authority a more sustainable revenue base. But those gains will depend on financing, execution and accountability—not the plan alone.

For Hughes, the central challenge is to turn the five-year roadmap into demonstrable results: safer airports, more reliable services and a financially stronger LAA.
