What the Minority Asked For

The Minority is the opposition bloc in Parliament, and its Foreign Affairs Committee ranking member, Samuel Abu Jinapor, spoke for it on Thursday 8 October. He said Ablakwa ought to brief the House “as a matter of urgency” once Parliament resumes.

Jinapor accepted that membership could bring alternative financing and wider trade links, but warned of implications that “may be adverse to the national interest”. He asked why Ghana was not following Nigeria, a partner country and member of the New Development Bank, which limits its exposure.

Ablakwa answered on 10 October that the previous government had also studied BRICS, quoting a report that recommended Ghana “express prospective interest in joining the bloc”. He accused the Minority of double standards, according to 3News.

Ayariga’s Five Demands on 17 October

In a statement dated Saturday 17 October 2026, Ayariga asked who gave Cabinet the authority to decide for “over 34 million Ghanaians” without parliamentary and public consultation. He cited Article 1(1) of the 1992 Constitution, which places sovereignty in the people of Ghana.

He called on the government to publish a policy document setting out the objectives, benefits, risks and obligations of participation. He also asked for the proposal to go to Parliament for debate and any approval the Constitution requires.

His remaining demands are a transparent consultation with political parties, civil society, economists and business groups, and the release of the constitutional and legal assessment behind the decision. He also wants a guarantee that any arrangement protects Ghana’s economic independence and sovereignty.

Ayariga urged the Speaker and all members of Parliament to demand a comprehensive briefing from the Foreign Minister on the economic case, risks and legal obligations. He added that Ghana “is not for sale” and that Parliament must not be left as a spectator.

What the Constitution Says About Treaties

Article 75 of the 1992 Constitution lets the President execute treaties, agreements or conventions in the name of Ghana. Any such instrument is subject to ratification by an Act of Parliament or by a resolution supported by more than half of all members.

Article 76 says the Cabinet assists the President in determining the general policy of the Government. Ayariga argues that if the BRICS arrangement counts as a treaty or agreement, ratification applies, and that even if it does not, the matter deserves debate.

None of the coverage reviewed says whether a partner-country application would legally count as such an agreement. That question is for lawyers and Parliament, and no court or government lawyer has addressed it in the sources we found.

Ablakwa Answers on the US Question

Speaking on JoyNews’ Newsfile on 17 October, Ablakwa rejected warnings that BRICS ties could invite American penalties. He said Trump himself was dealing with BRICS countries, citing a diesel arrangement with Russia that MyJoyOnline says was announced on 9 October.

That deal is Ablakwa’s example and we have not independently confirmed its terms. He also linked the bid to the non-aligned vision of Ghana’s first president, Kwame Nkrumah.

MyJoyOnline’s 12 October analysis noted that Trump’s earlier 100% tariff threat concerned a currency to replace the US dollar, while the 10% threat referred to “anti-American policies”. It said neither threat establishes a tariff that applies automatically to a country seeking BRICS status.

The same analysis reported that four of Ghana’s five largest export destinations in 2025 were BRICS members: the United Arab Emirates, India, South Africa and China. That trade pattern is part of the government’s case for closer ties with the bloc.

What It Means for You

US exporters and investors face no new rule today, because Ghana has announced an intention to apply and no admission has been reported. The risk to watch is how Washington reads any later steps, since the tariff threats were written in general terms.

Visitors and residents see no change to visas, prices or travel from this debate. Our guides Ghana Geopolitics Explained 2026 and Ghana Politics Explained, Who Holds Power in 2026 set out the players, and our Accra expat city guide covers daily life.

What Is Not Known

The sources do not say when Parliament will next sit or whether the Foreign Minister has been scheduled to brief it. Citi Newsroom reported in July that Parliament was due to adjourn on 31 July, and Jinapor’s request is tied to its return.

Ablakwa said on 17 October that Ghana seeks partner status rather than full membership, but it is not known whether an upgrade is planned, because MyJoyOnline reported on 12 October that he called partner status a first step. No application outcome has been reported, and current members must agree on any admission.

Ablakwa has said a policy paper underpins the Ghana BRICS bid, but its text has not been published in the coverage reviewed. Ayariga’s statement is a political demand, and the government has not yet replied to his five points in the sources we found.

Frequently Asked Questions

Did Ghana apply to join BRICS?

Cabinet approved a decision on 6 October to formally apply, according to Ablakwa. No outcome of an application has been reported.

Who is demanding a parliamentary role?

The Minority in Parliament asked on 8 October for an urgent briefing, and APC leader Hassan Ayariga repeated the call on 17 October. He also asked for public consultation and a published legal assessment.

Does the Constitution require Parliament to approve BRICS ties?

Article 75 requires ratification of treaties, agreements or conventions executed by the President. The sources do not say whether a partner-country application would count as one.

Is Ghana seeking full membership or partner status?

Ablakwa said on 10 October and again on 17 October that Ghana would seek partner-country status, and Mahama spoke of a partnership on 16 October. An earlier MyJoyOnline report on 12 October had described partner status as a first step towards full membership.

Could the United States penalise Ghana for it?

Trump has threatened a 10% tariff on countries aligning with BRICS policies and a 100% tariff over a replacement currency. Analysts quoted by Ghanaian media say neither threat applies automatically to Ghana.

Public auction at Belmopan Aggregates and Hardware set for October 28

By Breaking Belize News Staff (HP): Belmopan Aggregates and Hardware is hosting a public auction of industrial equipment, commercial tools, generators, office machinery and surplus supplies.

The auction takes place on Wednesday, October 28, starting at 8:00am at Belmopan Aggregates and Hardware in Belmopan. Everything will go to the highest bidder. Terms are cash, and food and drinks will be available on site.

Among the highlights is a wide range of power equipment, including a Katolight 125kW diesel generator, a Cummins 40kW diesel generator, Generac commercial and standby generators from 9kW to 222kW, Generac and Honda portable generators, and ASCO transfer switches.

Heavy equipment and shop tools include a Mitsubishi electric forklift, a John Deere backhoe extender attachment, Delta and Powermatic industrial table saws, a wood lathe, an electric pallet jack and hydraulic cylinders.

Also up for auction are large format printers, commercial food prep equipment, new pressure washers, a new air compressor, a 54 inch walk behind mower, appliances, furniture, electric scooters, solar batteries, building materials and much more.

World.title: NASA Satellites track warming Pacific waters as El Niño develops
World.content:
NASA Satellites track warming Pacific waters as El Niño develops

By Zoila Palma: NASA satellites are tracking signs of El Niño in the Pacific Ocean, including rising sea surface temperatures and changes in ocean levels and colour.

According to NASA, one of the first indicators appeared in January 2026, when a wave of warm water known as a Kelvin wave was detected near Micronesia in the western Pacific. By early April, the waves had reached the eastern Pacific, contributing to warmer ocean temperatures and rising sea levels in some areas.

Kelvin waves transport heat across the Pacific Ocean, helping trigger a chain reaction that weakens the trade winds and allows warm water to accumulate farther east. NASA reported that sea levels in parts of the eastern Pacific rose by approximately 1 to 1.3 feet, while levels around Indonesia and northern Australia were 6 to 8 inches below normal.

NASA data also show that sea surface temperatures in the eastern Pacific are approximately 3 degrees Fahrenheit, or 1.7 degrees Celsius, above the long-term average, with the possibility of further warming in the coming months. These temperature changes are significant because ocean heat influences atmospheric conditions, affecting rainfall and weather patterns around the world.

Another sign of El Niño is a change in the ocean’s colour as populations of microscopic marine plants known as phytoplankton decline in some equatorial Pacific waters.

NASA says that its scientists will continue monitoring El Niño through its fleet of Earth-observing satellites to better understand the phenomenon and its potential effects.

World.title: Flood alert remains in effect as continued rains affect Belize
World.content:
Flood alert remains in effect as continued rains affect Belize

By Zoila Palma: A flood alert remains in effect across Belize as additional rainfall is expected over the weekend.

The National Meteorological Service (NMS) forecasts between 2 and 4 inches of rain in portions of the country over on Sunday.

Residents in low-lying, flood-prone and riverside communities are urged to remain alert and monitor official weather updates.

The NMS warns that smaller streams and tributaries could rise quickly.

Although several rivers remain at normal or below-normal levels, conditions could change rapidly as rainfall accumulates.

Residents are advised to exercise caution near rivers, streams and low-level crossings and never attempt to cross flooded roads or waterways.

World.title: National Fire Service honors 27 officers for long service
World.content:
National Fire Service honors 27 officers for long service

By Zoila Palma: The National Fire Service (NFS) has recognized 27 officers for their years of dedicated service in protecting lives, safeguarding property and responding to emergencies across Belize.

The awards ceremony was held in Belize City on October 16, 2026, under the Ministry of the Public Service, Disaster Risk Management and Enterprise.

The ceremony celebrated the commitment and contributions of officers who have dedicated years of their careers to public safety and supporting communities during emergencies. Their service reflects the important role the NFS plays in providing emergency response services and protecting Belizeans throughout the country.

Among those recognized were Assistant Divisional Officer Kenneth Mortis and Station Officer Brenton Gentle, who each completed 30 years of service. Retired Station Officer Miguel Medina was also honoured for completing 20 years of service. Their years of experience and dedication highlight the commitment required to serve in the National Fire Service.

Minister of the Public Service, Disaster Risk Management and Enterprise, Henry Charles Usher, emphasized the importance of recognizing officers who have devoted their careers to serving and protecting the people of Belize. “Today, we honour not only the years these officers have given, but also the important contribution they have made to our nation,” Usher said.

World.title: International News: Police and protesters clash across France in major unrest over cost of living
World.content:
International News: Police and protesters clash across France in major unrest over cost of living

By Zoila Palma: Violent clashes erupted between police and protesters across France today as hundreds of thousands of people reportedly took to the streets to demonstrate against rising living costs, inequality and declining public services.

The unrest, described as some of the country’s most destructive in years, resulted in at least 272 arrests, according to France’s Interior Ministry, following incidents in Paris, Marseille, Toulouse, Angers and Lyon, Reuters report.

The CGT union estimated that 800,000 people participated in the demonstrations, although the Interior Ministry did not provide its own estimate.

Protesters said many marches were peaceful and blamed the violence on individuals who joined to cause damage and confront police. In Paris, officers deployed tear gas as clashes intensified, while shops and restaurants were damaged, vehicles and trash cans were set on fire, and several central areas experienced disruption. In Lyon, protesters set fire to the tourist office, while Marseille’s mayor reported vandalism at the town hall.

French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu said the government would not be intimidated by the violence, accusing the far-left and criminals of exploiting the demonstrations ahead of next year’s presidential election.

Meanwhile, protests over rising costs also took place in other European countries today.

World.title: Belize celebrates International Day of Living Heritage
World.content:
Belize celebrates International Day of Living Heritage

By Zoila Palma: Belize joined the global observance of the International Day of Living Heritage, celebrating the traditions, knowledge, skills and cultural practices that connect communities and help shape the country’s national identity.

The observance highlights the importance of preserving Belize’s rich intangible cultural heritage, including the customs and practices passed down through generations. These traditions continue to play an important role in strengthening community connections and maintaining Belize’s diverse cultural identity.

Through community-driven initiatives across the country, efforts are being made to place living heritage at the heart of national development, NICH noted.

NICH also expressed gratitude to its national and international partners and collaborators for their continued support in protecting and promoting the country’s living heritage.

World.title: International News: Taiwan promotes Educational exchanges and talent development partnerships in Latin America
World.content:
International News: Taiwan promotes Educational exchanges and talent development partnerships in Latin America

By Zoila Palma: Taiwan’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFA) is strengthening educational exchanges and cooperation with Latin America through initiatives aimed at developing talent, encouraging innovation and expanding economic partnerships.

MOFA Deputy Minister Chen Ming-chi hosted a welcome luncheon for students participating in the Executive Master’s in Asia-Pacific and Latin American Studies at Tamkang University’s Department of Global Politics and Economics.

Chen thanked the university for its longstanding efforts to promote exchanges with Latin America and highlighted Taiwan’s continued investment in education, talent development and emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence.

Chen also pointed to initiatives such as the Taiwan-Paraguay Polytechnic University project and Taiwan’s support for Taiwanese businesses seeking to expand internationally. He noted that these partnerships can help Taiwan’s diplomatic allies develop new industries through mutually beneficial cooperation. He encouraged the visiting students to explore opportunities for collaboration between Taiwan and their respective home countries during their stay.

Student representative Lorena Yael Piedra Cobo of Ecuador thanked MOFA and Tamkang University for organizing the academic courses and activities.

World.title: Belize City Council, IDB explore plans to revitalize historic Downtown
World.content:
Belize City Council, IDB explore plans to revitalize historic Downtown

By Zoila Palma: The Belize City Council is continuing discussions with the Inter-American Development Bank (IDB) on a proposed comprehensive program to revitalize historic downtown Belize City, with plans being explored to improve public spaces, support businesses and preserve the city’s historic character.

The proposed revitalization area includes the Albert and Regent Street corridors, stretching from the Swing Bridge toward the House of Culture and surrounding historic centre.

Ideas under discussion include cleaning and repainting building façades, improving sidewalks and public spaces, updating traffic signs and making sections of downtown more pedestrian-friendly.

A possible pedestrian route could connect the Swing Bridge with the market, courthouse area and City Hall, while a waterfront boardwalk along the southern coast toward the House of Culture has also been discussed.

The Council and IDB have also explored ways to make better use of vacant or underused lots and encourage more people to live in the downtown area. The IDB’s “IDB for Cities and Regions” program was discussed as a potential avenue for supporting future investment. However, the Council emphasized that discussions remain at an early stage and that the scope of any project has not been finalized.

Any future program would require careful assessment of its costs, the City Council’s financial and legal capacity, and coordination with national partners.

The proposed downtown rejuvenation aims to create more inviting public spaces, support local businesses and protect Belize City’s heritage while making the historic centre a more attractive place to visit, work and live.

World.title: Larry McDonald’s journey
World.content:
FOR nearly seven decades, the heartbeat of Jamaican music has echoed through the hands of one extraordinary musician: Lawrence “Larry” McDonald.

A master percussionist, cultural ambassador, and living legend, McDonald has devoted his life to preserving, celebrating, and sharing the rich rhythmic traditions of Jamaica with the world.

On Monday, October 19, 2026 his remarkable journey will receive national recognition as he is awarded the Badge of Honour for Meritorious Service in the field of Entertainment, acknowledging his tremendous contribution to Jamaica’s musical heritage and cultural identity.

For McDonald, whose hands have helped shape the sound of ska, rocksteady, reggae, jazz, and countless other musical traditions, the honour represents more than personal achievement. It is a celebration of Jamaican culture, its ancestral rhythms, and the generations of musicians who have carried those traditions across the globe.

Born on June 11, 1937, in Port Maria, St Mary, McDonald’s musical journey began long before he stepped onto an international stage.

Growing up immersed in Jamaica’s vibrant cultural traditions, he was deeply influenced by the powerful African-derived rhythms of Kumina, Burru, and Jonkannu. These traditions, rooted in the island’s history and ancestral heritage, became the foundation of his musical identity.

As Jamaican popular music evolved through the 1950s and 1960s, McDonald emerged as one of the percussionists helping to define its distinctive rhythmic character.

Working alongside pioneering musicians such as Carlos Malcolm, Count Ossie, and Toots and the Maytals, he brought the expressive power of traditional hand drumming into the developing sounds of ska, rocksteady, and reggae.

At a time when the drum kit, bass, and guitar were becoming central to Jamaican popular music, McDonald helped establish the conga as an equally compelling musical voice. His playing added depth, texture, and a connection to Jamaica’s African heritage.

After relocating to the United States in 1973, he became an influential presence in an international musical community, collaborating with some of the most celebrated names in reggae, jazz, blues, soul, and spoken-word performance.

His remarkable list of collaborators includes Bob Marley and the Wailers, Peter Tosh, Bunny Wailer, Lee “Scratch” Perry, Taj Mahal, The Skatalites, and the groundbreaking poet and musician Gil Scott-Heron.

His association with Scott-Heron, spanning nearly three decades, was particularly significant. Together, they helped create music that combined rhythm, poetry, social consciousness, and powerful cultural commentary.

Whether performing before thousands or contributing the subtle rhythmic details that elevate a recording, McDonald has always approached percussion as something greater than accompaniment.

In 2009, after decades of lending his extraordinary talents to the music of others, McDonald released his first album as a leader, Drumquestra.

The album was both a musical achievement and a cultural statement.

Bringing together an exceptional gathering of Jamaican musicians and vocalists, including Sly Dunbar, Toots Hibbert, Mutabaruka, Bob Andy, Bongo Herman, and members of the Mystic Revelation of Rastafari, Drumquestra placed percussion at the centre of the musical conversation.

Rather than treating the drum as a supporting instrument, McDonald presented it as the foundation of an entire orchestra of rhythm.

The project celebrated Jamaica’s African musical inheritance while demonstrating the extraordinary possibilities of traditional percussion in contemporary music.

At 89 years old, he continues to embody the spirit of creativity, resilience, and cultural pride that has defined his life’s work.

Far from slowing down, McDonald remains an active and dynamic presence on the international music scene, continuing to tour and perform with The Skatalites, David Hillard and the rocksteady 7, The NYC Ska Orchestra and Subatomic Sound System.

Whether introducing new generations to the infectious rhythms of ska and reggae, or sharing the stage with musicians decades younger than himself, McDonald continues to demonstrate that great music knows no age limits.

In January 2026 he was selected to deliver the keynote address at the University of California, Santa Cruz’s 42nd annual Martin Luther King Jr Convocation, a recognition of his extraordinary artistic journey and his enduring connection to music, history, and social consciousness.

Although his name may not always have appeared in the brightest lights, his rhythms have been heard alongside some of the most important voices in modern music.

He belongs to that exceptional generation of Jamaican musicians whose artistry helped transform a small Caribbean island into one of the world’s most influential musical nations.

World.title: BEYOND THE LENS
World.content:
In this file photo Samantha Hall competes in the women’s discus throw Group B qualification during the World Athletics Championships in Tokyo . (Photo: AFP)

WHEN Dominica’s Olympic champion Thea LaFond and Trinidadian journalist Dennis Allen first discussed the new European broadcast guidelines, they pointed out a tricky puzzle: While tight, suggestive camera angles objectify female athletes, those same viral moments often help competitors build a following and secure paying sponsor deals.

Published by the European Broadcasting Union (EBU) and European Athletics, the Raising the Bar guidelines instruct camera operators to avoid extremely low-angle shots from behind, limit unnecessary slow-motion replays during athlete preparations, and use wider shots that focus on technical execution over physical body parts.

For the women inside and around the sport every day, this debate goes much deeper than camera angles. It touches on what they describe as a frustrating double standard — a female athlete’s financial survival often depends on her looks, even when her hard work and talent should be doing all the talking.

Reigning Commonwealth Games champion and national discus thrower Samantha Hall knows this struggle first-hand. She sees a clear gap in how male and female athletes are treated.

“I understand both sides of the argument,” Hall told the Sunday Observer. “As athletes we do like to see ourselves — especially for field events, we can see where we went wrong with our technique based on pictures — but at the same time, we don’t want to be seen as sexual figures. I hate that for women, this is how we have to earn money — that we have to look sexy, and not for our talents. For men, they don’t really have to do much; it’s just about their talents. They’re getting paid for their talents but for women, it’s not enough. You have to have that image with it.”

Hall’s words point to a wider issue in sports. While male athletes build their careers purely on distances, times and medals, women are expected to win medals and meet a specific standard of beauty.

Long before the cameras zoom in on the field, female track stars face non-stop public criticism over their appearance—from make-up and hair to body art. Criticism male athletes rarely hear.

“I’ve seen it for other athletes, especially like Elaine Thompson-Herah and Ashanti Moore, because they have tattoos in various places on their bodies,” Hall said. “I’ve seen comments like, ‘Why do they have these tattoos? It’s the reason why they can’t perform well.’ And I’m like, ‘That has nothing to do with their performances.’ But yeah, you always have people criticising females based on how they look — like their make-up is off, ‘Her hairstyle doesn’t look neat on her’, ‘Her outfit doesn’t fit her’. They’re always judging female athletes based on their looks.”

Even off the screen, off-hand comments can be intrusive. Hall shared that people sometimes approach her to talk about her physique rather than her throws.

Yet Hall handles this pressure with incredible grace. Rather than letting outside noise get to her, she chooses to own her style and feel confident on her own terms. “It does affect me, but not in a negative way,” she said. “I want to impress my fans, so if this is what the fans want then I have to dress to impress them. At the end of the day, it’s all about fashion; they like your sense of style. For Shelly-Ann [Fraser-Pryce], it’s all about her wigs; they like her style of wigs. For me, if they talk about my bottom it doesn’t really affect me in any way. I don’t feel bad about it. I try to dress appropriately, but at the same time I want to feel sexy as well.”

Hall says other broadcasters around the world will eventually adopt Europe’s cleaner camera rules by 2028, to keep athletes respected and comfortable. But media experts say changing camera angles won’t fix deep-rooted cultural habits overnight.

Melena Helias, a Kingston based French sports journalist who has covered track and field for both local Jamaican outlets and France’s premier sports newspaper L’Équipe, welcomes the new European guidelines as a solid first step.

“My first reaction was quite positive,” Helias told the Observer. “That said, it’s a shame that it has come to the point where a guide on this is needed but I commend EBU Sport for their work. It won’t solve the problem of the sexualisation of sportswomen, or of inequality and stereotypes in sport, but it’s a good start.”

Helias reminds us that women have had to fight for basic space in sports history. Because track and field doesn’t offer massive multimillion-dollar contracts like football or basketball, athletes often have to rely on their public image to survive financially.

“A male athlete attracts sponsors thanks to his results and his personality, among other things,” Helias said. “A female athlete, on top of her results, needs to be perceived as beautiful. That’s precisely the paradox: There isn’t that much money in athletics compared to other sports so you have to capitalise on what sells. And I certainly don’t blame female athletes who use their assets or their beauty on social media to attract sponsors; it’s actually quite logical. I’d just like appearance to be a less omnipresent criterion in the way women are perceived.”

Speaking up against objectification isn’t always easy, either. Even inside the press box Helias admits that as a woman in a heavily male-dominated career, finding the courage to call out inappropriate remarks can be a challenge.

“Unfortunately, no,” Helias said when asked if she feels she has a safe platform to speak out. “I’d even say that I’ve heard, more than once, remarks that outraged me — comments about female athletes — but I didn’t dare say anything. It’s not always easy to find your place in sports journalism; we’re still very much a minority. It’s one thing to have confidence in your abilities and knowledge but it’s another to assert yourself, stand up for yourself, and express your opinions. I’m hopeful that all of this will improve, but it won’t happen overnight.”

When asked if Caribbean broadcasters will follow their European peers, Helias says protecting young athletes — especially minors competing in high school meets — should be a top priority. Ultimately, she believes that while better camera rules help, the real change has to happen inside the minds of the people watching.

“We can change the guidelines but social norms, mentalities, what is or isn’t acceptable, that’s another matter.”

World.title: Manchester dad charged in suspected revenge killing of two men over daughter’s murder
World.content:
File photo of the crime scene in Land Settlement, Manchester where two men were gunned down in March 2026.

MANCHESTER, Jamaica – A Manchester father has been charged with conspiracy to murder in relation to the killing of two men in the parish in March that is believed to have been a reprisal for the shooting death of his daughter a month earlier.

Charged is 37-year-old Kumar Obrien, otherwise known as ‘Frazzle’, of Melrose Drive, Land Settlement.

The deceased have been identified as 29-year-old farmer Yakieni Shaw, also known as ‘Yankee’, of Comfort District, Manchester, and 21-year-old Damien Edwards, otherwise known as ‘Damie’, of Melrose Gardens, Williamsfield, in the parish.

Reports from the Mandeville Police are that Obrien allegedly conspired with other men to kill Edwards and Shaw, who were gunned down about 3:50 pm on Saturday, March 14, 2026.

The shooting is believed to have been a reprisal for the fatal shooting of Obrien’s four-year-old daughter, Saniyah Obrien, on Sunday, February 8, while they were seated in his Voxy motor car in the parish.

An investigations led to Obrien being apprehended, interviewed, and subsequently charged. He is scheduled to appear before the Manchester Parish Court on Wednesday, October 21.

World.title: Adam Stewart, Sheryl Lee Ralph honoured at AFJ Hummingbird Gala
World.content:
Sandals Resorts Executive Chairman Adam Stewart and Emmy Award-winning actress Sheryl Lee Ralph pose with their awards after being honoured at the American Friends of Jamaica (AFJ) Hummingbird Gala at The Plaza in New York on Friday, October 16, 2026.

Sandals Resorts Executive Chairman Adam Stewart and Emmy Award-winning actress Sheryl Lee Ralph were honoured at the American Friends of Jamaica (AFJ) Hummingbird Gala, held at The Plaza in New York on Friday,

Stewart received the International Achievement Award in recognition of his contribution to Caribbean tourism, business and philanthropy, while Ralph received the International Humanitarian Award for her achievements in entertainment and longstanding advocacy, particularly in HIV/AIDS awareness.

Prime Minister Andrew Holness and Tourism Minister Edmund Bartlett were among the guests at the annual fundraising gala, which brought together business leaders, philanthropists and members of the Jamaican diaspora in support of AFJ’s work across Jamaica, including ongoing Hurricane Melissa recovery efforts.

World.title: DIRTY COWARDS
World.content:
Police personnel at the scene where one of their colleagues was fatally shot and another left with lifethreatening injuries in the Five Miles area of St Catherine on Friday. (Photo: Naphtali Junior)

THE police have identified one of three men killed in a firefight in the Five Miles area off the Sligoville main road in St Catherine, Friday morning, during which gunmen used a child to draw cops closer before opening fire, killing one law enforcer.

He is Malique Hussey, otherwise called Mal Boss, from Spanish Town, St Catherine, with connections in Five Miles.

According to the police, Hussey was a known associate of a high-risk target identified as Kenroy Willis, who operates out of the St Andrew North Police Division and is wanted for four murders.

Up to news time the police had not determined the identities of the other two men who were fatally shot in the gun battle which also resulted in the death of Corporal Trevoy Shaw, who was assigned to the Jamaica Constabulary Force’s (JCF) Special Operations Unit, and the injury to a constable who, up to press time, was in hospital in critical condition.

A third cop suffered minor injuries, not gunshot-related, during the incident.

A 10-year-old child was also shot in what Jamaica Observer sources say was a deliberate attack by Hussey, who was her father.

According to the police, about 5:15 Friday morning members of its Special Operations Unit went in search of Willis, Hussey, and their cronies.

On arrival, the police were met with gunfire by men who had barricaded themselves in a house with a woman and three children, including a monthsold baby.

During the stand-off the men indicated that they wanted to surrender, and used one of the children to signal their willingness to lay down their illegal firearms.

“I can confirm that a child was held out the door, and it was declared that they were willing to surrender, and when the police approached, seeking to retrieve the child, fire was opened upon those policemen,” senior communications strategist at the Jamaica Constabulary Force Dennis Brooks told journalists metres from the shooting scene.

“The gunmen shot from behind the child, which placed the police in a precarious position, even in accessing the building, because of the presence of children,” Brooks said.

He explained that they were met by heavily armed men, and a woman declared from inside the building that she and two children were inside.

The woman, the injured 10-year-old, and the baby were allowed to leave the building by the gunmen, who kept a child inside the house as they continued to fire at the cops who were supported by members of the Jamaica Defence Force.

According to Brooks, the men manipulated the presence of the children in the house and the police’s willingness to accept their surrender, pretending to wave the ‘white flag’ multiple times.

“It is the intention of the police on every operation to bring persons to justice, place them before the court, and so it is not our intention to proceed marauding into a building — whether or not there are children and women in there.

And if there is an indication, even the slightest indication, that they are willing to surrender then we are going to engage that possibility,” Brooks said.

He lamented the death of the corporal who was trying to retrieve the child, describing it as heartbreaking.

“I left several policemen and women in tears in Kingston because they knew him well… He was promoted to the rank of corporal about a month ago, which speaks to his own dedication and the recognition of his work.

“I mean, imagine at this time he is just enjoying this new development in his career, and he is [the] pride of his family in this moment, and for his life, his light to be put out in such a manner in seeking to make this country a safer place — it is heartbreaking,” Brooks said.

The pain of Shaw’s colleagues was palpable at Spanish Town Hospital as news spread that two of their colleagues had been rushed there with gunshot wounds.

It became worse when it was confirmed that he had died while the constable had been rushed into surgery.

Shortly after 10:00 am a policeman was seen leaving the hospital’s Accident and Emergency Department (A&E), with sources indicating that he was the person who had suffered the non-gunshot-related injury.

The cop appeared to be in some discomfort as he limped towards a police vehicle parked on the grounds of the hospital.

The vehicle was quickly surrounded by other cops.

Shortly after 11:00 am, people who appeared to be related to the shot cops stormed onto the facility, with cries of grief, as they sought to enter the A&E Department seeking answers.

About five minutes later a black police vehicle raced onto the compound, with cops carrying what appeared to be the bodies of the three slain criminals.

For a minute chaos unfolded as several people hurried to the van to observe what was happening.

But this curiosity was stopped in its tracks by police personnel, who chased away civilians trying to capture videos or photos.

In his immediate reaction to the attack on the men and women under his command, Police Commissioner Dr Kevin Blake, who visited the scene, described the gunmen as murderous.

He said while death is always a possibility for a cop, “We prepare, we equip, so that every single member after an operation goes home to his or her family safe and injury-free.

Unfortunately this morning, that hope and that preparation was shattered.” Blake told the police on the scene that the best way to honour their fallen comrade would be to remain relentless.

“Because we are who we are, because we would rather take them in to face the court, we lost a member… let not that define how we operate going forward,” said Blake.

“I know it is a tough time, and for the colleagues of the officer killed and the officer injured, I understand,” added Blake.

The attack on the police was condemned by political representatives during Friday’s sitting of the Senate, human rights group Jamaicans For Justice, and several other organisations

World.title: Clarendon power shift stalled by court order
World.content:
Member of Parliament for Clarendon Central Delroy Williams (left) and May Pen Mayor Joel Williams (second right) celebrate with JLP supports after special sitting of the Clarendon Municipal Corporation on Friday at which an ex parte interim injunction was tabled which blocked the PNPs efforts to take over leadership of the corporation

THE People’s National Party (PNP) says it plans to challenge a Supreme Court injunction that has stalled its bid to take control of the Clarendon Municipal Corporation.

PNP senior councillor in the corporation Scean Barnswell has also questioned how the injunction was handled at the corporation, claiming it was not entered in its registry, and raised doubts about whether it had been properly served.

The dispute emerged at a special meeting of the corporation on Friday, where councillor for the May Pen North Division Tanyalee Williams formally made the switch from the Jamaica Labour Party (JLP) to the PNP, giving the Opposition party a 12-10 majority in the 22-member council.

The switch had created an opening for the PNP to seek the removal of Mayor Joel Williams and Deputy Mayor Clivalee Mundle and elect replacements backed by the new majority.

However, the meeting was halted after the mayor said an ex parte interim injunction prevented the council from dealing with the matter.

In a statement issued on Friday, the PNP described the injunction as “profoundly anti-democratic”.

The PNP said its legal challenge is intended to allow the meeting to continue and the relevant resolutions to be considered.

Earlier, during the special meeting, Barnswell also raised concerns about how the injunction reached the corporation, questioning whether it had been formally recorded and properly served.

“Chairman, let the record reflect that we have asked the question of how the document has been received at the municipal corporation? We have a registry that logs all external correspondence that comes to the CEO.

It is logged into the registry and I just want to place on record that there is no indication of this document being logged into the council’s registry,” he said.

Barnswell later told reporters that the document appeared to have been presented without the usual procedures being followed.

“There was no signature on the document by the…judge who would have seen it.

There was no official seal or stamp on the document itself, [and] while we respect the court’s decision, we just want to highlight some of the things which we have a problem with the document, no signature, no file date, no official seal or stamp, and it was just a courtesy copy that was sent to us.

So… our attorney is vetting it some more, and they will advise further as to how we proceed,” added Barnswell.

CEO of the corporation Rowhan Blake told councillors during the meeting that he was served in his capacity as the defendant and had attended court at 9:05 Friday morning.

Blake said he then circulated the decision to councillors by email, using the same method through which he normally sends minutes and other correspondence.

He said the order restrained the corporation, its councillors and officers from considering, debating or voting on agenda items two to five, which were the ones that covered the proposed changes to the corporation’s leadership.

The mayor relied on the order to stop the meeting from proceeding.

But PNP councillors disputed his handling of the adjournment, arguing that the decision to end the meeting should have been put to a vote and decided by the majority.

Councillor Romain Morris (PNP, Mocho Division) referred to the Local Government Act and called on the corporation’s CEO to guide the meeting on how it should proceed.

“Mr CEO please note this meeting was not adjourned properly.

The motion of adjournment, Mr Chairman, is a question and is set out in the Local Government Act section 32(J) and with that said, Mr Chairman, it must be adhered to… With that being said the chairman is no longer in his seat, [and] I am going to ask if we can elect a member among ourselves to continue with the remainder of the meeting from the majority,” questioned Morris.

His intervention followed the mayor’s repeated attempts to end the meeting, citing the injunction.

The PNP councillors maintained that the decision to adjourn should have been put to a vote and decided by the majority, rather than the mayor declaring the meeting over.

As the dispute continued, Morris suggested that the councillors remaining in the chamber elect someone from their majority to continue with the meeting.

However, JLP councillors disputed that approach, maintaining that the mayor had already adjourned the meeting and that the council could not proceed in his absence.

PNP councillors continued to challenge the handling of the adjournment and called on Blake to advise them on the way forward, but Blake and the mayor subsequently left the chamber, even as the PNP members maintained that the meeting had not been properly adjourned.

The dispute over the adjournment added to the disagreement over the injunction, with the PNP unable to proceed with the planned leadership changes despite its new 12-10 majority.

Mayor Williams, speaking with the media after the meeting, defended his decision to seek court intervention.

“We are seeking to get clarity as it relates to the Section 16 of the Local Government Act… They are the ones who are playing political football with the people’s business, not us on this side.

We’re always serious about getting the people’s business done in the parish of Clarendon and [by] extension across Jamaica.

That’s what we’re here for, not to play games,” declared the mayor.

He declined to discuss Williams’s decision to leave the JLP, saying: “She’s on the other side and I don’t wish to speak on her.”

World.title: New custos commits to St Elizabeth’s post-Melissa recovery
World.content:
New custos rotulorum for St Elizabeth Bernard Henry gets a kiss from his wife Verna after he received his Instrument of Appointment from Governor General Sir Patrick Allen on Thursday. (Photos: Garfield Robinson)

BUSINESSMAN Bernard Henry has vowed to build on the work of predecessors as he moves into the role of custos rotulorum for St Elizabeth.

Henry received his Instrument of Appointment from Governor General Sir Patrick Allen, after taking the Oath of Allegiance and the Oath of Office during a ceremony at King’s House on Thursday.

He replaces Beryl Rochester who served 12 years as custos rotulorum for the parish.

“This is a humbling office; I’m very fortunate.

We have had an acting custos who was tremendous so we want to make sure that we work to continue to build on what our former custos, Honourable Beryl Rochester, put in place, and the custodes before, and also what Acting Custos Stevon Sheriffe… did.

So my role is really for us to build from there,” Henry told the Jamaica Observer following the ceremony.

According to Henry, the role is even more significant following the devastation caused by Hurricane Melissa last year.

“To be able to step into this role at this time, when we are in the process of rebuilding our parish, is significant.

And so we want to make sure that we operate with humility, that we are there to help, to add value, and to rebuild St Elizabeth.

“We are a very proud parish and we are a resilient people.

We want to show off who we are and what we do, and we want to make sure that the people who are hurting, we are there to lift them up — especially the youth,” Henry added.

The Category 5 storm, which hit Jamaica on October 28, 2025, left many residents of St Elizabeth scrambling to rebuild their lives, but Henry remains optimistic about the future of the parish.

“I’m hoping that we will get the support that we need to rebuild even better than what we had before.

I see the devastation but I’m also looking for the silver lining, and the silver lining is that we will be able to build back even better.

That’s what I see.

That’s what I want to support.

And so St Elizabeth people, we will come again,” Henry said.

In his address, Governor General Sir Patrick Allen charged Henry to execute the role with sound judgement, objectivity, and the ability to command public confidence.

“You will be my representative in St Elizabeth, and that means that you will support the administration of justice, provide leadership to the network of justices of the peace, and encourage civic participation.

I welcome your intention to improve access to the justices of the peace in St Elizabeth, to maintain meaningful engagement with communities, and encourage opportunities for our young people,” said Sir Patrick.

“Such priorities are especially pertinent as St Elizabeth continues its recovery and renewal.

You have spoken of the importance of listening, learning, and seeking wise counsel.

I encourage you to remain guided by these principles, recognising that the distinction of public office rests ultimately upon the honour with which its responsibilities are discharged,” added Sir Patrick.

The governor general said Henry’s long-standing investment in education, institutional governance, and national development has earned the businessman his confidence.

“He has demonstrated the vision and discipline required to establish enterprises, navigate complex responsibilities, and forge enduring partnerships.

However, his contribution to St Elizabeth extends beyond commercial enterprise.

“As inaugural chairman of the St Elizabeth Community Development Foundation, and through its involvement with the St Elizabeth Homecoming Foundation, he has helped to foster cooperation and advance the interests of the parish.

These experiences assume relevance as he undertakes the responsibilities of custos rotulorum,” said Sir Patrick.

World.title: Changes coming for Miss Jamaica World pageant
World.content:
The 23 finalists competing in the 2026 Miss Jamaica World pageant

Changes will be implemented for this year’s staging of the Miss Jamaica World beauty pageant.

At a sashing exercise and the Beach Beauty Fast Track competition held at the Jamaica Pegasus hotel in New Kingston on Tuesday night, Dahlia Harris, of the Miss Jamaica World Organization, gave an insight into how the new titleholder will be selected.

“Forty per cent of each contestant’s overall assessment will come from her performance throughout the training and development programme, while 60 per cent will come from the judges’ assessment.

Why have we made this change? Because we believe that how a young woman conducts herself throughout the journey is just as important as how she performs when she steps in front of the judges,” Harris told the Jamaica Observer.

“We want to reward punctuality, participation, discipline, deportment, commitment, and a willingness to learn.

We want contestants to understand that professionalism is not something you switch on when the spotlight comes on.

It is demonstrated in how you show up, how you treat people, how you respond to challenges, and how seriously you take the opportunities presented to you.

The crown should represent more than a performance on one evening; it should reflect the character, consistency, and commitment demonstrated throughout the competition.

And we believe this revised assessment structure will help us achieve exactly that.” Instead of a Top 10, a Top 12 will be selected and comprise the winners of the 5 fasttrack competitions; namely, Beach Beauty, Talent, Fitness Challenge, Top Model, and Beauty with a Purpose.

There will also be five judges’ selections and, for the very first time, the Head-to- Head and Multi-Media challenge winners.

“The Challenge events are, therefore, more extensive this year.

The Head-to-Head Challenge, for example, has already selected a top 10 based on their Round One performance and, on Thursday, October 15, they will compete in the semi-final and final rounds.

The judges will select a Top 5 and the public will select a People’s Choice winner, who will join them to complete a Top 6,” said Harris.

At Tuesday night’s event, the 23 finalists were sashed by their respective sponsors.

Afterwards, the Beach Beauty Fast Track competition took place, with Seana’Kay Wright, who is sponsored by Southdale Hardware and Glass Supplies, taking first place.

First runner-up was Matea Mahal Smith, Miss Aveeno, while medical doctor Samantha McLeod, Miss Island Smiles, was named second runner-up.

Ironically, at the recent Fitness Challenge, held at the Emancipation Park in New Kingston, Smith was declared the first-place winner and Wright was her first runner-up.

The coronation of Miss Jamaica World 2026 is scheduled for November 1 at Karl Hendrickson Auditorium, Jamaica College.

World.title: Starlink restrictions in Ukraine a ‘planned operation’, Zelenskyy says
World.content:
The restrictions have revived questions on Ukraine’s reliance on the satellite system operated by a U.S. company amid escalating tensions between Kyiv and the White House. “This will cost many of us our lives,” an experienced Ukrainian officer told POLITICO and the Axel Springer Global Reporters Network earlier this week.

“We’re reaching out to everyone at the military level, at the Ministry of Defense level, and at the diplomatic level, including to SpaceX. Right now, no one is responding to our military or the Ministry of Defense,” Zelenskyy told reporters.

The European Union is under increasing pressure to provide Ukraine with an alternative to Starlink. But negotiations between Brussels and Kyiv over access to the bloc’s Govsatcom program — which gives participating governments secure communications capabilities— have been stalling. And IRIS², the EU’s in-house planned network to match Starlink, is only expected to come online in 2030.

“The Europeans are now raising the question of alternatives themselves. And they’re already working on them. They’re already making progress, and they’ll succeed in this area. I can already see that,” Zelenskyy said.

SpaceX did not immediately responded to a request for comment.

Earlier on Saturday, Zelenskyy accused Russia of looking to create a blackout across Ukraine, amid attacks on energy infrastructure and the waiver of U.S. sanctions on Moscow.

World.title: Police, demonstrators clash on sidelines of mass French protests
World.content:
“A very large majority of people are protesting without violence,” Paris’s police prefecture said on Saturday afternoon.

Around 4,500 secondary school pupils and university students involved in the Yellow Vests movement demonstrated side by side against the cost of living in Pau, south-west of France on 17 October 2026. | Jean-Christophe Chartre/AFP via Getty Images

Saturday’s demonstrations grew out of the student protests that began last month with school blockades and calls for better study conditions, more teachers and more funding. The movement has since spread nationwide — and become a political issue as the campaign for next year’s presidential election heats up.

In recent weeks, the government has struggled to deal with the crisis — which Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu described as “urban violence” — and is hoping the student movement will now fade because of a two-week school holiday that started Friday evening.

“The mobilization is marked by a very strong involvement of the ultra-left movement, which is only looking to cause disorder,” Nuñez’s office said Saturday, adding that the minister reiterated his “instructions of utmost firmness” to local prefects and police forces.

Footage showed Lyon’s tourist board office engulfed in flames on the city’s Place Bellecour. A police station was vandalized in Marseille, where a group of “rioters” also entered city hall, Mayor Benoît Payan said. He told BFMTV that “damage was objectively fairly limited,” although the act of vandalism was “unacceptable.” The headquarters of right-wing TV channel CNews in Paris was also targeted , authorities said.

World.title: Spain’s far left fails to unite ahead of November vote
World.content:
The Broad Front is made up of Sumar, the current junior partner in the Socialist-led government, the Catalan Comuns, the Communist-led United Left and Más Madrid. Some smaller local parties have also joined the ticket. The lead candidate for prime minister will be Ada Colau, the former mayor of Barcelona.

Sumar, the dominant force in the alliance, has seen its vote share more than halve since 2023, to 5%, according to POLITICO’s Poll of Polls.

Although Podemos has only been polling at 3%, its full involvement in the Broad Front would have meant a greater overall share of seats for the far left, according to analysts.

The PSOE has been trailing the conservative People’s Party and would need a strong performance by parties to its left in order to keep Sánchez in office. The more likely scenario, polls show, is that the PP will be able to form a majority with the far-right Vox, whose support has been rising.

“The Spanish left is caught up in a game of thrones that demobilizes [voters],” said Irene de Miguel, coordinator of Podemos in the western region of Extremadura, as the deadline loomed.

World.title: EU leaders clash over migration, Ukraine and budget in Brussels — but delay big decisions
World.content:
Speaking to journalists during a packed news conference, Ukraine’s wartime leader urged his European counterparts to come up with a financial plan or risk facing an unprecedented migration crisis with “20 million Ukrainians” fleeing to Europe.

“The war will cost €155 billion next year. And we need at least €70 billion more from you — for defense, for weapons, and for our resilience,” Zelenskyy said. “This is a realistic amount. And I ask you to find this support. It will help us hold Russia back.”

But two diplomats told POLITICO that capitals would continue exploring a range of options to meet Kyiv’s needs, including a potential further loan from the EU.

Luc Frieden and Emmanuel Macron speak ahead of a round table during the EU summit in Brussels on Oct. 15, 2026. | Ludovic Marin/AFP via Getty Images

A debate over whether to mobilize some €300 billion in Russian frozen assets to help Ukraine is a case in point. Nearly a year after EU leaders rejected using the assets amid objections from Belgium, France and Italy, several countries have asked for the option to be revisited, and top EU diplomat Kaja Kallas had said frozen assets would be on the table when leaders met in Brussels.

But after hours of talks about Ukraine, “nothing has changed,” said Swedish Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson. “The money is not lost but in my belief nothing has happened since we had the discussion last time.”

“In the short term, money to support Ukraine must come from other sources than the frozen assets,” he concluded.

World.title: EU faces growing pressure to plug Ukraine’s Starlink gap
World.content:
"It is unacceptable for Ukraine’s defense — and therefore Europe’s security — to depend on the goodwill of a single American billionaire or on Donald Trump’s decisions," French centrist Member of the European Parliament Christophe Grudler told POLITICO.

Ahead of Thursday's high-level meeting, European lawmakers had been calling on the EU executive to fast-track Kyiv's access to satellite capabilities already pooled under the bloc’s Govsatcom program — which gives participating governments secure communications capabilities.

Negotiations between the EU executive and Ukraine over this access have been ongoing since March, with no breakthrough. Norway and Iceland secured such an agreement earlier this year.

"What I don’t understand is why the European Commission and the Member States have not done everything possible to quickly reach an agreement that would allow Ukraine to benefit from it," added Christophe Grudler, who wrote to EU leaders.

He also called on them to speed up work on IRIS² — the EU’s in-house, planned satellite network and full-fledged match to Starlink, which is only expected to come online in 2030.

Commission spokesperson Thomas Regnier confirmed in a statement that it is "currently in talks with Ukraine to fully associate" the country with the EU's Govsatcom program. "The war in Ukraine shows that our security also depends on space. And the EU has been doing quite a lot. We are ready to support Ukraine where we can support Ukraine," he added.

World.title: 21 things we learned at the EU leaders’ summit
World.content:
1) Energy stole the show right out of the gate

The summit’s first major clash came Thursday morning, with EU leaders split over whether to delay ETS2, the bloc’s second phase of carbon pricing, to address high energy prices, triggering a three-hour-long standoff.

Italy and Greece joined the Visegrád Four — Czechia, Hungary, Poland and Slovakia — in calling for a delay, a push rejected by the majority of countries.

The debate dragged on, delaying lunch (spare a thought for our hungry leaders!) and leading to the cancellation of a press conference on Thursday night.

2) Budget negotiations are a marathon…

Negotiations on the bloc’s next long-term budget were expected to be one of the summit’s most contentious topics. But they were a nothingburger, with most leaders repeating positions they have held for months. The summit brought them no closer to a breakthrough.

Many countries, of course, want a smaller budget, with Swedish Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson telling reporters that his country is “not an ATM for the EU.”

Belgian Prime Minister Bart De Wever, meanwhile, said he had no choice but to be frugal at the European level, arguing he is used to tightening his belt at home because his wife is Dutch. Think of Bart next time your Dutch friends ask you to pay them back for that coffee.

World.title: In Europe’s tech capital, Irish labor unions are booming amid AI-driven layoffs
World.content:
Ireland's lucrative tech sector has been rattled by waves of AI-driven layoffs — and the country's fledgling tech union has seen an exponential spike in sign-ups from workers who are worried about their future.

There’s an “awakening” happening right now among workers in Ireland’s tech sector, and a growing “awareness that they’re not bulletproof,” said Sinéad Gibney, a social democrat lawmaker who previously worked for Google.

“I do think what we will see is that parts of roles will be automated, which means that people will be competing more heavily for the same roles," she said. "They won't have the same labor power and therefore we're going to see a drop in quality of work, we're going to see more zero-hour contracts, in more places than we already see it.”

The labor movement brewing in Ireland, where many of the world's tech giants have their EU bases, is part of a wider trend among tech workers globally, who have seen their work disrupted by rapidly evolving AI.

Rise in layoffs

Ireland’s dedicated union for tech workers, the Digital and Techworker Alliance (DATA), has seen a five-fold increase in membership since it was first founded in 2023.

In its first year and a half of existence, membership hovered around 270 people. In the past year-and-a-half, it's jumped to more than 1,350 members, DATA organizer John Bohan told POLITICO. He added that this number tends to spike around layoffs and other actions.

World.title: Scottish government set to drop opposition to new oil and gas fields
World.content:
The Scottish government — led by the SNP since 2007 — released a draft energy strategy in 2023 which set out its “presumption against” new oil and gas fields in the North Sea.

That draft strategy is “out of date,” one senior Scottish government official said. They said a new strategy, expected by the summer, will not contain this wording. A second person with knowledge of the policy said the new strategy will “reflect the world as it is.”

The shift in policy comes with the U.K. government widely expected to give the go-ahead to the Jackdaw gas field next week.

While the Scottish government has little power over the granting of new licenses for projects such as Jackdaw or the Rosebank oil field — where a decision is expected to come separately and at a later date — it has an important symbolic role, and can apply pressure to the U.K. government to approve licenses.

SNP politicians at the party’s conference in Aberdeen privately admitted the stance on Jackdaw has hurt the party electorally.

The party passed a resolution at its conference Friday which stated that the “utilisation of domestic production” of oil and gas is “clearly preferable to importation”. This was seen as a further softening of the position of the SNP — which governed in a quasi-coalition with the anti-exploration Scottish Greens until as recently as 2004.

World.title: France reels after cost-of-living protests see widespread violence
World.content:
Between 550,000 and 800,000 people took to the streets of France on Saturday, mostly peacefully and often unaware of the unprecedented violence breaking out in some of the country's major cities.

 

Limoges city hall went up in flames, as did the iconic tourist office on Place Bellecour in Lyon. Vandals also forced their way into town halls in Marseille, Lille, and Angers, whilst in Bordeaux, the prefect's residence was ransacked.

Lyon tourist office, 17.10.2026 (AP Photo/Laurent Cipriani) AP Photo

Widespread destruction

"Scenes of insurrection," reads the front page of Le Parisien.

In Paris, Mayor Emmanuel Grégoire said "entire streets" had been "systematically devastated" after the French capital saw violent clashes between protesters and police.

The French capital quite literally went up in flames on Saturday. By midday, Place de la République was littered with projectiles, police were clashing with rioters in clouds of tear gas, and a thick column of black smoke rose above the city's iconic rooftops as emergency service vehicles burned.

After nightfall, in several districts, Parisians watched in fear from restaurants and café terraces as groups of young people continued to rampage through the city.

Dressed in black and wearing masks, the groups moved either in their dozens or in small, scattered bands.

Each time, they used the same tactic: several would approach a shop and attack its metal shutters until they give way, before people rushed in to loot the premises.

They left behind smashed storefronts, charred bicycles, and stolen goods scattered on the ground.

Riot police units, who were charged with maintaining public order, followed alongside firefighters as the groups moved on to find more targets ahead.

The looters did not spare the Champs-Élysées, and clashes with the police moved closer to the Élysée Palace and the National Assembly.

The government has said around 1,200 arrests were made across France and that 150 police officers and gendarmes were injured over the course of the day.

Politicians react

Addressing the protests in a post on social media on Saturday evening, French President Emmanuel Macron said there was "no place for violence" in France.

"Those who have vandalised and attacked prefectures and shops alike, and even looted our town halls, will be prosecuted and punished," he wrote.

People look at charred cars the day after a demonstration against rising living costs, joining students' grievances, in Paris, Sunday, Oct. 18, 2026. Copyright 2026 The Associated Press. All rights reserved.

For his part, the interior minister, Laurent Nuñez, has spoken of "groups of several hundred or even thousands of rioters, very clearly instigated by the far left."

Far-right presidential candidate Marine Le Pen said "legitimate social demands" had been "taken hostage by the far left and by the speeches of Jean-Luc Mélenchon's MPs who, by legitimising violence, by seeing order as oppression and disorder as a right, are trying to plunge the country into chaos."

According to Mélenchon, the far-left presidential candidate, the "absurd leadership has opened the door to chaos.

"The leaders no longer know what to do; the rank and file are afraid and running amok," he wrote on X.

"I do not know who will hear my voice in such circumstances, but my message is clear: those who share our struggle have no place in looting and vandalism," he added.

World.title: Lisbon named Europe's best city and cruise destination for 2026
World.content:
Lisbon has been distinguished as the Best City Destination in Europe at the World Travel Awards Europe 2026 (source in Portuguese). The Portuguese capital was also named Best Cruise Destination in Europe. The two accolades were presented on Saturday, 17 October, at a ceremony in Kotor Bay, Montenegro.

 

In a statement, the Lisbon Tourism Association says these awards "recognise Lisbon's international appeal and the diversity of its tourism offer".

António Valle, director-general of the Lisbon Tourism Association, quoted in the statement, stresses that "these awards show how Lisbon is a unique and authentic destination".

"Lisbon sets itself apart from the main European destinations by valuing its own identity while responding to different travel motivations," he says, underlining that the awards are also "recognition of a collective effort to improve and enhance the tourism offer".

For António Valle, these prizes "help boost the local economy and reaffirm the authenticity and identity that sets" the Portuguese capital apart.

"Lisbon is increasingly setting the trend in the international tourism sector, creating value both for those who visit us and for those who live and work here," he adds.

The Lisbon Tourism Association also points out that "the focus on improving the offer, enhancing heritage and culture, and diversifying the experiences available across the entire Lisbon Metropolitan Area remains central to the destination's international competitiveness".

"This strategy seeks to attract visitors who stay longer, discover different parts of the region and help generate greater economic and social value," the note sent to newsrooms adds.

The World Travel Awards are among the most prestigious international distinctions in the tourism sector and annually reward destinations, hotels, airlines and other industry players.

This year the ceremony took place at the Hyatt Regency Kotor Bay Resort, a five-star luxury hotel in Kotor Bay, in south-west Montenegro on the Adriatic Sea, classified as a UNESCO World Heritage site.

This was the first time the Balkan country had hosted the awards in the 33-year history of the World Travel Awards.

World.title: Possible drone explosion in northern Lithuania near Latvian border
World.content:
NATO fighter jets were scrambled on Sunday after an unidentified flying object, suspected to be a drone, entered Lithuanian airspace, Lithuanian authorities and the Latvian armed forces said.

 

The Latvian military said it appeared the jets "did not shoot down the suspected unmanned aerial vehicle" and that it was possible it had "detonated on its own."

The incident took place close to the Latvian border and triggered multiple air alerts, it added.

According to Lithuanian Defence Minister Robertas Kaunas, fighter jets carrying out a NATO air defence mission were tracking the object in the Biržai district of northern Lithuania on Sunday morning.

"Due to difficult weather conditions, the fighter jet pilots are currently unable to visually identify the object," he wrote in a post on social media.

The origin of the suspected drone remains unclear. Investigations are ongoing, with Lithuanian military personnel heading to the location where radio signal was lost to carry out a ground inspection.

The incident is the latest in a growing series of drone incursions and incidents along NATO's eastern flank, many of which are believed to be spillover from Russia's war in Ukraine.

It comes after Romanian authorities announced on Saturday that Romanian F-16 fighter jets had shot down two drones over the Black Sea.

The aircraft were called into action after radar surveillance systems detected a number of aerial targets, the Romanian Defence Ministry said. It later announced that the targets were "jet-powered attack drones from the Geran family."

Defence Minister Radu Miruta said the first drone entered Romanian airspace at around 17:59 and was shot down "within two minutes," 25 km south-east of the town of Sulina.

"The second drone, in the same area, was engaged and shot down at 18:05, five minutes after entering national airspace, 20 km east of Sulina," he added.

World.title: Canada reports 'fatalities and injuries' following incident at military base
World.content:
An incident at a Canadian military base has resulted in a number of deaths and injuries, Canada's defence minister announced late on Saturday.

 

"I'm saddened to share that there have been both fatalities and injuries as a result of an incident on the base," David McGuinty said in a statement, identifying the location as Canadian Forces Base Wainwright in Alberta.

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said a "serious incident creating a major fire" had occurred at the site.

"Our thoughts are with all the brave women and men affected. We are working closely with the Government of Alberta and local authorities," he wrote in a post on social media.

Further information will be released in the "coming hours and days," McGuinty added.

According to the Canadian government, Wainwright is one of the "busiest" army bases in the country and is home to the Canadian Manoeuvre Training Centre as well as the 3rd Canadian Division Training Centre.

Wainwright is around 210 kilometres east of Edmonton - the capital of Alberta - and 110 kilometres southwest of Lloydminster.

This is a developing story. Check back here for further details.

World.title: Spire collapses at historic Limoges town hall amid violent protests across France
World.content:
A 140-year-old town hall in France was largely destroyed as a fierce fire took hold on Saturday after masked protesters set the building alight, authorities said.

 

Dramatic footage showed the spire of the Limoges town hall collapse as flames engulfed the roof overnight amid mass cost-of-living protests across the country.

According to the Haute-Vienne prefecture, rioters broke into the town hall at around 6 pm on Saturday before setting it ablaze.

"Firefighters from Haute-Vienne were immediately mobilised in large numbers to tackle the fire," it said in a press release. "Limoges town hall, a heritage site and iconic landmark for everyone, was largely destroyed."

The prefecture added that a number of businesses were then looted around the Rue Jean Jaurès area.

Maurice Barate, the prefect of Haute-Vienne, has strongly condemned the "arson attack" on the town hall as well as other incidents in the city on Saturday.

The prefecture said roughly 2,000 people - including "more than 500 individuals deliberately seeking confrontation" - had gathered at around 2 pm in the Casseaux area in the east of the city, with some attacking security forces with projectiles.

Four police officers sustained "more serious" injuries, and four police vehicles were destroyed, it said. The protesters then moved to block the A20 motorway before heading for the city centre.

Nineteen people have been detained by police in the region in relation to the protests, and investigations are continuing.

Construction on the Limoges town hall began in 1879, and the building was inaugurated on 14 July 1883.

"Protesting is a right, and anger deserves to be heard. Yet, no disagreement or grievance can ever justify the destruction of public property," Guillaume Guérin, the mayor of Limoges, said, calling the violence "unacceptable."

Violence sweeps France

Major cost-of-living protests taking place across France on Saturday turned violent in a number of parts of the country as demonstrators clashed with police.

The French Interior Ministry said around 550,000 people took part in the protests - which joined up with ongoing student demonstrations - nationwide, including roughly 110,000 in Paris.

In the capital, chaotic scenes saw widespread looting as officers fired tear gas and water cannons to disperse crowds. A Euronews crew were also assaulted by looters and rioters in Paris on Saturday, near the Place de la Republique, as they covered the ongoing demonstrations.

However, in other parts of the city, such as around the Boulevard de Clichy and Place de Clichy in the 18th arrondissement, the situation remained peaceful, another Euronews journalist reporting from the scene said.

Addressing the protests in a post on social media on Saturday evening, French President Emmanuel Macron said there was "no place for violence" in France.

"Those who have vandalised and attacked prefectures and shops alike, and even looted our town halls, will be prosecuted and punished," he said.

World.title: Look, no hands: Euronews rode driverless in Europe's first robotaxi in Zagreb
World.content:
Uber launched a driverless taxi service in Zagreb, Croatia, earlier this year and has now unveiled plans to roll out a fully autonomous vehicle service in a host of European cities with partners across the continent, starting with Manchester.

 

The US tech company deployed driverless robotaxis on the streets of Zagreb in April in partnership with local service operator Verne and Chinese AI firm Pony.ai in a business model they want to scale up across the continent.

It is an odd partnership given the divergent philosophies at play in Europe, the US and China, with Europe being particularly cautious compared with the latter two. But the companies believe the partnership works thanks to their shared ambition to deploy autonomous vehicle taxi rides around the world.

The partnership is one of more than 30 Uber runs across Europe. Together with Verne and Pony.ai, Uber has begun tests in Manchester, and Pony.ai and Uber plan to launch in London, with many more cities in the pipeline.

The Zagreb partnership is the most advanced and was announced in March, in a move that aimed to bring driverless taxis out of testing grounds and onto the market in Europe for the first time.

Zagreb was a particularly appealing candidate city for Uber, as it is home to electric hypercar maker Rimac, whose founder Mate Rimac had already branched out into robotaxis through Verne. Verne has its own plans to roll out a “business class” form of autonomous vehicle mobility service.

In April, the partnership launched its robotaxi service, giving users in Zagreb the chance to order a driverless vehicle for their journey. These cars still have a human in the driving seat, known as a safety operator, who oversees the trip as a security measure. Safety operators are usually former taxi drivers.

The service’s vehicles have since clocked up 200,000 kilometres on Zagreb’s roads.

Now the partnership feels confident enough to take the next step and remove the operator from the car, leaving just you, the passenger, alone in the vehicle.

Europe’s first fully driverless trips began on 10 September, open to a limited number of invited users on a 22-kilometre route linking Verne’s headquarters with Zagreb’s Franjo Tuđman Airport.

‘Look, no hands’

Ordering an Uber with the currently available driverless ride service is just as simple as booking any other trip with the platform. Users can choose between human-driven and AI-driven robotaxi rides when requesting UberX or Comfort journeys.

Riders can unlock the car with their phone, get in and get comfortable, or as comfortable as possible in a car with no one driving, but with full access to Uber support should anything happen.

In Zagreb, riders travel in the BAIC Arcfox Alpha T5, a Chinese electric SUV. A human safety operator sits in the driving seat, and the front passenger seat has been removed to make more space for luggage.

Uber and Verne currently run about 30 autonomous vehicles in Zagreb, which return each night to a central hub called a “mothership” for cleaning and maintenance by the Croatian startup.

The current setup is what is known as a level 4 driverless car programme, which means the car can drive itself without human interference, but only in strictly controlled areas. Nowhere in the world runs a level 5 programme, which means unrestricted road access.

A woman sits and looks out the window during her taxi ride. Source: Uber.

It is a strange feeling seeing a car drive itself for the first time. From the rear passenger seat, you can see the steering wheel spinning as the car makes a turn calmly and methodically, even while negotiating oncoming traffic.

The smooth ride puts you at ease, and after a while you forget that it is not a person but an AI driving you to your destination.

“We call it a little bit magically boring, meaning, you get in and first you’re like ‘oh, no one’s hands are on the wheel’ and then all of sudden you’re in a car like you normally would be,” said Annie Duvnjak, global head of autonomous mobility operations at Uber.

That is not to say the ride is free of interruptions. The car comes to a complete stop at every stop sign, even when the road is empty, and it pulls over to avoid overly aggressive human drivers trying to overtake.

It is a learning process for the partnership, which is testing fully driverless vehicles, its end goal, in a limited area of Zagreb.

A unique partnership

The partnership, launched in April, is a unique combination of an American mobility firm, a European startup and a Chinese AI company, with each organisation coming from regions with wildly differing approaches to mobility and AI.

Given these divergent approaches and the current geopolitical friction on issues ranging from trade and consumer rules to technological sovereignty and supply chains, it may seem surprising that these companies have joined forces.
