World.title: People increasingly not paying hospital fees
World.content:
Since patient visit fees increased last year, more and more people have been falling behind on payments to hospitals. Patients with outstanding debts can no longer see a specialist.

A year and a half ago, the cost of visiting a doctor quadrupled, with patient visit fees rising from €5 to €20 and daily hospital bed fees doubling from €2.50 to €5. Since then, the number of patients owing money to North Estonia Medical Center (PERH) has doubled, while the total amount owed has tripled.

"Daily hospital bed fees account for about 70 percent of the debt, while visit fees, mainly for emergency department visits, account for the remaining 30 percent," said Anneli Habicht, PERH's head of customer service.

According to Habicht, in about half of cases patients simply forget to pay, while the other half have no intention of paying. Before turning to a debt collection agency, the hospital spends a couple of months trying to recover the money itself.

"When we look at which groups are more likely to owe us money, it seems to be older people approaching retirement age, as well as very young adults. In terms of gender, men tend to be more likely to fall behind on payments," Habicht said.

Last year, nearly 2,200 people owed money to Narva Hospital. The amounts involved are generally small and are usually paid after a reminder.

"In the first nine months of this year, the number of debtors has increased by about 25 percent. At the same time, we haven't seen any behavior that would require us to take aggressive action through debt collection agencies or any signs that people are deliberately trying to avoid their obligations," said Narva Hospital CEO Üllar Lanno.

Tartu University Hospital has not experienced the same problems as its counterparts in northern Estonia.

"The hospital still receives most of its revenue for medical treatment through its contract with the Estonian Health Insurance Fund. Patients' out-of-pocket payments account for less than 3 percent of that. We have half a million outpatient visits a year and perhaps 200 to 400 patients need to be sent payment reminders," said Joel Starkopf, a member of Tartu University Hospital's management board.

According to debt collection agency Julianus Inkasso, the number of claims submitted by hospitals has increased by a few percentage points, although some medical institutions have submitted 10 percent more claims.

"When the visit fee was €5, it was a little easier to pay. If you're in a difficult financial situation, €20 is harder to afford. And if you forget to pay on time, finding that extra money later can be more difficult when you're working with a tight household budget," said Merle Laurimäe, CEO of Julianus Inkasso.

More than half of debtors settle their debts within a year of receiving a letter from the collection agency. However, they must also cover late-payment interest and collection fees of up to €30.

"I think the total could rise to around €55 at most, provided you act in time," Laurimäe said.

World.title: Reform Party unveils campaign slogan as PM touts economic growth
World.content:
Prime Minister and Reform Party chair Kristen Michal says Estonia's economy is growing twice as fast as the EU average, as Reform pledges a clear course in the 2027 elections.

Speaking at the party's council meeting in Tartu on Saturday, Michal said the largest income tax cut in Estonia's history had doubled economic growth.

"Estonia's economy is growing twice as fast as the EU average," he said, also citing rising wages, consumption, exports and manufacturing, alongside lower unemployment and easing inflation.

"The Reform Party can say with confidence: our plan is working," the prime minister emphasized. "Estonia has been led through a major test and is now on a solid growth path, moving forward even in the face of headwinds."

He noted that wages are rising, with consumer confidence up and people taking home an average of 10 percent more money this year. Defense spending of 5 percent GDP, he added, is also strengthening security and giving families and businesses confidence to plan for the future.

Even the opposition is starting to see that the Reform Party's plan is working, Michal said, accusing Isamaa and the Center Party of already making plans to form a coalition — potentially joined by the Conservative People's Party of Estonia (EKRE).

"The Reform Party is their main enemy for a reason: they can only steal Estonia's prosperity and growth if we're out of the picture," the party chair said, emphasizing that the key issue in the March 2027 elections will be whether this prosperity will continue to grow or be taken away from them.

Michal said that incomes must rise faster than prices, as a wealthier Estonia can invest more in education, healthcare, a cleaner environment and a better quality of life.

"No other party in Estonia stands as firmly for the economy, national defense, liberal principles, Estonian-language education and culture, and European values," he said. "These are the foundations of Estonia's future."

'A clear course for the future'

The Reform Party also unveiled its campaign slogan: "A clear course for the future."

Tartu mayor and party council chair Urmas Klaas said it reflects the party's focus on security, economic growth and opportunities for families and businesses.

He recalled that Reform's "Blue, black and white plan" for Estonia, unveiled in March, centers on building a stronger middle class, bolstering security and making greater use of artificial intelligence (AI) in the economy and government.



"We're running for election to ensure that robust security can give families confidence, people's work and knowledge can create prosperity and technology can help businesses grow and the state operate more efficiently," Klaas said.

MP and Reform Party secretary general Kristo Enn Vaga said the slogan emphasizes that Estonia's future is up to its own choices.

"We in the Reform Party want Estonia to be secure and the economy to grow, because that gives people and businesses more opportunities to carry out their plans," Vaga said. "This is the future we want to build."

World.title: Gallery: Public bomb shelter in Tallinn hidden behind woodland mural
World.content:
A street-level public civil defense shelter in the heart of downtown Tallinn has been transformed with a mural featuring Estonian trees and wildlife.

Located next to Kalev Sports Hall in Tiigiveski Park, the modular concrete shelter cannot withstand a direct missile hit, but it can protect around 20 people from blast waves, shrapnel and debris from an explosion as close as 50 meters away.

Similar shelters are already widely used in Ukraine, including in Kramatorsk.

The concrete module, donated by security company Citysec, is also now fully wrapped in a woodland mural by Colorees Art's Helena Hanni and Vahur Agar, featuring a wild hare, a bear family, an owl in flight and a wolf.

While usually kept closed in peacetime, the shelter was open to visitors on Friday, when officials were on hand to explain its features to the public.

Tallinn unveiled a new street-level civil defense shelter on Juhkentali tänav. October 2026. Source: Ellen Rudi/Tallinn Strategic Management Office

City weighs dozens more shelters

Citysec CEO Eduard Rikkas said the module was developed on a 50-50 basis with partners in Ukraine, where the design has already been in use for years.

Deputy Mayor Tiit Terik (Center) said the shelter door can be opened remotely during an emergency, and will unlock automatically if power or communications fail.

The shelter door, he added, will be kept locked in peacetime.

Tallinn has mapped 40 to 50 potential sites for similar shelters, with public procurement to follow if the city decides to order more.

According to the manufacturer, the shelter model installed on Juhkentali tänav costs up to €70,000.

World.title: Nearly third of teachers at schools transitioning to Estonian unqualified
World.content:
Nearly a third of teachers at schools transitioning to Estonian lack the required qualifications, as heavy workloads and limited pay make recruitment and retention harder.

When Tallinn's Ehte High School of Humanities switched to Estonian-language instruction in 2024, it hired 17 new teachers. One in three has since left, and the school continues to hire 10–15 more a year to replace both retiring teachers and those who leave due to burnout.

Principal Marika Kranisver said teaching students whose first language is Russian can require more work, as teachers have to adapt materials and bridge students' language gaps. Some end up leaving for schools with more native Estonian-speaking kids.

"I have tremendous respect for the teachers who have taken on this challenge and come to a transitioning school," Kranisver said, acknowledging how much more work it involves than teaching at schools where Estonian is already the main language.

Higher pay has helped attract teachers, but increasing funding constraints are making this harder for schools.

Tartu Jogentaga School principal Alina Braziulene said their school has had to cut the bonus pay for qualified teachers from 20 percent to just 3 percent as state support for Ukrainian students has ended and enrollment is down.

"A third of our students came from Ukraine, and the state used to provide substantial funding to support them," Braziulene explained. "That support is gone now."

Empty classroom in an Estonian school. Photo is illustrative. Source: Ken Mürk/ERR

When schools could no longer offer higher pay, some teachers quit. Meanwhile, the number of teachers required to teach in Estonian has grown, but funding has not, further squeezing budgets for bonus pay.

'The workload is killing them'

At Tallinn's Läänemere High School, principal Deniss Presnetsov said bonus pay is important, but the school can't offer it to everyone, especially as some applicants lack the required qualifications.

He said workloads are also taking a toll on teaching staff, who juggle heavy administrative demands, lesson planning and consultations on top of the teaching itself.

"That kind of constant workload is killing them," Presnetsov stressed, adding that it quickly drives young teachers away. "They end up leaving the school after a couple of years. Some leave after just one."

The Ministry of Education and Research recommends training to help teachers work with students with non-Estonian language backgrounds, adding that with the right methods, teaching Russian-speaking students isn't necessarily harder.

World.title: Estonia's Eneli Jefimova sweeps skins event, snags MVP at college swim meet
World.content:
Estonian swim star Eneli Jefimova swept the breaststroke skins event at California college meet Friday, snagging MVP honors, a personal best and a win for alma mater NC State.

Estonian swim star Eneli Jefimova swept the breaststroke skins event at California college meet Friday, snagging MVP honors, a personal best and a win for alma mater NC State.

Jefimova clocked 2:06.19 in the 200-yard breaststroke at the College Swimming League (CSL) meet in Walnut, California, pulling away in the second half to beat Stanford University's Addie Robillard by 2.12 seconds — and shave 0.14 seconds off her previous personal best from February.

Robillard finished in 2:08.31, with teammate Lucy Thomas third in 2:09.67.

NC State's relay win gave the team the right to choose the stroke for the women's knockout skins competition, in which eight swimmers start and the two slowest are eliminated after each round until two remain.

The team picked breaststroke, and Jefimova won every 50-yard round despite having less than two minutes to complete all four, leaving little time to recover.



Jefimova swam the first three rounds in 26.71, 26.89 and 26.68 seconds before clocking her fastest time of 26.65 in the final. Italy's Anita Bottazzo, swimming for Indiana University, finished 0.42 seconds behind.

About 15 minutes later, the Estonian also took second in the 100-yard breaststroke, finishing 0.49 seconds behind Bottazzo with 58.74.

Another 15 minutes on, she helped NC State reach the final of the 4x50-yard medley relay skins event, where the team narrowly lost to Indiana, 1:36.95 to 1:36.18.

'It was so hard, I teared up'

"That was an insane meet!" acknowledged Jefimova, a two-time Olympian and four-time European champion. "I even teared up during the last 50 yards of the relay because it was so hard."

She was pleased with her new 200-yard personal best, saying it showed her endurance was improving. "I showed good speed in the skins," Jefimova said. "And the 100 breastroke? That was just hard!"

North Carolina State University (NC State) won the meet with 544.83 points, well ahead of Indiana's 469.83. Fellow Estonian swimmer Egle Salu's University of California, Berkeley (UC Berkeley) team placed third with 394.33, followed by Stanford with 311.

The season's main event for both Estonians is the short-course world championships in Beijing on December 1–6. Jefimova won bronze in the 100-meter breaststroke at the previous championships.

Estonian swimmers Egle Salu (UC Berkeley) and Eneli Jefimova (NC State) at the College Swimming League (CSL) meet in Walnut, California. October 2026. Source: Estonian Aquatics

World.title: Gallery: Central Estonia's upgraded Mäo junction reopens to traffic
World.content:
Mäo's upgraded highway junction has reopened with five bus stops, two roundabouts and a 30-space parking lot, improving long-distance bus connections in Central Estonia.

A Lux Express bus made the symbolic first stop at Mäo on Friday, marking the completion of construction and the launch of bus service at the junction.

"By Monday morning, ten Lux Express routes en route to Tallinn and another ten en route to Tartu will be stopping here," said Urmas Kupp, executive director of the Järva County Public Transport Center (JÜTK).

Other bus operators are also interested and could begin stopping there as early as November 2.

One key amenity, however, is still missing. Despite assurances at the opening that the upgraded junction is safer and ready to accommodate long-distance buses, passengers have no proper public bathroom at Mäo, with only a temporary portable toilet installed next to one of the bus shelters.

The Transport Administration says building a passenger terminal is not its responsibility.

A portable toilet next to one of the bus stops at the updated Mäo junction in Central Estonia. October 2026. Source: Olev Kenk/ERR

"Our job is to maintain and develop national roads," said Transport Administration director general Priit Sauk, adding that it's up to public transport centers and local governments to build stops and passenger terminals.

JÜTK plans to sell an unused terminal and use the proceeds to build a new one at Mäo, which would also solve the bathroom problem. Infrastructure Minister Kuldar Leis (Reform) said the project should be a joint effort with the state.

"I think the most logical approach for projects like this is for the state and local governments to work together," Leis said.

Next stretch of Tallinn–Tartu Highway roadwork begins

Friday also marked the start of reconstruction on an eight-kilometer stretch of Tallinn–Tartu Highway between Käsukonna and Imavere. The work, expected to take about two years, includes a multilevel interchange at Imavere that will connect traffic from Viljandi to the highway.

Sauk said another 15 to 16 kilometers between Mäo and Käsukonna also need rebuilding.

"It's included in our road maintenance plan and long-term plans," he noted. "If the next funding period allows, we'd like to get started on it within the next couple of years."

The updated Mäo junction in Central Estonia. October 2026. Source: Karli Saul/Transport Administration

World.title: US dollar hits 168,000 IQD across Baghdad, Erbil, and Basra exchanges
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate of the U.S. dollar against the Iraqi dinar climbed to 168,000 IQD per $100 across major parallel market hubs on Sunday, October 18, 2026, widening the spread against the official statutory peg established by the Central Bank of Iraq.

Parallel wholesale desks across Baghdad, Erbil, and Basra converged at an identical selling rate of 168,000 dinars per $100. In Baghdad, currency exchanges quoted cash buy bids at 167,000 dinars against the 168,000 dinar selling ceiling.

In both Erbil, the capital of the Kurdistan Region, and the southern commercial hub of Basra, trading desks maintained a narrower buy-sell margin, taking in cash dollars at 167,500 dinars against 168,000 dinars for outgoing customer transactions.

The prevailing parallel quotations stand at a noticeable premium above the official benchmark mandated by the Central Bank of Iraq, which anchors the statutory public retail cash price at 1,520 dinars per dollar, or 152,000 dinars per $100.

The divergence of 16,000 dinars per $100 underlines sustained liquidity frictions and elevated merchant demand for physical banknotes outside the official trade-finance window.

World.title: Central Bank of Iraq launches digital portal to exchange damaged currency
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) launched a new digital service on Sunday, October 18, 2026, enabling citizens to submit requests for the replacement of damaged and mutilated banknotes online.

The initiative, rolled out through Iraq’s unified national e-government portal “Ur,” aims to modernize statutory currency services, eliminate administrative red tape, and streamline banking procedures for the public.

According to an official statement received by the Iraqi News Agency (INA), the electronic platform permits applicants to register identification details, log damaged currency specifications, and upload necessary source-of-funds verification before routing submissions directly to the Issuance and Vaults Department at the central bank.

Once preliminary digital verification is concluded, users receive automated notifications and scheduled processing windows to complete in-person banknote swaps at designated CBI cash counters without undergoing manual application delays.

World.title: Iraq’s IT sector gains access to Lenovo servers under Redington distribution deal
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Redington, a technology distributor, has reached a deal with Lenovo Infrastructure Solutions Group (ISG) to sell the company’s enterprise servers in Iraq, increasing access to computing infrastructure for local enterprises and technology providers.

According to the agreement, Redington will distribute Lenovo’s server portfolio via its Iraqi distribution network, with a focus on organizations modernizing their data centers, cloud systems, and digital operations.

The alliance will also assist Iraqi technology resellers and service providers with technical training and business development programs, allowing them to supply enterprise infrastructure solutions to clients across various industries.

Jeetendra Berry, Redington’s President for the GCC and Levant, said that Iraq was a developing market for the firm, especially as enterprises increasingly demand infrastructure capable of managing data-intensive operations and artificial intelligence applications.

Mohammed Hilili, Lenovo’s Gulf General Manager stated that the partnership will increase the availability of the company’s server solutions in Iraq and help organizations looking to grow their IT capabilities.

The agreement expands Redington and Lenovo’s current cooperation into Iraq’s corporate server market, as demand for computing infrastructure rises with the country’s digital transformation ambitions.

World.title: 52nd OIC Council of Foreign Ministers convenes in Baghdad with 55 nations
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The 52nd session of the Council of Foreign Ministers of the Organization of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) officially opened in the Iraqi capital, Baghdad, on Saturday, October 17, 2026. Convening under the banner of advancing regional solidarity, peace, and sustainable development, the two-day summit brings together diplomatic delegations representing 55 member states and observer nations.

The spokesperson for the 52nd ministerial session, Ambassador Hassanein Kamil, announced in a formal statement that proceedings commenced following the arrival of all participating international delegations in Baghdad.

The commencement follows an announcement by the Iraqi Ministry of Foreign Affairs on Friday confirming the completion of all logistical, technical, and security arrangements required to host the high-profile multilateral convention, which runs through October 17–18.

Baghdad’s stewardship of the OIC foreign ministers’ summit reinforces Iraq’s proactive diplomatic posture aimed at bridging regional divides and serving as a neutral convening hub for dialogue.

Ministerial agendas across the two-day meetings are set to address collective security frameworks, cross-border economic integration, humanitarian response mechanisms, and coordinated diplomatic strategies to de-escalate ongoing conflicts across the wider Islamic world.

World.title: AI is coming for every company, Nvidia boss says
World.content:
Stockholm – Artificial intelligence will ultimately become a key aspect of all companies, the head of AI chip giant Nvidia said during a visit to Stockholm, where he urged Europe to ramp up its AI industry.

“Every single company will be an AI company eventually. Every single industry will be impacted by AI,” Jensen Huang told an event late Thursday, part of a European tour that includes a Nvidia-hosted conference in Berlin next week.

“The important thing for us is to recognise that Europe needs to build out the entire stack,” he said, referring to the AI technology chain from data centres to chatbots and other apps.

Speaking later to AFP, Huang said his company had invested $8 billion in Europe over the past year.

“We’ve strategically invested in different parts of that ecosystem, really high quality companies that we believe could help lift it, the whole ecosystem in Europe,” he said, citing the British data centre and AI cloud provider Nscale and the Dutch cloud provider Nebius as examples.

“In the last one year, we’ve invested $8 billion already. We have another couple of billion dollars in the pipeline,” he added. “We’re helping Europe create the AI ecosystem.”

Huang was in Stockholm for the launch of Sferical One, a Swedish supercomputer using Nvidia chips that will keep sensitive Swedish data and expertise in the country.

During his visit, Volvo Cars also announced it was expanding its partnership with Nvidia to improve safety technology in its planned self-driving vehicles.

World.title: Chelsea captain James has knee surgery
World.content:
London – Chelsea captain Reece James has undergone successful knee surgery, the Premier League club announced on Friday.

The England international has missed Chelsea’s past two league games — a 3-0 defeat by Brentford and a 5-1 win over Bournemouth.

“The 26-year-old was absent from Saturday’s 5-1 victory over Bournemouth at Stamford Bridge while medical assessments took place following the injury suffered in training,” the club said in a statement.

“Those assessments confirmed surgery would be the required course of action.

“Reece has already begun his road to recovery and will be supported by the club’s medical department at Cobham during this rehabilitation phase.”

Chelsea are sixth in the Premier League ahead of Saturday’s visit to Everton.

World.title: Asian stocks rise as tech bounces from rout, Warsh upbeat on AI
World.content:
Hong Kong – Most Asian markets bounced Friday after the previous day’s tech rout fuelled by concerns over the AI boom, which Federal Reserve boss Kevin Warsh said offered huge benefits to the global economy.

Seoul and Tokyo enjoyed healthy gains in early exchanges boosted by chipmakers SK hynix and Kioxia, after having been pummelled Thursday as investors bailed out of the once-dominant AI sector.

The selling had been fuelled by forecast-beating US inflation data that ramped up bets on Fed interest rate hikes, as well as concerns about the financial health of data centre operator CoreWeave owing to its huge debt pile.

The New Jersey firm — which has borrowed heavily to finance hefty purchases of pricey semiconductor chips from Nvidia — tanked 15.5 percent Wednesday in the US as yields on some of its bonds soared, reflecting heightened angst over its future.

That added to concerns about the whole AI-tech complex, but Nvidia chief Jensen Huang on Thursday lifted spirits by defending the company and its health.

“CoreWeave’s strength is improving every day,” he told Bloomberg. “I’m optimistic. Their cost of capital is actually decreasing.”

CoreWeave’s shares climbed almost six percent.

Huang’s “defence of CoreWeave’s financial position was enough to pull the NeoCloud complex off the floor, drag AI equities higher and give the broader market something resembling a pulse”, wrote SPI Asset Management’s Stephen Innes.

“One moment the market was pricing the possibility that the AI financing machine had started eating its own tail, the next it was listening to the high priest of the boom explain that the patient was getting stronger.

“AI Jesus had entered the trading room and, for a while at least, the machines found religion again.”

Seoul jumped more than two percent and Tokyo around 1.8 percent, though they slumped 7.6 percent and 4.9 percent respectively Thursday.

Hong Kong, Shanghai, Singapore, Taipei, Mumbai, Bangkok and Manila were also up.

Paris and Frankfurt opened higher but London fell.

Fed chief Warsh said Friday that AI was the “most consequential change” to the global economy in his lifetime, predicting its effects would be positive but the path forward “bumpy”.

At an event at the IMF-World Bank Annual Meetings in Bangkok he said the AI investment boom would drive prices up in the short term, but “there really is, I think, a huge benefit to the global economy, to the US economy over the horizon”.

He also reiterated his previously stated belief that the technology would “make economies and countries that put it to good use more productive”.

But he added: “The path from where we are to there is likely to be a very bumpy one, bumpy in our understanding of the technology, bumpy because we really don’t know what the market structure is going to be of these new technologies.”

Shares in Jakarta tanked more than 11 percent — its heaviest loss since 1998 — after index compiler MSCI said it was “no longer appropriate” to maintain Indonesia’s emerging-market status, fuelling fears of an exodus of foreign investment.

The US firm said earlier this year that investors had raised concerns about “ongoing opacity in shareholding structures” as well as co-ordinated trading behaviour that affected price information.

Authorities said they had carried out changes but MSCI said Friday that investors had indicated the “sufficient progress has not been observed consistently across the Indonesian equity market”, adding “it considers Indonesia’s continued classification as an Emerging Market no longer appropriate”.

World.title: Trump’s new press secretary says China lacked ‘proper’ toilets
World.content:
Washington – White House Press Secretary Katie Zacharia, who was appointed less than a week ago, said China lacked “proper toilets” in an interview that aired on Thursday.

Zacharia, 41, is already under scrutiny over her legal credentials, after giving an inconclusive answer about where she had passed the bar exam, a prerequisite for practicing law in the United States.

The press secretary, who previously lived in China, recalled in an interview that the perception in 2016 was that China would soon overtake the United States.

“We were all being told Hillary (Clinton) was going to win. The golden days or the glory days of America were over. That China was on the horizon,” Zacharia told right-wing influencer Jack Posobiec.

“I remember this very distinctly, having just come from China, thinking, ‘How is China the next country on the horizon? They don’t even have proper toilets,” she added.

There was no immediate comment from Chinese authorities.

Trump has boasted about his “great relationship” with Chinese President Xi Jinping.

During a Washington summit in September, the two leaders discussed topics ranging from AI and trade to the stalled war in Iran, and confirmed that they would meet for a third and fourth time this year.

Zacharia held her first White House press briefing on Tuesday and only answered questions from three journalists.

She succeeded Karoline Leavitt, a loyal Trump supporter and often combative spokesperson, who stepped down in August to care for her young children.

Zacharia has described herself as a lawyer and listed herself as general counsel of a California-based conservative nonprofit. She also said she had worked at a law firm in Beijing.

Asked about her legal background on Thursday, Zacharia said she had registered to take the bar exam but was then “distracted and overwhelmed” by plans to move with her husband to China.

Zacharia said that she did not retake the bar exam upon returning to the United States due to the birth of her first child.

World.title: Trade & connectivity in focus: Rajnath Singh to represent India at SCO meet in Tajikistan
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Defence Minister

will visit Dushanbe, Tajikistan, on October 19 and 20 to represent India at the 25th meeting of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisationâs (SCO) Council of Heads of Government.

According to news agency ANI, citing the Ministry of Defence, the meeting will focus on strengthening multilateral cooperation among SCO member states in trade, economy, investment, connectivity, innovation and cultural-humanitarian exchanges. The participating countries are also expected to review ongoing cooperation initiatives and consider decisions related to the organisationâs financial and institutional functioning.

The agenda is expected to cover trade and investment cooperation, transport and logistics, industrial cooperation, the creative and digital economy, innovation and financial interaction, according to Interfax, which cited the Russian trade mission in Tajikistan. Social and cultural-humanitarian cooperation is also expected to feature in the discussions.

India has highlighted the need to expand intra-SCO trade, lower trade costs, strengthen supply chains and improve connectivity.





At a meeting of SCO ministers responsible for foreign economic and trade activities in Dushanbe in September, India called for simplified customs procedures, paperless trade, electronic document exchange and stronger multimodal connectivity, according to the Ministry of Commerce and Industry.

India also highlighted opportunities for cooperation in agriculture, critical minerals, pharmaceuticals, manufacturing, electronics, energy security, renewable energy and green hydrogen.

It called for greater use of digital and cross-border payments and improved access to trade finance for micro, small and medium enterprises and start-ups.

The October meeting will provide India an opportunity to exchange views with other SCO member states on advancing practical and mutually beneficial cooperation. India remains actively engaged in SCO mechanisms and contributes to regional cooperation through initiatives in start-ups and innovation, digital public infrastructure and people-to-people exchanges, the Ministry of Defence said.

World.title: AI cuts job demand in exposed occupations by nearly 10% across Asia: IMF report
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping labour demand across Asia, with employer demand falling by nearly 10% in occupations more exposed to the technology since the launch of ChatGPT in November 2022, according to the International Monetary Fundâs (IMF) October 2026 Regional Economic Outlook: Asia and Pacific.

The report, based on approximately 40 million online job postings across 19 Asian economies, highlights the challenges facing countries such as India, Indonesia and the Philippines as they seek to create productive jobs for growing working-age populations while AI transforms the sectors expected to absorb new workers.

However, the decline in demand for workers in AI-exposed occupations appears to have stabilised, suggesting that the technologyâs impact on employment is not limited to job displacement.

AI creates demand for new skills

The IMF report points to the emergence of new employment opportunities requiring specialised AI skills, including prompt engineering, retrieval-augmented generation and AI agent development.

Employers are increasingly seeking workers who can integrate AI into business processes, improve productivity and translate technological capabilities into practical applications.





Firm-level adoption of AI, however, remains uneven. Around 6% of firms in Asia explicitly seek AI skills in their job postings, the report said.

Businesses adopting AI are experiencing stronger labour demand growth than those that have not adopted the technology, including in occupations highly exposed to automation. This suggests that AI can complement human capabilities even as it reduces demand for certain tasks.

India faces jobs and skills challenge

The implications of AI differ across Asian economies. Emerging economies such as India may initially be less exposed to the technology because a large share of their workforce remains employed in agriculture and other sectors less affected by AI.

However, this could pose a longer-term challenge if AI makes it harder for workers to transition into higher-productivity manufacturing and services, the report said.

For countries with expanding working-age populations, the challenge is to generate enough productive employment while ensuring that workers have the skills required by an increasingly technology-driven economy.

Education, reskilling key to managing AI disruption

The report emphasises that the response to AI must go beyond encouraging technological adoption. Education reform, reskilling programmes, digital infrastructure and stronger labour-market institutions will be essential to prepare workers for changing occupational demands.

Businesses will also need to invest in workforce development alongside AI adoption to help employees adapt to new roles and changing skill requirements.

The report suggests that AI need not become a barrier to inclusive growth. With timely investments in skills and preparedness, Asian economies could use the technology to boost productivity, encourage innovation and support sustainable employment.

World.title: FSSAI may curb sugar in baby food, set pesticide caps for tea
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has proposed two changes to food safety rules: prohibiting the addition of sucrose and fructose to products meant for babies up to six months and setting maximum residue limits for two pesticides in tea.

The draft amendments were published in the Gazette of India on Oct 16. Currently, lactose and glucose polymers are the preferred carbohydrate sources in infant foods. Sucrose and fructose can be added when needed, but their combined amount cannot exceed 20% of total carbohydrates. The proposed amendment seeks to prohibit their addition in products for babies up to six months.

The proposal aims to limit early exposure to added sugars amid concerns over childhood obesity and related health risks.

It also complements recommendations for exclusive breastfeeding during the first six months. A doctor said the restriction must be enforced at the licensing stage. âFSSAI should also consider extending the ban to products intended for children above six months, given concerns over obesity.

World.title: Crowd, rain or misleading announcement: What led to Kolkata stampede tragedy?
World.content:
NEW DELHI: A sudden surge of people, heavy rain and alleged confusion over announcements and entry-exit routes are among the factors being investigated after a stampede at the Chorbagan Sarbojanin Durga Puja pandal in Kolkata killed at least 19 people and injured 25 others on Saturday evening.

The incident occurred around 7.15pm on Maha Saptami, when a large crowd waiting on the narrow Radha Madhab Saha Lane to enter the pandal reportedly surged forward as a downpour began. Those already inside were caught in the rush, with people unable to move towards the exit as visitors ahead blocked their way. Several people reportedly fell down a flight of stairs near the exit and were trampled by those behind them.

What we know about Kolkata stampede

A misleading announcement by the puja committee is also suspected to have added to the confusion, while the blowing of whistles by private security guards may have triggered a rush among visitors, according to CM Adhikari.

Crowd management and security under scrutiny

Kolkata Police are investigating whether lapses in crowd management, confusion over entry and exit routes, and heavy rain contributed to the tragedy, a senior officer told PTI. Eyewitnesses alleged that announcements about entry, exit and crowd movement were improper, leaving visitors confused during peak hours.

Locals also questioned the police deployment at the venue, claiming that personnel were largely stationed near the VIP entrance.





"I have not seen adequate police presence this year. This resulted in the mismanagement," Chorbagan resident Sanghamitra Bhowmik told PTI.

Another concern raised by locals was the alleged lack of administrative assistance in taking the injured to hospitals.

"There must be some lapses, but these should be probed. Whether lapses were on the part of the organisers or they had flouted the rules to erect the pandal will be checked," the police officer told PTI.

A forensic team visited the site late on Saturday to collect evidence. Police are questioning the organisers and examining CCTV footage, while also seeking details of the security guards and other personnel deployed to manage the crowd. Officers who were posted at the venue will also be questioned as part of the investigation.

State orders safety review of pandals

Adhikari, who visited the injured at Kolkata Medical College and Hospital, said the incident had raised concerns about safety arrangements at crowded Durga Puja venues.

According to hospital sources, 11 injured people were shifted to SSKM Hospital. The deceased included 13 women and a child, a source at the medical college said.

The chief minister announced a high-level committee to inspect prominent pandals across West Bengal and review crowd management, exit routes, lighting and structural safety. The panel will be led by Disaster Management Principal Secretary Rajesh Sinha, Fire Services Director General Anuj Sharma and Additional Director General of Police (Law and Order) Javed Shamim.

He also called for wider exits, better lighting and the removal of bottlenecks created by temporary rope enclosures. The state government has announced Rs 25 lakh in compensation and a Group D government job for the family of each deceased victim. A toll-free helpline, 18003455678, has also been set up to help people seeking information about those affected.

World.content:
Telugu Desam Party (TDP) MLC from the North Andhra Graduates’ constituency Vepada Chiranjeevi Rao on Sunday (October 18, 2026) said brisk economic activity, industrial progress and effective implementation of welfare schemes would make people of all sections vote for the TDP and its allies, the Jana Sena Party (JSP) and the BJP.

He said North Andhra had been witnessing unprecedented development. He cited the Alluri Sitarama Raju International Airport and the proposed Reliance data centre at Bhogapuram in Vizianagaram district, the Google AI data centre near Visakhapatnam, the ArcelorMittal steel plant in Anakapalli district and others.

Mr. Chiranjeevi Rao, who came to Vizianagaram to campaign for the local body elections, told the media that people were eager to vote for the TDP in the ensuing urban, parishad and panchayat elections.

“With the concerted efforts of Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu and Minister for Education, the State attracted around 1,037 projects with ₹29.3 lakh crore investments. It will create nearly 20 lakh jobs for unemployed youth in the State,” Mr. Chiranjeevi Rao said.

He said the State government had been conducting recruitment drives in a systematic way, strictly following the job calendar. He said over 35,000 jobs would be given in various government organisations.

“Recruitment drives for assistant professors, lecturers, teachers, Group-1 officers and others had been taken up and notifications were also issued for some of them. It had instilled confidence among unemployed youngsters and they would opt NDA parties in local body elections,” he said.

Mr. Chiranjeevi Rao won the North Andhra Graduates’ seat in 2023, when the YSRCP was in power. An academician, he hoped that intellectuals, teachers, lecturers and business persons would vote for the TDP in the municipal and parishad elections because they were satisfied with the efficient administration, sustained development and implementation of new welfare schemes.
